jobs.description:
Overview of position

CTG is looking for an ICT Systems Integration Technician EFMS/CARLOG to support its client operation, administration, integration, maintenance, and modernization of the UN mission Electronic Fleet Management System (EFMS) utilizing the CARLOG platform. The incumbent will be responsible for the administration and operational support of fleet technology systems, fuel monitoring systems, SQL databases, GPS tracking infrastructure, CAN Bus integrations, and related transport technology solutions.

The objective of the assignment is to ensure the reliable, secure, and efficient operation of the CARLOG Electronic Fleet Management System and its interoperability with Umoja ERP, Transport Management systems, Fuel Management Enhancement Solutions, and other approved services.

The incumbent will maintain fleet technology infrastructure, vehicle monitoring systems, receiving stations, communication networks, databases, and operational reporting systems while supporting fleet oversight, operational compliance, fuel management, investigations, data analytics, and platform modernization initiatives.

Role objectives

Within delegated authority, the incumbent will be responsible for the following duties:

A. EFMS / CARLOG Administration and Operations

Administer, configure, maintain, and support the CARLOG Electronic Fleet Management System (EFMS).

Maintain CARLOG databases, SQL Server environments, and associated applications.

Manage fleet master data including vehicles, drivers, devices, users, and organizational structures.

Create, modify, suspend, and maintain user accounts, permissions, and access privileges.

Maintain the World Fleet Log platform, including reporting and access administration.

Manage CARLOG F1 3G and F2 LTE/Wi-Fi devices and ensure their continuous operation.

Monitor system performance, synchronization services, scheduled jobs, and data transmission activities.

Establish and maintain backup, recovery, and business continuity procedures.

Maintain system documentation, architecture diagrams, asset inventories, and technical records.

Coordinate with the client sections, E-Drive Technology (EDT), vendors, and internal stakeholders on technical support activities.

Ensure completeness, integrity, and accuracy of fleet monitoring data.

B. Systems Integration and Platform Modernization

Maintain reliable and secure integration between CARLOG, Umoja ERP, Transport systems, Fuel Management Enhancement solutions, and other approved platforms.

Monitor and support automated data exchange and synchronization processes.

Validate interface configurations and ensure proper data flow between integrated systems.

Support modernization initiatives and migration from legacy CARLOG environments to web-based platforms.

Assist with requirements analysis, configuration, testing, data migration, deployment, stabilization, and user adoption activities.

Maintain integration documentation and interface inventories.

C. Receiving Station Administration

Establish, administer, maintain, and support all CARLOG Receiving Stations throughout the mission area.

Monitor receiving station availability, communications, data downloads, and synchronization performance.

Ensure continuous connectivity between receiving stations and CARLOG servers.

Troubleshoot hardware, software, communications, network, and synchronization failures.

Perform system restoration and recovery activities following communication outages.

Maintain operational records and performance statistics for all receiving stations.

D. Fleet Monitoring and Operational Compliance

Monitor and track mission vehicles using CARLOG systems.

Monitor real-time vehicle movements, deployment activities, and utilization patterns.

Analyze vehicle operational performance and fleet usage trends.

Monitor speeding violations, unsafe driving practices, and road safety compliance.

Monitor unauthorized vehicle movements, curfew violations, and misuse of assets.

Investigate vehicle activity anomalies and driver behavior irregularities.

Monitor excessive idling and operational inefficiencies.

Generate alerts, notifications, and operational compliance reports.

Maintain fleet performance indicators and statistical data.

E. Fuel Management and Monitoring

Monitor fuel consumption, fuel efficiency, and fuel-system performance.

Analyze fuel monitoring data generated through CARLOG and Fuel Management Enhancement systems.

Investigate fuel anomalies, unauthorized fuel usage, fuel loss, and suspected theft incidents.

Validate fuel performance indicators and consumption trends.

Support fuel-related investigations and corrective actions.

Produce fuel consumption, efficiency, and utilization reports.

F. Vehicle Systems Integration and Diagnostics

Review vehicle technical manuals, wiring diagrams, and electronic documentation.

Analyze vehicle communication networks including CAN Bus, J1939, OBD-II, LIN, and ECU interfaces.

Support installation, configuration, calibration, and validation of CARLOG devices and vehicle integrations.

Configure data acquisition from vehicle electronic control units.

Support mechanics, electricians, workshop staff, and installation teams during deployments.

Diagnose communication, electrical, and integration faults.

Verify compliance with CARLOG installation standards.

Perform testing and operational acceptance of installations and upgrades.

G. SIM Card and Communication Management

Administer and monitor active SIM cards supporting CARLOG live communications.

Maintain communication performance and monitor transmission quality.

Coordinate activation, replacement, provisioning, and troubleshooting activities with the section and service providers.

Maintain SIM card inventories, assignment records, subscriptions, and data plans.

Resolve communication outages and connectivity disruptions.

Ensure uninterrupted transmission of vehicle data to fleet monitoring platforms.

H. Monitoring, Incident Resolution and Service Support

Monitor application availability, server performance, interfaces, synchronization services, logs, and exception queues.

Investigate incidents and restore services within agreed service levels.

Provide Level 1 and Level 2 technical support to users.

Maintain complete incident records, root-cause analyses, and resolution documentation.

Escalate unresolved issues appropriately and coordinate corrective actions.

Support system upgrades, patching, and maintenance activities.

I. Data Quality and Reconciliation

Validate vehicle, driver, fuel, trip, maintenance, mileage, and operational data.

Perform data reconciliation between CARLOG, Umoja ERP, and other integrated systems.

Investigate inconsistencies and data anomalies.

Coordinate corrective actions with stakeholders and business owners.

Maintain data quality standards and reporting accuracy.

J. Reporting, Business Intelligence and Analytics

Generate and distribute:

Daily fleet monitoring reports.

Weekly and monthly operational reports.

Vehicle movement and utilization reports.

Management dashboards and KPI reports.

Driver behavior and road safety reports.

Curfew violation and compliance reports.

Fuel consumption and efficiency reports.

Fuel anomaly and investigation reports.

Receiving station performance reports.

Fleet deployment and operational readiness reports.

Annual mileage audit reports.

Historical vehicle activity reports.

Statistical reports for the CTO and Transport Management.

Data-driven recommendations to improve fleet efficiency, safety, compliance, and resource utilization.

K. Investigation and Compliance Support

Support Safety and Investigations Unit (SIU) inquiries and transport-related investigations.

Analyze vehicle movement histories and reconstruct routes.

Produce evidence-based reports using CARLOG data.

Support accident investigations and vehicle misuse assessments.

Monitor compliance with transport regulations, policies, and operational procedures.

Provide analytical support for management decision-making.

L. Workshop and Maintenance Support

Support vehicle maintenance management activities.

Maintain vehicle maintenance records within CARLOG.

Monitor maintenance schedules and vehicle service status.

Ensure maintenance activities are accurately recorded.

Support vehicle diagnostics and troubleshooting activities.

Assist in identifying technical faults and reducing unnecessary parts replacement through accurate analysis.

M. Security, Change and Release Management

Apply role-based access control and user security management.

Implement approved system changes, upgrades, configurations, and releases.

Maintain audit trails, access records, and security documentation.

Support testing, validation, rollback procedures, and change-control processes.

Ensure compliance with applicable UN ICT security standards and policies.

N. Training, Knowledge Management and Stakeholder Coordination

Deliver technical and user training on CARLOG, EFMS, fleet monitoring systems, and related technologies.

Develop technical procedures, user guides, and training materials.

Conduct knowledge-transfer sessions and support user adoption initiatives.

Provide vehicle tracking support to the Security Operations Centre (SOC).

Liaise with Transport, ICT, IT section, Finance, Supply Chain, Fuel Management personnel, vendors, and service providers.

Maintain knowledge repositories, operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and technical documentation.

Perform other related duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Monthly Deliverables

Monthly service-performance report covering system availability, incidents, service requests, recurring problems, changes implemented, outstanding risks, and corrective actions.

Fleet monitoring report covering vehicle utilization, operational compliance, driver behavior, curfew violations, and fleet performance indicators.

Fuel monitoring and reconciliation report covering fuel consumption trends, anomalies, investigations, and corrective actions.

Integration and data-quality report covering CARLOG, Umoja ERP, Transport systems, Fuel Management Enhancement solutions, and related interfaces.

CARLOG modernization status report covering migration progress, testing, deployment readiness, user adoption, and stabilization activities.

Receiving station performance report covering availability, connectivity, synchronization status, and maintenance activities.

Updated technical documentation, system inventories, operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and knowledge articles.

Training and knowledge-transfer report identifying sessions delivered, participants, materials used, and follow-up actions.

Forward work plan outlining priorities, milestones, dependencies, risks, and resource requirements for the following month.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Education

High school diploma or equivalent is required.

Technical training in Information Technology, Electronics, Telematics, Automotive Technology, Fleet Management Systems, Vehicle Diagnostics, Computer Science, Transport Technology, or related disciplines is required.

A university degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics, Automotive Engineering, Transport Management, or a related field is desirable.

Work Experience

A minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in fleet management, fleet monitoring, telematics systems, transport operations, fuel management systems, vehicle tracking technologies, or comparable operational systems in a multi-site environment.

Demonstrated experience in the administration and support of Electronic Fleet Management Systems (EFMS), GPS tracking platforms, telematics solutions, and fleet-monitoring applications.

Practical experience in systems integration, data validation, database administration, incident management, testing, deployment support, and technical documentation.

Experience administering and maintaining SQL databases, fleet management applications, and reporting systems.

Proven experience with CAN Bus integration, vehicle communication protocols (OBD-II, J1939, LIN), vehicle diagnostics, and automotive electrical systems.

Experience maintaining vehicle communication networks, monitoring devices, fuel monitoring systems, and related fleet technology infrastructure.

Experience supporting large and geographically dispersed vehicle fleets of 500 vehicles or more is highly desirable.

Experience supporting web-based application deployments, platform upgrades, or migrations from legacy client/server environments is highly desirable.

Knowledge of CARLOG, World Fleet Log, Umoja ERP, UN transport operations, fuel management systems, or comparable fleet-management platforms is highly desirable.

Experience within the United Nations, military, government, humanitarian, peacekeeping, or other international organizations is an advantage.

Demonstrated ability to analyze operational data, produce management reports, and support evidence-based decision-making through fleet analytics and performance monitoring.

Technical Skills

CARLOG Fleet Monitoring System Administration

Electronic Fleet Management Systems (EFMS)

World Fleet Log Platform Administration

Fleet Telematics and Vehicle Tracking Technologies

GPS Monitoring and Geolocation Systems

Microsoft SQL Server Administration and Database Management

Database Design, Querying, Data Validation, and Reporting

Systems Integration and Data Synchronization

Umoja ERP Interface Support and Data Reconciliation

CAN Bus, J1939, OBD-II, LIN, and ECU Communications

Vehicle Diagnostics and Automotive Electronic Systems

CARLOG F1 3G and F2 LTE/Wi-Fi Device Administration

Fuel Monitoring Systems and Fuel Analytics

SIM Card, GSM, LTE, and Mobile Data Connectivity Management

Receiving Station Administration and Communications Management

Server Administration, Performance Monitoring, and Troubleshooting

Incident Management and Technical Support

Business Intelligence, Data Analytics, and Dashboard Development

Microsoft Excel (Advanced)

Microsoft Power BI

Technical Documentation and Knowledge Management

Technical Reporting, Fleet Analytics, and Performance Measurement

Change Management, Testing, Deployment, and Release Support

Information Security, Access Control, and Audit Compliance

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are strongly advised to apply.

jobs.title: NTD Project Officer - Reaching the Last Mile Fund
jobs.description:
Sightsavers is looking for an experienced Project Officer with excellent partner management skills and experience of Digital Health, to support the continued success of Neglected Tropical Disease projects in Benin.

**NTD Project Officer**
Salary: Local terms and conditions apply
Location: Benin, Cotonou
Contract: 12-month Fixed-term Contract
Hours: 35 hours per week - Standard office hours

We are looking for an experienced Project Officer with excellent partner management skills and experience of Digital Health, to support the continued success of Neglected Tropical Disease projects in Benin, in collaboration with The Reaching the Last Mile Funds (RLMF) and several other donors.

In Benin, Sightsavers has successfully supported the elimination of trachoma in 2022. However, Benin like many other Sub-Saharan African countries is endemic to several NTD and in line with the WHO roadmap, the country ambition to eliminate most NTDs by 2030. Sightsavers is supporting Benin for the elimination of onchocerciasis, lymphatic filariasis with the ambition of growing the portfolio to include schistosomiasis and soil transmitted helminth.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced, talented and enthusiastic programme officer to play a crucial part in impactful change. You will utilise your capacity building and partner relationship skills to assist in the digitalisation of projects, and to build strong relationships with partners, other INGOs and Government organisations.

Key duties will include:

This is a varied role, please read the full [job description](https://sightsavershh.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/HRExternal/IQAGgx2aWWBLQb2DWR4ujBFsATR1lJfw9rF4ltwXWpVOatU?e=GDgTlR) for further details.

jobs.title: Humanitarian NGO Platform - Deputy Director (Ukraine Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
**Save the Children International**

Save the Children International is a leading global humanitarian organization that has been protecting children's rights worldwide for over 100 years. We operate in more than 100 countries, responding to emergencies, implementing innovative development programs, and advocating for children's rights on a global scale.

Our work in Ukraine began in 2014. Since then, we have significantly expanded our presence, providing support to children and families affected by war. Our key areas of focus include education, child protection, food security, social support, and advocacy to drive lasting change in children's lives.

**ROLE PURPOSE:**

The Humanitarian NGO Platform in Ukraine was established in February 2023 and brings together local, national and international NGOs engaged in the humanitarian response. The Secretariat currently consist of the Director, a Deputy Director, a Policy and Advocacy Advisor, and a Comms and Admin Officer, and is supported by the Steering Committee comprising of five NGOs including the NGO Platform host, Save the Children. The NGO Platform currently has over 120 members.

The Platform serves its members by strengthening collective coordination, advocacy, information-sharing and representation to support an effective, principled and locally informed humanitarian response.

The Deputy Director leads the NGO Platform’s subnational coordination and engagement. Based in Kyiv or Dnipro or Kharkiv, the role creates spaces for information sharing and coordination across NGO Area Managers, ensures that operational realities and priorities from frontline regions inform national coordination and advocacy efforts, and supports engagement with local authorities, local NGOs, and UN.

The Deputy Director also provides strategic support to the Director, contributing to governance processes, engagement with the Steering Committee and members, and representing the Platform when delegated.

The post requires strong diplomacy, analytical capacity and relationship-building skills to navigate complex humanitarian dynamics and support a coordinated, principled and locally informed response.

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:**

**Subnational Coordination Leadership**

Lead the NGO Platform’s engagement with NGO actors operating in eastern Ukraine. Facilitate coordination and dialogue among regional representatives / Area Managers of member NGOs. Convene and support Area Manager Working Groups to enable operational problem-solving, information exchange, and collective positioning where relevant. Monitor coordination needs across frontline and high-impact areas to identify gaps, duplication and opportunities for improved collaboration. Promote principled and effective humanitarian coordination that supports quality response and accountability to affected populations. Facilitate opportunities for peer learning, lessons learned and exchange of best practices among NGOs (and among NNGOs and INGOs) operating in similar contexts.

**Engagement with Subnational Humanitarian Coordination Architecture**

Support NGO engagement with humanitarian coordination mechanisms at regional level. Maintain regular engagement with Humanitarian Operations Coordination Groups (HOCGs) and other relevant coordination structures. Ensure transparent information flows between these structures and NGO Platform members. Ensure operational realities from frontline regions inform national-level discussions and advocacy. Monitor the evolution of area-based coordination approaches and identify opportunities to strengthen NGO engagement and leadership.

**Government and Access Engagement (Subnational)**

Support constructive collective engagement between NGOs and relevant authorities at regional level. Maintain dialogue with local and regional authorities on humanitarian NGO priorities and coordination challenges where appropriate. Support members in navigating operational challenges related to humanitarian access, regulations and coordination with authorities. Represent the NGO Platform in relevant subnational coordination forums where delegated.

**Strategic Support to the Director**

Act as a strategic deputy to the Director and support the overall functioning of the NGO Platform. Support the Director in implementation and follow-up of the NGO Platform strategy and engage with the NGO Platform Working Groups. Represent the NGO Platform in external engagements when delegated. Maintain situational awareness of humanitarian, political and operational developments in Ukraine. Support development of updates, briefings and analytical inputs to inform NGO Platform engagement with members and partners.

**Support to localization**

Promote meaningful participation of national and local NGOs in Area Manager Working Groups and other relevant coordination discussions. Facilitate exchange of practices and lessons learned that contribute to a more locally informed and locally led humanitarian response. Promote discussions on complementarity across INGOs and NNGOs to inform NGO Platform discussions and positioning where relevant.

**Finance and Compliance**

- Ensure compliance with donor and host agency (Save the Children) requirements.
- Contribute to monitoring of activities and budget implementation where relevant.

**Additional job responsibilities**

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience. In the event of a major humanitarian emergency, the role holder will be expected to work outside the normal role profile and be able to vary working hours accordingly.

**BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice)**

Accountability

- Takes personal responsibility for decisions, effective use of resources, high-quality results, and acting in alignment with Save the Children values.
- Supports colleagues and partners to take ownership of their responsibilities by providing guidance, opportunities for development, and constructive feedback.
- Addresses underperformance proactively and fairly, ensuring accountability for outcomes.

Ambition

- Sets clear, ambitious goals for themselves and contributes to a culture of continuous improvement and professional growth.
- Actively promotes and communicates the vision of Save the Children to inspire, motivate and engage others.
- Thinks creatively and strategically to drive progress and long-term impact for children.

Collaboration

- Builds positive, trusting, and inclusive relationships with staff, partners, and stakeholders.
- Values diversity and different perspectives as strengths that enhance the organization’s collective impact.
- Demonstrates strong communication skills, showing empathy, openness, and willingness to support others.

Creativity

- Proactively seeks and encourages innovative, practical solutions to improve effectiveness and staff experience.
- Confident in proposing new ideas and taking responsible, well-considered risks to enhance results.

Integrity

- Acts with honesty, fairness and professionalism in all interactions.
- Promotes an environment of transparency, trust, and mutual respect, upholding the highest ethical standards.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:**

**Essential**

- Advanced university degree in international relations, political science, humanitarian studies, social sciences or related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- At least 7 years of experience in humanitarian response or coordination roles, including field-level engagement in complex emergencies.
- Strong understanding of humanitarian coordination architecture and operational dynamics in conflict contexts.
- Demonstrated experience facilitating coordination between multiple humanitarian actors.
- Proven ability to build relationships and navigate complex stakeholder environments.
- Fluency in English and Ukrainian (knowledge of Russian an asset).
- Ability to work independently in fast-paced and evolving contexts.
- Commitment to humanitarian principles and ethical practice.
- Experience engaging with local authorities and civil society actors in conflict settings.

**Desirable**

- Experience working with NGO coordination platforms or civil society alliances.
- Familiarity with the humanitarian and civil society landscape in Ukraine.
- Proven experience engaging in or supporting localization/partnership work, advocacy, and/or coordination processes at national and/or international level.
- Strong understanding of localization, partnership models, humanitarian financing, and power dynamics within the humanitarian system.

**Additional job responsibilities**

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience.

**Equal Opportunities**

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.

Save the Children is committed to create a truly inclusive, effective and representative organisational culture, encouraging equity and diversity among its employees and eliminating discrimination. Having a diverse profile of employees, different age groups, backgrounds, cultures, gender identities and expressions, sexual orientation etc., including a range of different experiences and capabilities helps us understand, represent and serve children better. Therefore, all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, or age.

**Child Safeguarding Policy:**

We are committed to ensuring children's safety. Our recruitment process includes strict background checks and reflects our commitment to protecting children from harm.

**Safeguarding our Staff:**

The post holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI Safeguarding, Code of Conduct and other policies.

**Health and Safety:**

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

**Application Information:**

If you are interested in this position, please submit your CV and cover letter in English and include details of your salary expectation and English proficiency.

We need to keep children and their families safe, so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the safeguarding of children from abuse.

**Disclaimer:**

Please be cautious of individuals who may misuse the Save the Children name to solicit fees from job seekers. We do not engage third parties or agencies to recruit candidates. If someone contacts you promising recruitment or placement at Save the Children for a fee, please do not proceed.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**Save the Children does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process.**

jobs.title: COORDINATOR - UNITED NATIONS UNIVERSITY (UNU) HUB [FIXED-TERM PROJECT POSITION]
jobs.company: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development
jobs.description:
## Position overview

ICIMOD is seeking a Hub Coordinator for its newly established United Nations University (UNU) Hub at ICIMOD.

The UNU Hub at ICIMOD is a newly established collaborative platform that advances research, education, and partnerships to strengthen the resilience of mountain communities in the HKH region facing climate and socio-economic change. Building on the long-standing collaboration between ICIMOD; United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS); Eurac Research, Italy; and the Himalayan University Consortium (HUC), the Hub supports the sustainable management of mountain social–ecological systems, particularly in the HKH. It aims to generate knowledge, foster innovation, and develop a new generation of mountain researchers, practitioners, and leaders. Through research, capacity building, outreach, and advocacy, the Hub promotes evidence-based solutions and regional cooperation for sustainable and climate-resilient mountain development. The focus topics of the first years will be designed as:

- mountain climate risk and adaptation,
- sustainable management of natural resources in mountains, and
- mountain habitability, local knowledge systems and intangible heritage.

The Hub Coordinator will be responsible for the strategic, programmatic, research, and financial coordination of the UNU Hub at ICIMOD. The role includes developing and implementing the Hub’s strategy, leading fundraising efforts and project proposal development, and ensuring sustainable funding. The coordinator will supervise the Hub team; coordinate the Hub steering board, advisory board, and management board meetings; manage technical and financial reporting to partner institutions; and serve as the primary liaison among ICIMOD, UNU-EHS, Eurac Research, and HUC to ensure effective collaboration and the delivery of the Hub’s objectives.

## Person specification/competencies

\[Experience, knowledge, and skills\]

### **ESSENTIAL**

- A Master's degree, preferably a PhD, in a relevant field.
- At least 5 years of project/programme/hub management experience.
- At least 3 years of experience in leading and coordinating large and complex research programmes, including managing partnerships, leading multisectoral coordination, project development, donor liaison, managing interdisciplinary teams, monitoring and reporting, and complex budget management.
- Excellent interpersonal, teamworking and communication skills, both written and spoken, comfortable working with and to all levels, internal and external.
- Excellent communication and report writing skills (in English) and analytical skills with an ability to understand and contextualise research.
- Respect for ICIMOD’s and UN core values

### **PREFERRED**

- Prior work experience with the UN or any international organisation.
- Familiarity with HKH, its social, economic, and ecological context
- Ability to travel within and outside the HKH region.

## Duration

Three-year fixed-term project contract, with a six-month probation period. There is a possibility of an extension, subject to performance, need for the position, and the Hub’s future funding levels.

## Remuneration

This is a Specialist/Senior Officer position at ICIMOD with a competitive salary and benefits. Salary comprises basic salary, provident fund, and family/post adjustment allowance. We offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes insurances (medical, life and accidental), children allowance and children’s education grant for a maximum of 2 children below 18 years of age, severance pay, paid leave (30 holidays and 10 public holidays per year) and day care facility.

For expatriates, there is a tax exemption in Nepal; they are responsible for paying their home country’s taxes. Expatriate staff are entitled to housing allowance, annual home leave ticket, shipment of personal effects, and an installation and repatriation allowance.

## ICIMOD’s core values

Our core values are integrity, neutrality, relevance, inclusiveness, openness, and ambition. These values express our culture and are central to the guiding beliefs and principles of our work and behaviour. Our core values will lie at the heart of ICIMOD operations and delivery. They will underpin everything we do and frame how we work with our partners. They reflect our founding intentions and the balances we seek to hold, while equipping ourselves for the future.

## UN Core Values and Behaviours

**Values:**

- **Inclusion** - Take action to create an environment of dignity and respect for all, regardless of age, culture, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, geography, grade, language, nationality, racial identity, religion, sex, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, social origin or any other aspect of identity.
- **Integrity** - Act ethically, demonstrating the standards of conduct of the United Nations and taking prompt action in case of witnessing unprofessional or unethical behaviour, or any other breach of UN standards.
- **Humility** - Demonstrate self-awareness and willingness to learn from others.
- **Humanity** - Act according to the purposes of the United Nations: peace, dignity and equality on a healthy planet.

**Behaviours:**

- **Connect and Collaborate** - Build positive relationships with others to advance the work of the United Nations and work coherently as One UN
- **Analyse and Plan** - Seek out and use data from a wide range of sources to understand problems, inform decision-making, propose evidence-based solutions and plan action
- **Deliver Results with Positive Impact** - Hold oneself and others accountable for delivering results and making a positive difference to the people and causes that the United Nations serves
- **Learn and Develop** - Pursue own learning and development and contribute to the learning and development of others
- **Adapt and Innovate** - Demonstrate flexibility, agility and the ability to think and act in novel ways

jobs.title: A CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT SCREENING, ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION FOR INCLUSIVE WELLBEING FOR CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL EDUCATION NEEDS AND DISABILITIES .
jobs.company: Adventist Development and Relief Agency International
jobs.description:
**REQUEST FOR CONSULTANTS**

The Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA) is a global humanitarian organization with a mission to work with people in poverty and distress to create just and positive change. ADRA Somalia belongs to the worldwide network, comprised of more than 130 supporting and implementing country offices. ADRA Somalia is seeking to recruit a consultant to undertake the following assignment: **SCREENING, ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION FOR INCLUSIVE WELLBEING FOR CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL EDUCATION NEEDS AND DISABILITIES**

1. **Background Information**

In many contexts, even where there is strong commitment to promoting the rights, inclusion and wellbeing of children with disabilities, adequate systems for identification, assessment, referral and individualized support remain limited. Children with disabilities have diverse needs that may relate to physical, sensory, intellectual, developmental, communication, behavioral or psychosocial functioning. Without appropriate mechanisms to identify these needs and connect children and their families to suitable services, many conditions may remain unrecognized or inadequately addressed. Early identification, comprehensive assessment and targeted follow-up are therefore essential to ensuring that children with disabilities receive appropriate support and can participate meaningfully in family and community life.

Disability and poverty are deeply interconnected, with persons with disabilities often experiencing disproportionate levels of social and economic exclusion and reduced access to essential services, livelihood opportunities and civic participation. Children from economically vulnerable, displaced or otherwise marginalized households may face additional barriers to accessing assessment, rehabilitation, assistive devices and specialized support. In some cases, relatively straightforward interventions can significantly improve functioning and independence. For example, unidentified visual impairment may restrict a child's ability to undertake everyday activities but may be substantially addressed through appropriate assessment and corrective devices. Similarly, hearing, mobility, communication, cognitive, developmental and psychosocial difficulties may remain undetected or unsupported where appropriate screening and referral mechanisms are unavailable.

Children with less visible disabilities, including intellectual, developmental, communication, behavioral and psychosocial difficulties, are particularly vulnerable to remaining unidentified. Their challenges may be misunderstood or attributed to behaviour, personality or other factors, resulting in stigma, isolation or inadequate support. Families and caregivers may also lack information about available services or may face financial, geographic and social barriers to accessing specialized assistance. Without timely identification and intervention, these challenges can become more pronounced and adversely affect children's development, independence, wellbeing, social participation and future opportunities.

There is therefore a clear need to strengthen disability inclusion beyond any single sector or service. A holistic and systematic approach is required that considers the child within the broader family and community environment and recognizes the interconnected nature of health, protection, psychosocial wellbeing, rehabilitation, social inclusion and economic vulnerability. Such an approach should strengthen the capacity of relevant institutions, service providers, communities and families to identify children with disabilities, understand their individual needs and facilitate access to appropriate interventions and services.

While broader improvements in accessibility and inclusion can benefit many children, some barriers experienced by children with disabilities require specialized and individualized responses. These may include functional assessments, assistive devices, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and communication support, psychosocial services, medical referrals, caregiver support and adaptations to the physical and social environment. Effective support therefore requires mechanisms that can identify individual needs and translate assessment findings into practical interventions.

Strengthening these systems requires clear and accessible pathways for screening, assessment, referral, intervention and follow-up. It also requires appropriate coordination among relevant government institutions, service providers, community structures, families and other stakeholders. Addressing gaps in accessibility, technical capacity, service availability and referral mechanisms will contribute to an environment in which children with disabilities can exercise their rights, enhance their functioning and independence, participate more fully in their communities and achieve improved overall wellbeing.

1. **Rationale for Disability Assessment and Intervention**

Children with disabilities continue to experience significant barriers to accessing essential services, participating fully in their communities and realizing their rights and potential. The number, characteristics and specific support needs of children with disabilities remain inadequately documented in Somalia, limiting the ability of families, service providers and relevant institutions to plan and provide appropriate assistance. These challenges are particularly pronounced among vulnerable and marginalized populations, including internally displaced children, children living in rural and nomadic communities, working children, orphans and children from economically disadvantaged households. Gender, displacement, poverty and geographic isolation can further compound disability-related vulnerabilities and should therefore be considered when identifying and responding to individual needs.

Promoting disability inclusion requires more than identifying the presence of an impairment. Children with disabilities should have opportunities to participate meaningfully in family and community life, access appropriate services and support, develop their capabilities and achieve greater independence and wellbeing. This requires a holistic approach that recognizes each child's individual circumstances, strengths and needs while addressing the physical, social, economic, communication and attitudinal barriers that may restrict participation.

Comprehensive assessment is an important component of early identification and intervention for children with disabilities, developmental delays and other functional difficulties. A structured assessment process can help determine a child's functional abilities and support needs and identify appropriate interventions, assistive devices, specialized services and referral pathways. Assessments should consider relevant areas of functioning, including mobility, vision, hearing, communication, cognition, behaviour, psychosocial wellbeing, self-care, social interaction and participation in everyday activities.

Assessment should be undertaken with a clear understanding of its purpose and should inform subsequent intervention planning, implementation, referral and progress monitoring. It should also consider the child's family and living environment, recognizing that parents and caregivers play an important role in identifying challenges, understanding the child's day-to-day functioning and implementing recommended support.

Assessment processes should therefore be individualized, child-centred, inclusive and sensitive to age, gender, disability and contextual vulnerabilities. Most importantly, assessment should not be treated as an end in itself but as the starting point for practical action. Findings should lead to appropriate and feasible interventions, referrals and follow-up mechanisms that strengthen children's functioning, independence, participation, protection and overall wellbeing.

1. **Consultancy Objective**

The objective of the assignment is to gather information for decision-making and intervention in the following four areas:

1. Screening.
2. Recommending intervention.
3. Individual program planning and implementation.
4. Progress monitoring and evaluation.
5. **Scope of Work**

Assessment teams must consider the purpose of each assessment and gather initial information at the onset of the process. The following are some general considerations, which will vary depending on the purpose of the assessment.

- What is the purpose of this assessment, or why is it being conducted (for example, screening, recommending intervention, program planning and implementation, progress monitoring, program evaluation)?
- What are the characteristics of the child (for example, age, physical abilities, communication skills, temperament, delay or disability)?
- Who will take the lead or coordinate the assessment (for example, early childhood special educator, physical therapist, speech–language pathologist)?
- Where will the assessment sessions take place (for example, home, childcare program, classroom, playground)?
- Who will be involved in the assessment (for example, parents, other family members, early childhood special educator, related service practitioners), and what roles will these individuals assume (for example, facilitator, observer, assessor)?
- When will the assessment sessions take place (for example, in the morning, after child’s nap)?
- How will the assessment be conducted (for example, formal testing, observation, interview)?
- What areas of development or content will be assessed? Will all integrated developmental domains or content areas be the focus of the assessment?
- What assessment instrument(s) will be used (for example, formal test, observational checklist, play- based measure, family interview)?
- How will the assessment area(s) be set up (for example, amount of space needed, equipment or materials needed)?
- What skills or behaviors are important to the child’s family, and what are the family’s priorities (for example, walking, talking, social skills, eating, toileting, literacy)?
- What skills or behaviors are important to the child in his or her environment (for example, communicating, toileting, turn-taking, following directions)?
- What adaptations are necessary for the child to display optimal skills (for example, use of an alternative communication system, adaptive seating, assistive technology)?

1. **Deliverables**

The following services and outputs are expected:

1. Detailed work plan for undertaking the assessment.
1. Assessment Report and Debrief on the findings
2. Proposed intervention e.g. (type of equipment, availability, estimated price) other recommended support.
3. Workplan on the way forward
2. **Supervision and Management**

ADRA Somalia

1. **Timeframe**: The assignment will be conducted over a duration of **40 days** during the months of October 2026 and November 2026.

Proposals should include:

1. Detailed description of proposed approach and methodology
2. Projected budget – including projected travel and in-country accommodation and subsistence costs.
3. Short overview of how the candidate (s) meets the qualifications, experience and skills requirements
4. **Qualifications and Experience of the Preferred Consultant**

The assignment may be undertaken by an individual consultant, consultancy firm, or multidisciplinary team with expertise in disability screening, functional assessment, rehabilitation and individualized intervention planning.

The preferred consultant/team should meet the following requirements:

- Hold an advanced university degree in a relevant field such as rehabilitation sciences, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, psychology, developmental psychology, speech and language therapy, public health, social work, disability studies, medicine, nursing or another closely related discipline.
- Have at least five (5) years of demonstrated professional experience in disability screening, functional assessment, rehabilitation, early intervention, assistive technology, case management or related disability-inclusive programming.
- Demonstrate practical experience conducting comprehensive assessments of children with disabilities, developmental delays or functional difficulties, including identification of individual support and intervention needs.
- Have demonstrated experience assessing functional needs across areas such as mobility, vision, hearing, communication, cognition, developmental functioning, psychosocial wellbeing, behaviour, self-care and activities of daily living.
- Demonstrate experience in recommending appropriate assistive devices and technologies, including mobility aids, visual and hearing support, communication devices, adaptive equipment and other individualized solutions.
- Have experience developing individualized intervention, referral and follow-up plans based on assessment findings.
- Demonstrate knowledge of available rehabilitation, health, psychosocial, protection and disability-support services and experience establishing or utilizing referral pathways for children requiring specialized assistance.
- Have a strong understanding of child safeguarding, informed consent, confidentiality, protection and ethical standards applicable when working with children and persons with disabilities.
- Demonstrate experience working with vulnerable and marginalized populations, including internally displaced persons, rural and nomadic communities, economically vulnerable households and other crisis-affected populations.
- Previous professional experience in Somalia is highly desirable. Familiarity with the Somali context, including available disability services, cultural considerations and barriers affecting persons with disabilities, will be a strong advantage.
- Demonstrate strong skills in data collection, analysis, documentation and preparation of high-quality technical reports and practical recommendations.
- Demonstrate the ability to engage effectively with children, parents and caregivers, community structures, government institutions, service providers and humanitarian/development actors.

**Mandatory Statutory and Compliance Requirements**

- Consultants/firms must be legally eligible to undertake consultancy services in Somalia and must submit the applicable registration and statutory documentation.
- A valid Somalia Tax Compliance Certificate (TCC) issued by the relevant tax authority is mandatory and must be submitted as part of the application. Proposals that do not provide a valid Somalia Tax Compliance Certificate may be considered non-responsive.
- The consultant/firm should also disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest and confirm its commitment to ADRA's safeguarding, protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and other applicable policies and codes of conduct.

1. **Submission of Proposals**

To achieve the objectives of the assignment, the consultant will be expected to take complete responsibility for all the activities identified in the TOR. The Technical Proposal should contain a complete description and explanation of the proposed methodology for the Assignment (work plan), timelines and any other resources that the consultant will make available to effectively execute the assignment.

The Financial Proposal should stipulate the professional fees, travel, taxes, etc for the assignment. All fee and costs are to be expressed in USD.

jobs.title: Casework Supervisor
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:**
The Casework Supervisor manages staff providing direct client services across the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and Refugee Social Service (RSS) case management program. The Casework Supervisor plans programming, coordinates service delivery, supervises a team, ensures program goals are met, and satisfies budgetary, compliance, and reporting responsibilities for the assigned portfolio. This position is based in Louisville, Kentucky, with regular on-site presence within the office.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Staff Supervision responsibilities**

- Lead and develop direct service staff through facilitation of team meetings and individual supervision, including coaching and goal setting.
- Liaise regularly with HQ colleagues for guidance, case consultations, direct financial assistance, and other support as needed, and share relevant information with the casework team.
- Cultivate a respectful and supportive environment for team members and clients.
- Recruit, train, and manage the team in accordance with IRC’s People Manager Standards.
- Carry out timely, professional interventions to ensure responsive, appropriate, and client-centered service delivery.
- Train direct reports on using IRC systems such as Integra, ETO, and IRIS.
- Representing IRC in public, professional, and governmental fora as needed.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Service Delivery**

- Guide PIR program implementation and ensure all required services are completed in a timely manner.
- Assign cases to caseworkers and manage timely provision of services including airport pickups, provision of safe, sanitary, and affordable housing, home visits, school enrollment, domestic health assessments, and connection to community resources as applicable.
- Supervise the RSS Case Management Program, including staff referrals, connection of clients to services, and tracking client participation and progress
- Ensure follow-up on all necessary services, including application to public benefits as applicable, referrals to immigration services, applications for Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and medical and mental health needs.
- Provide oversight so each client receives at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days during their service period.
- Ensure case closeout procedures are followed once a client has reached the goals of their program.

**Partnership Building**

- Manage relationships with property owners and managers to expand access to sources of affordable housing.
- Collaborate with colleagues to encourage timely internal referrals for additional services, such as employment, immigration services, and intensive case management.
- Identify and maintain relationships with local government and community-based organizations to connect clients with necessary benefits and services.
- Develop relationships with community resources such as shelters for temporary housing, domestic violence shelters, mental health providers, and medical specialists.
- Develop and maintain vendor relationships that create budgetary savings and improve efficiency.

**Documentation, Reporting and Contract Compliance**

- Ensure that case file documentation is maintained in compliance with contract requirements.
- Guide the timely implementation of program updates as needed.
- Liaise with the HQ colleagues to ensure thorough understanding of program guidelines and disseminate guidelines to the direct service team.
- Review data to meet donor reporting requirements.
- Assist with the preparation for all monitoring visits, including IRC, the Kentucky Office for Refugees (KOR), and the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR).
- Monitor program execution to ensure compliance with all funding requirements; communicate program needs to the management team.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree is strongly preferred, preferably in social work or related field

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum two to three years of experience implementing domestic refugee resettlement or similar programs
- Experience supervising, supporting, and training staff strongly preferred
- Experience in program management and responsibility for budget management preferred

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Familiarity with Integra, IRIS, SMART, and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) strongly preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
- Ability to prioritize and manage time effectively
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a team member in a multicultural environment
- Excellent written and oral communication skills in English; proficiency in a language spoken by client populations is a plus
- Valid driver’s license, reliable access to a vehicle with current insurance, and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of a standard office environment and ‘field’ time in and around the service delivery area to perform the above-outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($$59,962.5 - annually). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements”.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Program officer
jobs.description:
**About GHP**

One billion people will never see a qualified health worker in their lives. For over thirty years, GHP – [www.thet.org](http://www.thet.org) – has been working to change this, training health workers to build a world where everyone has access to affordable and quality healthcare. We do this by leveraging the expertise and energy of the UK health community, supporting health partnerships between hospitals, colleges and clinics in the UK and those overseas.

From reducing maternal deaths in Uganda to improving the quality of hospital care for injured children in Myanmar, we work to strengthen local health systems and build a healthier future for all. GHP’s work is rooted in the Health Partnership Model, which builds long-term, institutional relationships between health organisations in the UK and LMICs based on co-development, reciprocal learning, and mutual benefit.

**The UFUQ Programme**
The UFUQ Programme supports the rebuilding of postgraduate medical training for Syrian doctors, working across four specialties: Emergency Medicine, Anaesthesia, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, and Psychiatry. It brings together relevant Syrian local stakeholders such as the Scientific Councils along with established international medical colleges and societies, and Global Health Partnerships (GHP), which coordinates the programme together with UOSSM. UFUQ is funded by the European Union; GHP is the employing entity for this role.
The programme has several linked strands of work. One strand (track) delivers postgraduate diploma training directly to trainees. This role sits within Track 3, Institutional Strengthening, which focuses on a different but connected goal: helping each Scientific Council build the internal governance, standards, and continuing-education systems it needs to run its own specialty training over the long term, so that capability remains in Syria once the programme ends.
Track 3 builds on two years of prior work in North-West Syria. Following the liberation and the programme's expansion to cover the whole country, the scope of this work has been revised accordingly. Contracting is complete with two of the four international partners, and is in progress with the remaining two.
**The Track 3 Standard Operating Procedures**
Track 3's day-to-day work is guided by a single reference document, referred to here as "the SOP". It sets out, step by step, how the three main outputs of Track 3 are produced, reviewed, and approved: an Operational Manual for each Scientific Council, a set of priority Clinical Guidelines, and a framework for continuing medical education. The SOP also sets out who is responsible for each step, how quality is checked at each stage, and how progress and problems are tracked and reported over the programme's life. The SOP will be reviewed on a regular basis
**UFUQ Programme — Job Description**

considering emerging needs and priorities of implementation and the position holder will play a key role in informing this iterative development. The SOP and governance structures are themselves being formalised during this contract period, so part of the first few months genuinely involves bedding in a new system alongside Syrian counterparts, not just running an established one.
**1. Role Purpose**
The Programme Officer, Track 3 is responsible for the day-to-day leadership of the Track 3 activities translating the Track 3 workplan, RACI matrix, and governing templates into consistent, quality-assured practice across all four specialties. The role sits at the centre of Track 3's delivery model — holding the common architecture and quality standard that GHP is responsible for, while ensuring every deliverable is genuinely co-produced and owned by the Scientific Councils and Professional Associations it serves. Per the SOP, each deliverable is a piloted product that embeds institutional capacity in the SC/PA. This is intentionally a single-person role covering all four specialties, matching its seniority and pay grade; the postholder works closely with the Senior Programme Coordinator and GHP's Medical Education Technical Team to take full ownership of these responsibilities. Each Scientific Council has its own secretariat and coordination person handling specialty-level legwork — the postholder's role is to hold the connective tissue together across all four, not to do each specialty's work personally.
The postholder is the responsible for keeping Track 3 activity on schedule, for the technical and institutional quality of its three flagship deliverables (Operational Manual, Clinical Guidelines, CME Framework and Plan) in addition to assuring alignment and harmonization with the other tracks and the rest of track three activities , and for the integrity of the monitoring evidence used to assess programme success.
**2. Key Responsibilities**
2.1 SOP implementation and workplan management
•
Own, apply and refine the Track 3 SOP as the context requires for all four specialties, ensuring activities proceed in the sequence, timing, and ownership model it defines. (for example coordinating the stakeholder mapping and conference funding application in collaboration with the technical team)
•
Track delivery of the standardised workplan phase by phase (Foundation, Development, Consolidation, plus cross-cutting activities) and flag schedule risk early.
•
Coordinate the parallel drafting processes across the four specialties so outputs remain structurally coherent without becoming templated or losing specialty-specific content.
•
Ensure Phase 0's Institutional Reality & Mandate Mapping and Legal/Mandate Validation are completed before Manual drafting begins, and keep each specialty's standing committees to a Minimum Viable Governance Structure (2–3 core committees, expanded only where capacity and demonstrated need justify it) rather than the full illustrative list.
2.2 Deliverable oversight and quality assurance
•
Lead the standard document-review procedure for all three deliverables: structural/template compliance review, cross-specialty coherence check, coordination of GESI review, STC multi-stakeholder review, and preparation for Scientific Councils/Professional Associations sign-off.

•
Maintain the checklist evidence log and confirm no deliverable is marked complete without documented GHP quality sign-off from the GHP technical group
•
Safeguard the co-production and ownership standard specifically: confirm Arabic-primary drafting on the Operational Manual, SC/PA members named as co-authors, and evidence of at least two co-production workshops per specialty per phase.
2.3 Governance and stakeholder coordination
•
Support and, where chaired by GHP, help run the monthly Specialty Technical Committee (STC) meetings, keeping Operational Manual implementation and deliverable status as a standing agenda item. Represent the STC as a GHP-facilitated coordination platform outside the Ministry of Health
•
Support facilitating and Coordinating the monthly GHP–International Counterpart bilateral and maintain the joint risk log.
•
Coordinate quarterly Track 1 / Track 3 discussions with AICPD on curriculum and accreditation, applying the SOP's baseline-dependent sequencing
•
Define and review Dependency & Contingency Matrix so a Track 1 delay is flagged before it cascades into SC endorsement or accreditation-work delay.
•
Hold structured, candid conversations with SC and PA members — separately from the International Counterpart — to assess institutional and relational progress, not only outputs.
2.4 Monitoring, evidence and reporting
•
Conduct document review against Output indicators and maintain the Success Checklist evidence log on a continuous basis. Treat indicator wording as intentionally general — deliverable content specifics are a floor set by the templates and remain to be agreed with the SC/Syrian Board, not fixed unilaterally by this role.
•
Prepare quarterly progress and financial reports, the annual report, and the three structured phase review reports (Month 4, Month 12, Month 18–19).
•
Ensure all reporting narrates warning indicators transparently, whether or not yet resolved.
2.5 Risk and warning indicator management
•
Identify and log warning indicators as soon as they arise, without waiting for a scheduled review point.
•
Raise active warning indicators in the GHP–International Counterpart bilateral and agree specific, time-bound corrective action as per escalation steps in the SOP .
**3. Person Specification**
3.1 Essential
•
Degree in public health, medical education, health policy, international development, health governance, health system strengthening, international relations or a related field; a postgraduate qualification is an advantage.
•
Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-stakeholder health or education programmes involving professional or scientific governing bodies, ideally in fragile, conflict-affected, or post-conflict settings.
•
Working understanding of postgraduate medical education systems, clinical governance, or CME/CPD accreditation processes.
•
Strong document and quality-assurance review skills — able to assess a draft deliverable against a template and a defined standard, and to give structured, actionable feedback.
•
Professional fluency in both Arabic and English, written and spoken.
•
Excellent facilitation, relationship-management and diplomatic skills, with demonstrated ability to support institutional ownership rather than substitute for it.
UFUQ Programme — Job Description

•
Experience maintaining monitoring and evidence systems (evidence logs, indicator tracking, structured reporting).
•
Strong organisational skills and comfort managing several parallel workstreams (four specialties, three deliverables) against a fixed timeline.
3.2 Desirable
•
Familiarity with international postgraduate medical education standards (e.g. WFME) and their adaptation to national contexts.
•
Experience integrating gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) considerations into programme design and review, rather than as a standalone reporting requirement.
•
Prior experience working with Syrian health institutions, diaspora-led medical governance bodies, or comparable emerging professional councils.
•
Experience coordinating with a companion programme track or partner organisation delivering an interconnected but separately governed workstream.
**4. Key Relationships Relationship Nature of engagement**
Senior Programme Coordinator (line manager)
Day-to-day direction, escalation of risks; quality sign-off sits with the GHP technical group rather than this role alone
Medical Education Technical Team (GHP)
Close, hands-on support so the postholder can take full ownership of Track 3 responsibilities Scientific Councils / Professional Associations/Syrian Board Primary co-production partners; candid structured conversations; follow up on deliverable authorship and sign-off
Specialty Technical Committees
Monthly coordination platform; deliverable review before submission International Counterparts Joint delivery of advisory and capacity-building input; monthly bilateral and risk log
AICPD / Track 1 team
coordination on shared curriculum, accreditation , research and other shared areas GESI Consultant Coordination of GESI review at defined checkpoints
MEAL Team
Assure needed MEAL activities are conducted to serve the impact measurement
**5. How Performance Is Assessed**
Performance in this role is assessed against the same three categories used to define Track 3 success, so that the Programme Officer's own effectiveness and the programme's progress are read from the same evidence base:
•
Output indicators — deliverables produced to template, on schedule, with complete evidence logged (Operational Manual, Clinical Guidelines, CME Framework and Plan; committee ToRs; STC and bilateral minutes).
•
Institutional & relational indicators — genuine SC/PA authorship and growing independence, evidenced through structured conversations and observed meetings, not only through document sign-off.
•
Warning indicator management — indicators identified promptly, corrective action agreed and tracked, and timely escalation where an indicator persists.
Probation is 2 months, with a check-in at 4 weeks covering relationship-building progress and workplan familiarity rather than deliverable completion, since deliverables take longer than this to produce.

Council relationship struggles for reasons outside the postholder's control (for example, the Council's own capacity constraints or political disruption), performance review distinguishes between process indicators the postholder controls (meetings held, issues logged and escalated, support offered) and outcome indicators only partly within their control (the Council's pace of authorship), so the postholder is not judged on what they cannot fully drive.

**Notes**

aligned to the UFUQ Program contract period (17 months of substantive activity (assuming a November 2026 start), with potential extension depending on the next funding cycle; timing of that decision relative to contract end will be communicated as it becomes clear

jobs.title: Safety and Security Assistant - Idleb Saraqeb
jobs.description:
**General Description of the Programme:**

Established in 1977, GOAL is an international humanitarian and development agency, committed to working with communities to achieve sustainable and innovative early response in crises, and lasting solutions to poverty and vulnerability. GOAL has worked in over 60 countries and has responded to almost every major humanitarian disaster. We are currently operational in 18 countries.

GOAL began operations in Syria in 2013 responding to the acute needs of conflict-affected communities. GOAL's areas of operations include but not limited to Aleppo, Idleb and Lattakia Governorates, and is expanding to new governorates in Syria. Programmes focus on Food and Nutrition Security, WASH, Shelter, Livelihoods/ERMS and Emergency Response with an emphasis on cash and voucher modalities. GOAL Syria implements its programmes directly, with over 500 staff based in Syria, and through Syrian NGO partners. GOAL's programme works at the household and community levels to improve community resilience and household coping strategies.

**Job purpose:**

**Duties, objectives and competencies**

- **E**nsure the management of the Guards.
- The Safety and Security Assistant manage all safety and security equipment, ensuring that it is well maintained and functional, including First aid Kits and Fire Extinguishers.
- Ensure the safety of the offices and staff.
- Train new staff members in communication protocols and the communication tree.
- Maintain a table of contact numbers for all staff working in the Office, Update, and share list with Safety & Security Manager Northwest and Central Syria.
- Keep a copy of the visitor log and check it monthly.
- Ensure that the APPROPRIATE contact numbers are available in Idlib office.
- Ensure that all staff in the Office have an updated 'GOAL ID.
- Report daily to the Safety & Security Manager Northwest and Central Syria about the general situation of the office regarding the safety and the security of the building.
- Maintain verbal contact with all cars and Team Leaders in the field at regular intervals.
- Ensure that the team travel has the appropriate equipment as required per GOAL safety procedures and vehicles have a First Aid Kit.
- Follow GOAL communication procedures.
- Gather information from the field as and when requested.
- Raising reports on accidents and violations.
- To carry out any other relevant tasks as requested by Safety & Security Manager North and Central Syria

**Requirements (Person Specification):**

- BA degree.
- Work experience in NGO for 3 years at least.
- Work at S&S in NGOs for 1 year at least.
- Good spoken and written Arabic.
- Computer skills – (Word and Excel…)
- Technical skills, including setup, and social media…
