jobs.title: Facilitador/a Comunitario/a en Agricultura y Seguridad Alimentaria
jobs.description:
**Acerca del Empleo**

En Feed the Children, conocemos el valor de las personas excepcionales. Más importante aún, queremos encontrar a las personas adecuadas para unirse a nuestro equipo. Nos enorgullece proporcionar a nuestros/as colaboradores/as un entorno propicio para el empleo productivo, gratificante y a largo plazo.

Como una organización líder en la lucha contra el hambre, Feed the Children se dedica a ayudar a las familias en dificultades. Estamos buscando personas que se unan a nosotros mientras brindamos esperanza y recursos a aquellos que carecen de lo esencial para la vida. Creemos que todos juntos, trabajando en conjunto, podemos vencer el hambre y crear un mundo donde ningún niño se acueste con hambre. En Feed the Children creemos que las "personas" y su "talento" son lo esencial. El logro de nuestra misión y visión solo puede suceder a través de un equipo de colaboradores (as) que inspira, motiva, apoya, poseen vocación de servicio y están comprometidos (as) con nuestros beneficiarios.

**Nombre de la Posición:**

Facilitador/a Comunitario/a en Agricultura y Seguridad Alimentaria

**Sede:**

Región de Sololá, Guatemala

**Misión:**

El/la Facilitador/a Comunitario/a en Agricultura y Seguridad Alimentaria/a es el implementador principal y punto de contacto con los participantes en la región de Sololá, se centrará en la implementación de actividades programáticas relacionadas con el mejoramiento de la educación de niños y las escuelas; sobre técnicas de producción agropecuaria sostenible a nivel escolar, familiar o comunitario, gestión financiera e iniciativas de generación de ingresos para adolescentes, jóvenes y adultos. Tendrá la responsabilidad de ejecutar todas las actividades de campo y organizar la colaboración de los participantes durante todo el año, asegurando que los procesos se completen e informen de acuerdo con la planificación y dentro de la disponibilidad presupuestaria.

**Reporta a:**

Coordinador/a de Educación y Seguridad Alimentaria

Perfil de la Posición

- Calificaciones y Experiencia:
- Finalización exitosa de estudios a nivel secundario, diversificado o de educación media con enfoque técnico en los temas de la agricultura, seguridad alimentaria o similar.
- Certificaciones de capacitación en temas relacionados con agricultura, seguridad alimentaria cambio climático o similar.
- Al menos tres (3) años de experiencia en campo como promotor o facilitador en ONGs, cooperación internacional o agencias gubernamentales relacionadas con Educación, Seguridad Alimentaria, Cambio Climático o Agricultura Sostenible.
- Conocimientos técnicos intermedios en seguridad alimentaria y sistemas de producción agropecuaria sostenible.
- Experiencia implementando programas productivos agropecuarios sostenibles.
- Capacidad para trabajar con la diversidad cultural, incluyendo conocimiento básico o intermedio del idioma Maya Kaqchikel, o experiencia en la implementación de estrategias de comunicación e interpretación que aseguren una interacción efectiva con participantes hablantes de Maya Kaqchikel. (Indispensable)
- Experiencia avanzada en conducción de motocicletas y vehículo 4x4 con transmisión manual en terrenos accidentados. Contar con licencia de conducir motocicleta y vehículo 4x4 vigente (Indispensable).
- Conocimiento y dominio básico en programas y sistemas informáticos para la elaboración de informes, creación de materiales info-educativos, recolección de datos y uso de bases de datos.
- Habilidad para proyectar y mantener un ambiente de trabajo calmado mientras a la vez opera en un ambiente definido por tiempos y fechas límites y requeridos por sus clientes internos y externos.
- Excelentes habilidades interpersonales, relacionales y de comunicación, con una historia de inspirar la colaboración a lo largo de varias funciones.
- Poseer una conexión profunda con el contexto local de las comunidades en condiciones de riesgo social.
- Facilidad para adoptar y promover una actitud positiva hacia los procesos de cambio, renovación y transformación.
- Estar comprometido (a) a crear un impacto positivo en el mundo, con inspiración, pasión, compasión y vocación de servicio.

**Funciones Esenciales:**

**Mejora de la educación, la seguridad alimentaria y la resiliencia:**

- Crear y capacitar grupos comunitarios en temas como huertos escolares, familiares y comunitarios, agricultura sostenible, producción pecuaria, gestión financiera y generación de ingresos, utilizando una metodología práctica de aprendizaje.
- Facilitar la mejora de los entornos escolares en agua, saneamiento e higiene, así como en huertos pedagógicos, bajo el enfoque de escuelas saludables.
- Fortalecer la calidad educativa mediante la provisión de materiales escolares para docentes y estudiantes.
- Implementar metodologías en las comunidades y proporcionar retroalimentación sobre su ejecución para la creación o adaptación de estrategias y materiales informativo-educativos.
- Motivar a los participantes a compartir los conocimientos adquiridos con otros miembros de la comunidad.

**Monitoreo, evaluación y rendición de cuentas**

- Elaborar un plan de seguimiento comunitario bajo la supervisión del/la Coordinador/a de Educación y Seguridad Alimentaria, en colaboración con el/la Facilitador/a Comunitario/a de Nutrición y Salud.
- Reportar las actividades utilizando los instrumentos de control establecidos.
- Recopilar datos para encuestas e información relacionada con la seguridad alimentaria.
- Identificar las necesidades de la comunidad e informar los hallazgos al/la Coordinador/a de Educación y Seguridad Alimentaria.

**Participación comunitaria para alianzas estratégicas**

- Representar a Feed the Children a nivel comunitario ante autoridades locales.
- Establecer comunicaciones e interacciones externas efectivas con actores clave de la comunidad.

**Apoyo a programas y gestión administrativa**

- Ejecutar los procesos administrativos y financieros necesarios para la correcta ejecución de fondos.
- Apoyar actividades de otros programas, como el de Apadrinamiento Infantil.

**Responsabilidades Adicionales**

Las funciones y responsabilidades laborales establecidas anteriormente no son exclusivas y es posible que se requiera que el/la titular del puesto realice tareas adicionales dentro de lo razonable y de acuerdo con su nivel de habilidades y experiencia.

**Compromiso con la Igualdad de Género, la Diversidad y la Inclusión**

Feed the Children se compromete a crear un entorno de trabajo diverso, inclusivo, respetuoso y seguro donde todas las personas sean tratadas de manera justa, con dignidad y respeto. Feed the Children prohíbe expresamente y no tolerará la discriminación, el acoso, la represalia o el acoso laboral de las personas en cualquier entorno laboral. Parte de nuestra estrategia es aumentar la representación y la incorporación de mujeres en nuestros equipos de talento humano, así como de personas que se identifican con diferentes razas y etnias.

**Política de Igualdad de Oportunidades**

En Feed the Children creemos en la Igualdad de Oportunidades, por lo tanto, consideramos a todos (as) los (as) solicitantes según el mérito sin importar raza, sexo, color, origen nacional, religión, orientación sexual, edad, estado civil, discapacidad u otra característica protegida por la ley aplicable. De igual manera estamos comprometidos con promover el enfoque de género como un eje transversal en nuestra organización.

**Política de Salvaguarda**

Feed the Children se esfuerza por proporcionar un entorno libre de explotación sexual y abuso, así como de acoso en todos los lugares donde se implementan programas de ayuda y desarrollo. Feed the Children tiene una política de tolerancia cero contra la explotación sexual y el abuso, así como el acoso. Feed the Children espera que sus colaboradores (as) mantengan altos estándares éticos, protejan la integridad y reputación organizacional, y garanticen que el trabajo de Feed the Children se realice de manera honesta y justa, en línea con las políticas de salvaguarda y asociadas de Feed the Children. Necesitamos mantener a los niños seguros, de modo que nuestro proceso de selección incluye controles de antecedentes, reflejando nuestro compromiso con la salvaguarda de los niños.

Nuestro principal compromiso es impulsar una cultura centrada en la promoción de entornos seguros y protectores para los niños que participan en los diferentes programas implementados por Feed the Children en El Salvador, Guatemala y Honduras, garantizando la tolerancia cero a toda forma de daños y abuso hacia ellos.

Las violaciones a las políticas establecidas estarán sujetas a acciones correctivas, incluida la terminación del empleo.

***Para continuar con tu proceso de postulación ingresa al siguiente link y completa toda la información solicitada:***

[**Atracción y Adquisición de Talento - Feed the Children Centroamérica 2026: Rellenar formulario**](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/jvUCzMaus2)

¡Gracias por tu interés en formar parte de nuestro equipo, para juntos crear un mundo donde ningún niño y ninguna niña se vaya a la con hambre!

jobs.title: Project Manager – Support to Democratic Reforms in Jordan (SDR)-National Position
Consultant - Conformité Fiscale, Paie & Statut Juridique RH (7 Pays)
jobs.description:
INTERSOS est une Organisation Humanitaire Non Gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, qui a l’objectif d’assister les victimes de désastres naturels et de conflits armés. INTERSOS base son action sur les valeurs de la solidarité, de la justice, de la dignité humaine, de l’égalité des droits et des opportunités pour tous les peuples, du respect des diversités, de la cohabitation, de l’attention aux groupes sociales les plus vulnérables.

## **Termes de référence**

**Intitulé du poste** : Consultant - Conformité Fiscale, Paie & Statut Juridique RH (7 Pays)

**Code :** SR-00-10284

**Lieu d’affectation** : Télétravail avec déplacements éventuels sur le terrain

**Date de prise de fonction** :02/11/2026

**Durée du contrat** : 8 semaines (indicatif)

**Sous la supervision de :** Coordinateur RH Régional Afrique

**Contexte général du projet**

INTERSOS est une organisation humanitaire fondée en 1992, qui intervient en première ligne dans les situations de crise. Dans ses pays d'intervention, INTERSOS vient en aide aux populations les plus vulnérables touchées par les conflits, l'extrême pauvreté et les catastrophes naturelles ou d'origine humaine, au cœur de zones complexes et difficiles d'accès où les besoins humanitaires sont les plus importants et la présence humanitaire souvent faible. Dans ces contextes, INTERSOS se concentre sur la fourniture d'une assistance humanitaire vitale aux populations déplacées de force ainsi qu'aux communautés d'accueil, principalement dans les domaines de la Protection, de la Santé et de la Nutrition.

Afin de garantir la pérennité et la sécurité de ses opérations, INTERSOS place la maîtrise des risques et la conformité légale au cœur de son modèle de gestion. L'organisation s'attache à identifier, prévenir et maîtriser les risques juridiques, fiscaux et sociaux liés au déploiement de son personnel, tout en garantissant une structuration contractuelle sécurisée et un ancrage institutionnel solide auprès des autorités locales.

Les opérations d'INTERSOS sont guidées par sa Charte des valeurs et par les principes humanitaires d'humanité, de neutralité, d'impartialité et d'indépendance. Plus précisément, INTERSOS est une organisation sans frontières, impartiale, indépendante, sensible aux cultures locales, attentive aux capacités locales, professionnelle dans la solidarité et transparente. INTERSOS adhère également au Code de conduite pour le Mouvement international de la Croix-Rouge et du Croissant-Rouge et pour les ONG lors des opérations de secours en cas de catastrophe.

## **Objectif général de la position**

INTERSOS déploie du personnel international sous contrat de droit italien — notamment via des collaborations coordonnées et continues (co.co.co) relevant de régimes d'expatriation spécifiques (ex. loi 398/87) ou des contrats de travail autonomes — au sein de 7 pays d'Afrique : Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Tchad, Cameroun, République démocratique du Congo (RDC) et République centrafricaine (RCA).

Objectifs principaux du conseil :

- Conformité légale et opérationnelle : Déterminer l'ensemble des obligations fiscales, parafiscales, sociales et déclaratives qui incombent à INTERSOS (employeur) et aux collaborateurs dans chaque pays d'affectation, selon la nature de leur contrat.
- Optimisation, ingénierie de la paie et efficience des coûts: Identifier l'ensemble des leviers d'optimisation légale, à travers la structuration du paquet salarial, la formalisation de cadres conventionnels spécifiques (ancrage institutionnel), ainsi que l'évaluation de scénarios contractuels alternatifs. L'objectif est de rationaliser, chiffrer et sécuriser la charge fiscale et sociale globale supportée par l'organisation et ses collaborateurs.

## **PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS ET TÂCHES**

### VOLETS EXAMINÉS PAR LE CONSULTANT

Pour chaque pays, l'analyse devra couvrir les volets suivants :

- Statut ONGI et cartographie des exonérations : Régimes préférentiels applicables à INTERSOS, portée des exonérations sur le personnel international sous contrat de droit italien, et conditions/procédures pour en bénéficier.
- Obligations de l'employeur et retenues à la source : calculs, immatriculations, déclarations, versement des impôts sur le revenu, taxes sur les salaires, contributions patronales/salariales, ainsi que formalités d'arrivée et de départ du personnel.
- Obligations personnelles des collaborateurs (Distinction des responsabilités) : Identification claire des obligations fiscales, sociales et déclaratives incombant personnellement au personnel international, afin qu'INTERSOS puisse l'informer et le sensibiliser adéquatement.
- Traitement, ingénierie de la paie et scénarios contractuels : Analyse de l'imposition locale du salaire de base, per diem, indemnités (logement, transport, hardship/risque) et arbitrage des modes d’octroi. Cette analyse inclura la comparaison avec des scénarios contractuels alternatifs (détachement, contrat local, mission courte ou consultance) pour évaluer la base légale, les risques et l'incidence financière (employeur/employé).
- Cadre conventionnel d'établissement et démarches de clarification administrative : Identification des instruments juridiques et administratifs prévus par la réglementation locale (accords-cadres, conventions d'établissement, procédures d'interprétation administrative ou rescrits) permettant de formaliser, sécuriser et harmoniser le statut fiscal et social de l'organisation et de ses collaborateurs auprès des autorités compétentes.
- Rémunérations versées depuis l'étranger et situations de détachement : Analyse des incidences fiscales et sociales locales pour les salaires ou avantages versés totalement ou partiellement depuis l'Italie (ou un autre pays), et gestion des cas de détachement ou d'affectation temporaire.
- Conventions internationales, régimes spécifiques et protection sociale : Analyse des règles d'imposition des non-résidents (seuil des 183 jours, conventions fiscales), des taxes et formalités spécifiques liées aux travailleurs étrangers (y compris les permis de travail), ainsi que du traitement local des régimes de protection sociale et de retraite maintenus en Italie ou à l'étranger (accords de sécurité sociale et justificatifs de non-double imposition).
- Documentation, conformité et gestion des risques: Identification stricte des pièces justificatives et documents à obtenir, transmettre et conserver. Cartographie des risques de non-conformité (défaut de retenue, retard, redressements), pénalités encourues et recommandations de mesures préventives. L’analyse devra également couvrir la distinction entre l’entité qui verse le salaire et celle qui en supporte le coût réel, ainsi que l'évaluation des éventuels risques historiques et la proposition de mesures de régularisation.

### LIVRABLES ATTENDUS

- Livrable 1 – Rapport pilote (2 pays) : Analyse complète de deux pays pilotes (sélectionnés lors de la réunion de cadrage) permettant de valider la méthodologie, la structure des rapports et le niveau de détail attendu.
- Livrable 2 – Rapports opérationnels par pays (7 pays) : Rapports détaillés incluant un résumé exécutif RH/Finance qui précise pour chaque pays ce qu’INTERSOS doit retenir, déclarer, payer, obtenir et conserver, auprès de quelle administration et dans quel délai. Chaque rapport devra être accompagné des références précises aux textes légaux et réglementaires applicables.
- Livrable 3- Note d'orientation stratégique et d'optimisation : Note synthétique identifiant, pour chaque pays, des pistes d'optimisation fiscale et sociale légales, documentées et défendables en cas de contrôle. Selon les spécificités de chaque pays, le consultant analysera l'une ou plusieurs des pistes suivantes :
- Ingénierie de la paie et scénarios contractuels alternatifs : Restructuration et efficience des composantes de la rémunération (indemnités, avantages en nature, per diem) et comparatif chiffré entre le modèle actuel et d'autres typologies d'engagement. Pour chaque option, l'analyse précisera la base légale, les conditions d'application, les formalités, les risques ainsi que l'incidence financière pour INTERSOS et pour l'expatrié
- Ancrage institutionnel : Formalisation administrative et accords préférentiels auprès des autorités locales (accords d'établissement, procédures de rescrit) afin de sécuriser le cadre d'intervention.
- Livrable 4 – Matrice opérationnelle transversale (Excel) : Outil de pilotage au format Excel regroupant pour l'ensemble des pays : Pays / Typologie contractuelle / Obligation / Base légale / Assiette / Taux ou Barème / Échéance / Administration / Formulaire ou Document / Sanction encourue.
- Livrable 5 – Checklist de conformité et Note d'information des collaborateurs : Grille d'évaluation pratique pour les contrôles internes RH/Finance et note synthétique à destination du personnel international précisant leurs obligations fiscales et sociales personnelles.
- Livrable 6 – Présentation de restitution : Séance de restitution orale présentant les principales conclusions, la cartographie des risques prioritaires et la feuille de route opérationnelle à destination des équipes INTERSOS.

### MÉTHODOLOGIE

- Analyse juridique et opérationnelle : Fondée sur les codes fiscaux, lois de finances, textes sur les cotisations sociales, régimes des ONGI, travailleurs étrangers et conventions internationales (fiscales et de sécurité sociale).
- Sécurisation juridique : Chaque conclusion doit s'appuyer sur une base légale précise, avec signalement explicite des ambiguïtés ou divergences administratives.

## PROFIL DU CONSULTANT OU CABINET

- Qualifications : Titulaire d’un diplôme supérieur en droit fiscal ou en droit des affaires, le consultant ou le cabinet devra justifier d’au moins 7 ans d’expérience confirmée en fiscalité internationale, ingénierie de la paie et gestion des rémunérations d’expatriés. Une maîtrise avérée des conventions fiscales internationales, des accords de sécurité sociale ainsi qu’une connaissance approfondie des législations locales dans plusieurs des pays concernés sont indispensables.
- Expertise sectorielle : Expérience auprès d'ONG internationales fortement souhaitée et capacité à mobiliser des experts fiscaux locaux dans les 7 pays.
- Langue : français professionnel obligatoire (oral et écrit) pour l'ensemble de la mission et des livrables. Anglais maîtrise professionnelle

### DURÉE ET CALENDRIER INDICATIF (8 SEMAINES)

- Semaine 1 : Réunion de cadrage et validation de la méthodologie.
- Semaines 2 à 4 : Production des rapports pilotes sur 2 pays (Livrable 1), intégrant les premiers schémas d'ingénierie de la paie.
- Semaines 5 à 6 : Rédaction des rapports pour les 5 autres pays (Livrable 2) et élaboration du Plan de structuration du paquet salarial et du cadre d'orientation institutionnel (Livrable 3).
- Semaine 7 : Remise de la version consolidée de l'ensemble des livrables (Rapports par pays, Livrable 3, Matrice Excel - Livrable 4, et Checklist - Livrable 5).
- Semaine 8 : Intégration des retours et séance de restitution finale (Livrable 6).

Le consultant pourra proposer un calendrier différent s’il estime qu’il permet de garantir une meilleure qualité des livrables

### COORDINATION, CONFIDENTIALITÉ ET PROPRIÉTÉ

- Supervision : Traitement en étroite collaboration avec les départements RH et Finance d'INTERSOS. INTERSOS fournira au consultant, dans la mesure nécessaire à la réalisation de la mission, les informations utiles relatives au modèle contractuel et à la gestion de ses salariés internationaux. Le consultant devra signaler dès le démarrage toute information complémentaire nécessaire à la bonne réalisation de l’étude.
- Confidentialité : Obligation stricte concernant les données salariales, financières et contractuelles.
- Propriété : Propriété exclusive d'INTERSOS sur l'ensemble des livrables produits.

### CONTENU DE L'OFFRE

- Offre technique : compréhension de la mission , méthodologie, approche pour les 7 pays, organisation de l'équipe, experts locaux éventuellement mobilisés , calendrier et description des livrables
- Offre financière : L’offre financière sera soumise sous la forme d’un prix forfaitaire, ferme et global (all-inclusive) en euros (€), couvrant l'intégralité des coûts de la mission. Le candidat présentera un détail séparé de son budget incluant les honoraires, les coûts éventuels des experts locaux, les frais de déplacement éventuels, les taxes applicables et tout autre coût lié à la prestation.
- Profil & Références : CV du consultant principal ou des membres clés de l’équipe, CV des experts locaux, le cas échéant, références de missions similaires, expérience auprès d’ONG internationales ou d’organisations similaires, expérience dans les pays concernés.

### CRITÈRES D'ÉVALUATION DES OFFRES

- Compréhension et méthodologie (15 %) : Pertinence et clarté de l'approche globale pour l'analyse des 7 pays d'affectation et compréhension des enjeux liés aux contrats de droit italien (co.co.co et travail autonome).
- Expertise fiscale, sociale et en ingénierie de la paie (15 %) : Maîtrise de la fiscalité internationale, de la sécurité sociale transfrontalière et des schémas d'optimisation légale de la paie.
- Expérience de la gestion du personnel international (10 %) : Pratique avérée des régimes d'expatriation, des statuts de non-résidents et du traitement des collaborateurs internationaux.
- Couverture géographique des 8 pays (15 %) : capacité d'intervention directe ou via un réseau éprouvé d'experts fiscaux et juridiques locaux dans les 7 pays concernés.
- Expérience sectorielle ONGI et cadres conventionnels (10 %) : Connaissance approfondie du secteur humanitaire, des accords d'établissement et des procédures de concertation auprès des administrations locales.
- Qualité et caractère opérationnel des livrables (10 %) : Clarté opérationnelle des fiches pays, de la matrice comparative Excel, des checklists RH et de la note d'orientation stratégique (ingénierie de la paie et ancrage institutionnel).
- Offre financière (25 %) : Transparence, compétitivité et cohérence globale du budget

### RÉSULTAT FINAL ATTENDU

INTERSOS doit disposer d'un outil de pilotage clé en main couvrant les pays d'affectation pour déterminer avec précision ses obligations employeur (calculs, retenues, déclarations, paiements) et maîtriser la conformité fiscale et sociale du personnel sous contrat de droit italien. L'organisation devra également être en mesure de décider de la stratégie d'optimisation la plus adaptée pour chaque pays (ingénierie de la paie, recours à des scénarios contractuels alternatifs, ou ancrage institutionnel), tout en ayant une vision claire de l'incidence financière, de la distinction entre coût réel et flux de paiement, ainsi que des mesures nécessaires pour régulariser les éventuels risques historiques.

### MODALITÉS DE PAIEMENT

Le paiement sera échelonné selon la validation explicite par INTERSOS des livrables attendus :

- 20% à la validation du Livrable 1 (Rapports pilotes sur 2 pays et validation définitive de la méthodologie) ;
- 40% à la remise de la première version consolidée des rapports pays, de la matrice Excel et du plan d'ingénierie de la paie (Livrables 2, 3 et 4) ;
- 40% à la validation finale de l'ensemble des livrables (Checklist/Note d'information - Livrable 5) et après la tenue de la séance de restitution (Livrable 6).

Chaque versement est conditionné par la validation écrite préalable des livrables par les départements Ressources Humaines d'INTERSOS.

## **Profil requis**

- Diplôme supérieur en droit fiscal ou en droit des affaires.
- Expérience auprès d'ONG internationales fortement souhaitée et capacité à mobiliser des experts fiscaux locaux dans les 7 pays.
- Au moins 7 ans d’expérience confirmée en fiscalité internationale, ingénierie de la paie et gestion des rémunérations d’expatriés.
- Une maîtrise avérée des conventions fiscales internationales, des accords de sécurité sociale ainsi qu’une connaissance approfondie des législations locales dans plusieurs des pays concernés sont indispensables.
- Français professionnel obligatoire (oral et écrit) pour l'ensemble de la mission et des livrables.
- Anglais maîtrise professionnelle
- Vision stratégique
- Bon sens de l'organisation et de la planification
- Flexibilité comportementale

jobs.title: Consultancy for the Development of a Facilitation Guide and Facilitation of Trainings for Beach Management Unit (BMU) Members in Kwale County
jobs.description:
## **The full Request for Proposals (RFP) document is available at the following link:** [**https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/17XdKj9sJdsiyUeuwm7_8UrN15OJ6Zo97**](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/17XdKj9sJdsiyUeuwm7_8UrN15OJ6Zo97)

## **About CEFA**

**CEFA** - European Committee for Training and Agriculture (Comitato Europeo per la Formazione e l’Agricoltura) is an Italian Non-Governmental Organisation established in 1972 and active in countries across Africa, Latin America and Eastern Europe. CEFA’s medium- and long-term interventions in the agricultural, environmental and human rights sectors focus on the sustainable development of communities, achieved by involving local counterparts and promoting the active participation of beneficiaries.

## Project Summary

The project **AGROBLUE - Promoting Sustainable Agriculture and Blue Economy in Kenya** is a 36-month initiative implemented in four sub-counties (Galole, Tana Delta, Msambweni and Lunga Lunga) within Tana River and Kwale Counties, Kenya. The project is implemented by a consortium of partners with extensive experience in resilient agricultural models and the blue economy, led by Action Against Hunger (ACF) in collaboration with CEFA, MWARP and Politecnico di Milano. The initiative works closely with the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Health to ensure institutional sustainability and long-term impact.

The project aims to increase food security, income and resilience to food crises through an integrated, climate-smart and gender-sensitive approach. It addresses barriers such as low productivity, high post-harvest losses and the limited economic participation of women by providing farmers and fishermen with the tools, technologies and knowledge needed to diversify their livelihoods and increase their incomes, while protecting natural ecosystems. The project works across three result areas:

- Increasing access for small-scale farmers and artisanal fishermen to products and services for climate-resilient production and fishing systems, and to community practices that prevent ecosystem degradation;
- Increasing access of farming and fishing families in rural and coastal areas to technical and financial services, infrastructure and knowledge to sustainably manage supply chains that add value to their food production, in order to increase and diversify their income;
- Sensitising communities on nutritional needs, with a focus on vulnerable groups such as women and children, to improve access to and consumption of diverse, nutritious food.

Within the project, CEFA works in the fisheries and beekeeping components, targeting farmers’ groups and Beach Management Units (BMUs) through training and the provision of equipment. The intervention adopts a value chain strengthening approach covering production, post-harvest handling and marketing.

## Objectives of the Consultancy

The objectives of the consultancy are:

- The development of a **facilitation guide** covering practical offshore fishing techniques and best practices; basic navigation, including the use of navigation equipment and the interpretation of weather and sea conditions; maritime safety, emergency preparedness and response procedures; sustainable management of marine resources, including marine ecosystem conservation, pollution prevention, overfishing and the impacts of climate change; and fisheries data collection and analysis, including data on fishing fleets, fishers, fishing gear, fishing effort and landings. The guide will provide practical guidance and standardised messages to support the delivery of the planned training sessions.
- The delivery of **four training topics, through five trainings and 18 sessions in total**, to BMU members, including fishermen, boat owners, members of BMU executive committees and fish traders, through refresher and cascading trainings, to strengthen technical skills, maritime safety practices, environmental awareness and the capacity to collect and use fisheries data.

## Timeline and Duration of the Consultancy

The consultancy covers a total of **37 days**:

- 10 days for the design and preparation of the training sessions and the drafting and finalisation of the facilitation guide;
- 24 days for the facilitation of the trainings, divided among the training sessions as set out under Methodology below;
- 3 days for the drafting and submission of the final consultancy report.

The consultancy shall commence in **November 2026** and will extend over a period of four months, concluding in **February 2027**. The allocation and scheduling of the training days will be agreed with the CEFA team according to the availability of participants, the project implementation timeline and the logistical requirements of each session, within the overall number of consultancy days established in the contract.

## Methodology

**Participants**

The trainings will be delivered to members of Beach Management Units, notably:

- Fishermen;
- Members of BMU executive committees (e.g. chairperson, secretary, treasurer);
- Boat owners and individuals involved in eco-tourism activities;
- Fish traders and dealers.

The total number of participants across all trainings will be **501**, drawn from **three** BMUs already selected in Msambweni and Lunga Lunga Sub-Counties.

**Content and Design of the Trainings**

BMU members will participate in five trainings covering, progressively, offshore fishing, marine resource management, maritime safety, and fisheries data collection and analysis:

- **Refresher Training on Offshore Fishing:** 20 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a two-day training per BMU. The training will focus on practical offshore fishing techniques, navigation, interpretation of weather and sea conditions, and basic safety practices during fishing operations. One practical **at-sea session** is planned as part of the two-day training for each BMU. CEFA will provide the boat and all necessary safety equipment.
- **Refresher Training on Offshore Fishing (Restitution Session):** A one-day feedback and cascading session on offshore fishing will follow, reaching 210 BMU members (70 per BMU) through three sessions, so that the trained participants can pass on the knowledge acquired to a wider group of BMU members. The trained BMU members will deliver the cascading sessions under the supervision of the Consultant.
- **Environmental Impacts and Conflict Reduction in the Use of Marine Resources:** 20 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a one-day training per BMU. The training will address marine ecosystems and their conservation, pollution and its impact on marine resources, overfishing and sustainable fisheries management, climate change and its effects on marine ecosystems, and approaches to reducing conflicts over the use of marine resources. It will also include a module on co-management areas and co-management plans for sustainable use.
- **Maritime Safety Training for Offshore Fishing:** 50 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a one-day training, delivered through six sessions in total (two per BMU), each targeting 25 fishermen. The training will focus on the risks of illegal fishing, safety procedures, safe use of protective gear, safe operations at sea, risk prevention, emergency preparedness and response, and appropriate action in case of accidents or other emergencies during offshore fishing.
- **Fisheries Data Collection and Analysis:** 7 members from each BMU will participate in a two-day training delivered through three sessions, for a total of 21 participants. The training will cover data collection methodologies, data sources and basic data analysis, with a focus on fisheries information such as fleet characteristics, number of fishers, fishing gear, fishing effort and fish landings.

## Safeguarding and Do No Harm

The Consultant shall comply with CEFA’s safeguarding, PSEAH (Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment), Code of Conduct and data protection requirements. Personal data collected from participants, including attendance lists and pre- and post-training assessments, shall be handled in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019 and used only for the purposes of this assignment.

## Management and Implementation Responsibilities

The Consultant will report directly to the CEFA Project Manager and the CEFA Project Officer in charge of AGROBLUE implementation.

The Consultant will be responsible for their own insurance during the contract period, and CEFA will not be responsible for any injury or damage incurred during the assignment. The Consultant will also meet their own communication and incidental costs. The Financial Proposal must include all anticipated expenses, including travel to and from the assignment sites, local transport in Kwale County, meals and accommodation.

## Qualifications of the Consultant

**Essential**

- A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Fisheries, Marine Resources, Aquaculture or a related field from a reputable institution;
- Relevant professional experience in fisheries development, sustainable fisheries management, offshore fishing, marine ecosystem conservation and/or capacity building of fishing communities and BMUs, preferably at least 7 years;
- Demonstrated experience in training fishermen and/or BMU members in the thematic areas of this assignment;
- Strong participatory training and facilitation skills, and good report-writing skills;
- Ability to deliver training in Kiswahili and English.

**Desirable**

- Previous experience working with fishing communities on the Kenyan coast, particularly in Kwale County.

jobs.title: Regional Finance Manager - Central America Region
jobs.description:
**About Feed The Children:**

Feed the Children is a global movement to end child hunger. Together with communities, we provide children in the U.S. and around the world with food, essentials, and opportunities so they can survive and thrive.

**Our Mission:**

Feed the Children is a global movement working to end child hunger in the U.S. and around the world. Together with communities, we provide food, essentials, and opportunities so every child can survive and thrive.

**Our Vision:**

Creating a world where no child goes to bed hungry

**People & Culture**

At Feed the Children, we recognize the value of exceptional people and, more importantly, we seek to attract those who align with our values and purpose. We take pride in offering our team members an environment that promotes productive, fulfilling, and sustainable long-term employment.

We recognize that our human talent is essential, and that fulfilling our mission and vision is only possible thanks to a team of collaborators who inspire, motivate, support, possess a true vocation for service, and are committed to impacting and transforming the lives of our beneficiaries.

We are looking for people who wish to join us in the mission to bring hope and resources to those lacking the essentials to live. We firmly believe that, by working together as one team, we can overcome hunger and **create a world where no child goes to bed hungry.**

**Regional Finance Manager - Central America Region**

**Mission:** The Regional Finance Manager will contribute to the financial management of Feed International Country Offices mainly in Central America Region (CA) or any other country offices as assigned. The position supports the following areas: Financial accounting, Operations support budget preparation, financial reporting, audit/internal controls review and systems support.

The role will oversee the Country Offices finance teams and will report to the VP of International Finance Operations with a dotted line reporting to the Regional Director. The Regional Finance Manager will work with HQ finance team on month end close, year-end procedures and other common finance duties as assigned including coordination of audits. This is a hybrid position and can be based in Guatemala or Honduras. This role serves as a member of the Regional Management Team.

**Location:**

Guatemala

**Qualifications and Experience:**

- Bachelor’s degree in public accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field with a CPA.
- Master’s degree in finance, Business Administration (MBA), Accounting, or a related field will be considered an advantage.
- Specialized training in financial management for nonprofit organizations, auditing, internal controls, or risk management will be considered an advantage.
- More than 10 years of demonstrated experience in finance and operations
- More than 5 years of proven experience as a Financial Manager.
- Minimum 5 years of experience leading, coaching, and developing finance or cross-functional teams, fostering accountability, collaboration, and high performance.
- Experience providing functional leadership for financial operations across multiple countries or regional structures will be considered an advantage.
- Strong knowledge of international accounting principles and financial reporting standards applicable to nonprofit organizations.
- Advanced knowledge of tax and labor legislation and regulatory requirements across El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras.
- Demonstrable skills in the development of finance and accounting policies, procedures, and systems in the context of an international NGO.
- Fluency in both English and Spanish is essential.
- Knowledge of U.S. Government grants, contracting and auditing standards as they apply to effective management of multi-year funds.
- Working knowledge of finance and regulatory standards (GAAP) and International Finance Reporting Systems (IFRS).
- Experience driving standard 4x4 vehicles in rough terrain. Valid driver's license.
- Ability to project and maintain a calm work environment while operating in a time and deadline-defined environment required by internal and external clients.
- Excellent interpersonal, relational, and communication skills, with a history of inspiring collaboration across multiple functions.
- Possessing a deep connection with the local context of communities in social risk conditions.
- Ability to adopt and promote a positive attitude towards processes of change, renewal, and transformation.
- Committed to creating a positive impact on the world, with inspiration, passion, compassion, and a sense of service vocation.

**Essential Job Functions:**

**Financial Management, Accounting and Reporting**

- Work with the Global Finance team to provide guidance on financial accounting issues and audit support to country offices.
- Coordinate the resolution of all accounting system issues and financial reporting.
- Provide and document the financial tracking and monitoring of ledgers, accounts, and related financial documents.
- Support the creation of financial reports and other required financial disclosure documents.
- Provide guidance to Country Offices for financial files management and maintenance.
- Assist in the review of payroll systems.

**Budget Management and Financial Planning**

- Monitor and review operational budgets to support financial stability, ongoing program viability, efficient cost structures, and appropriate spending.
- Produce reports and follow-up on any Country Offices outstanding advances (workshop and travel) for review by the Global Finance team.
- Monitor the project’s operational plan and provide guidance for the performance and achievement of the project’s finance, budget, administrative and procurement matters.

**Internal Controls, Risk Management, Audit and Compliance**

- Work with the Regional Management Team to develop and implement robust systems of internal controls and ensure general management of risk and control environment.
- Support funder-initiated financial reviews for Feed the Children International portfolio.
- Ensures continual review of internal and strategic controls, communications, risk assessments, and maintenance of documentation.

**Partner and Sub-awardee Financial Management**

- Provide financial oversight and support to the sub partner.
- Review financial reports of all sub-awardees for processing monthly.
- Supports partners as needed to ensure sound financial management and operations.
- Work closely and transparently with all external partners, including third-party vendors and consultants, on financial and Operations support as requested by HQ.

**Country Office Financial and Administrative Oversight**

- Effectively communicate and present critical financial matters to the Regional Management Team, Country Offices, Funders, and other external stakeholders.
- Oversee and review of all financial documentation uploaded for Feed International Country Offices.
- Provide oversight to the finance and administration Country Office POC and ensure their compliant and efficient support of the project’s activities.

**Financial Systems, Processes and Capacity Building**

- Train and Orient staff on new accounting systems and business processes as they relate to finance.
- Adapt policies from HQ for local implementation.

**Operations, Procurement, Fleet and Goods in Kind Management**

- Overall responsibility of Feed the Children International Goods in Kind system.
- Oversight of Fleet management policies and processes.

**Additional job responsibilities**

The job duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the post holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reason and in line with their level of skills and experience.

**Safeguarding Policy**

Feed the Children strives to provide an environment free from sexual exploitation and abuse and harassment in all places where relief and development programs are implemented. Feed the Children holds a zero-tolerance policy against sexual exploitation and abuse and harassment. Feed the Children expects its employees to maintain high ethical standards, protect organizational integrity and reputation, and ensure that Feed the Children work is carried out in honest and fair methods, in alignment with the Feed the Children safeguarding and associated policies. Violations to stated policies will be subject to corrective action up to and including termination of employment.

**Standards of Conduct**

Feed the Children is committed to creating and promoting a people-centered culture, at the heart of the strategy, while simultaneously living the values as core drivers to guide people's behavior, shaping the culture. The Standards of Conduct serve as the foundation for guiding the best way to behave, so that it positively benefits the organization and respects the needs of others. Their purpose is to better understand what constitutes commonly acceptable and appropriate behavior within the culture of Feed the Children and is not intended to monitor employees, although it may serve as the basis for disciplinary measures, including termination of employment.

**Commitment to Gender, Diversity and Inclusion**

Feed the Children is committed to reducing gender gaps and promoting gender equality and equity in all our operations and is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful, and safe work environment where all individuals are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. Feed the Children expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or workplace bullying of individuals in any work environment. As part of our strategy, we aim to increase the representation women and inclusion in our human talent teams, as well as individuals who identify with different races and ethnicities. Violations to stated policies and protocols will be subject to corrective action up to and including termination of employment.

jobs.title: Project Manager – Northeast Syria
jobs.description:
We are currently recruiting a **Project Manager – Northeast Syria** to join our **Programs** team.

This is a **country-based position** in **Deir ez Zor, Syria**, with regular field visits across project locations in Deir ez Zor and Al-Hasakeh governorates, including approximately **25% travel to Al-Hasakeh**.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring **standard pre-employment checks and enhanced due diligence**.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. Our team works across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, delivering Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience. We do this by working with local actors to develop safe, inclusive and evidence-based programming that is conflict-sensitive, climate-smart and responsive to community needs.

**About the Opportunity**

The Project Manager will oversee Relief International's programme portfolio in **Deir ez Zor and Al-Hasakeh governorates**, ensuring projects are implemented effectively, safely and in compliance with donor and organizational requirements. The role is responsible for the planning, delivery, monitoring and adaptation of projects, ensuring high-quality implementation, strong stakeholder coordination and effective management of resources.

Working in one of the most complex humanitarian environments in the region, you will coordinate closely with technical teams, support departments, partners and local stakeholders to ensure projects achieve their objectives on time and within budget. You will provide leadership to multidisciplinary teams while navigating operational challenges, evolving security dynamics and changing humanitarian needs.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced humanitarian project manager looking to take ownership of a diverse programme portfolio and contribute to impactful humanitarian action in Northeast Syria.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- Lead project planning, implementation and monitoring to ensure programmes are delivered on time, within budget and in compliance with donor and organizational requirements.
- Oversee programme and budget performance, ensuring effective use of resources and timely resolution of operational or financial challenges.
- Conduct regular field visits to monitor progress, engage with staff and partners, identify risks and support adaptive programme management.
- Ensure high-quality donor reporting, project documentation and project management systems are maintained and updated.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with local authorities, partners, donors and coordination bodies, representing Relief International in relevant forums.
- Mentor and supervise programme teams, strengthening capacity in project management, compliance, reporting and accountability.
- Support proposal development, programme design and strategic planning processes for future programming opportunities.
- Ensure risk management, safeguarding and safety considerations are integrated across all project activities.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- Bachelor's degree in International Development, Project Management, Business Administration or another relevant field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Proven experience managing humanitarian or development projects, including implementation oversight, budget management, reporting and stakeholder coordination.
- Experience managing and supporting teams in complex operational environments.
- Strong organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
- Excellent communication and relationship-management skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams.
- Experience working with donor-funded programmes and understanding of donor compliance requirements. Experience with SHF/OCHA, ECHO and US Government-funded projects is highly desirable.
- Knowledge of one or more sectors such as Health, Protection or other areas relevant to Relief International's programming.
- Professional fluency in English is essential. Arabic language skills are highly desirable.
- Experience working in Northeast Syria or a comparable humanitarian context would be a significant advantage.

jobs.title: Security Advisor - North Africa

jobs.title: Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist
jobs.description:
***Candidates must be authorized and able to work daily in Bogotá.***

**Position Summary**

The Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist serves as the Foreign Assistance Unit's (FAU’s) technical adviser for digital-infrastructure and connectivity programming across South America. The position provides technical analysis and recommendations to support Government officials in identifying, assessing, and structuring U.S. Government-funded digital development programs that advance U.S. foreign-policy and national-security objectives and respond to partner-country priorities. The portfolio may include information and communication technologies (ICT) deployment (fiber, wireless, satellite, and last-mile connectivity), digital inclusion strategies, cybersecurity considerations for critical digital infrastructure, and broadband/connectivity expansion planning.

The incumbent reports to the FAU’s Programs Team Lead and translate digital connectivity needs into technically credible and implementable program designs. Responsibilities include preparing technical scopes of work; contributing to program-design and acquisition or assistance documents; reviewing proposals, market studies, network designs, specifications, cost estimates, schedules, and other technical products; and providing input to the FAU on technical alternatives, implementation risks, project readiness, sustainability, and operations and maintenance considerations. The Specialist collaborates with other FAU technical and program personnel to ensure that digital infrastructure investments are appropriately incorporated into sector-specific programs.

Drawing from practices used across the U.S. Department of State and other U.S. Government agencies, the incumbent provides technical analysis and recommendations to support programming aligned with the America First foreign policy framework, including economic security, strategic competition, trusted and secure digital infrastructure, supply chain resilience, and partnerships that reinforce U.S. interests. The salary will be commensurate with an FSN 11 position within Colombia.

**Major Duties and Responsibilities**

**1. Strategic Digital Infrastructure Program Development (35%)**

Supports the identification, assessment, and design of USG-funded digital-connectivity programs that advance U.S. foreign-policy and national-security objectives. Responsibilities include:

- Identifies potential digital-development programming opportunities based on USG priorities, partner-country needs, connectivity gaps, existing investments, and regional market developments.
- Supports programs involving ICT infrastructure deployment, broadband and last-mile connectivity expansion, digital inclusion initiatives, secure network architecture, and cybersecurity-conscious infrastructure design.
- Translates connectivity needs and policy objectives into technically credible, feasible, and sustainable program concepts.
- Supports the development of technical scopes and statements of work, program descriptions, acquisition and assistance planning documents, budgets, implementation approaches, and other program-design products.
- Develop recommendations regarding the technical scope and requirements for market assessments, network design studies, cybersecurity risk assessments, digital-inclusion needs analyses, and other project-preparation activities.
- Provides technical recommendations regarding requirements, performance standards, implementation assumptions, schedules, cost parameters, and risk-mitigation approaches in collaboration with relevant FAU personnel.
- Assesses project readiness, technical feasibility, implementation risks, operational requirements, and the capacity needed to operate and maintain proposed digital infrastructure.
- Incorporates sustainability, commercial viability, and operations and maintenance considerations throughout program design.
- Coordinates technical, programmatic, procurement, financial, monitoring, and stakeholder inputs into coherent digital-development programs.
- Supports the adaptation, expansion, or modernization of existing connectivity programs when performance findings, policy changes, or market conditions warrant revised approaches.
- Identifies technical capability gaps and provides input on potential needs for short-term telecommunications, network engineering, or cybersecurity expertise.

**2. Technical Review and Quality Assurance (30%)**

Provides technical review and quality-assurance support for proposed and ongoing digital-development activities. Responsibilities include:

- Reviews proposals, market studies, network designs, technical specifications, pricing structures, cost estimates, schedules, work plans, and other technical submissions.
- Conducts market research and performs technical and commercial analysis of proposals for pricing, competitiveness, and commercial viability relative to comparable connectivity solutions.
- Conducts technical assessments of proposedapproaches to evaluate if they are credible, implementable, appropriately scaled, priced, and responsive to program requirements.
- Evaluates design assumptions, technology choices, deployment methodologies, energy and energy storage requirements, equipment specifications, sequencing, and operations and maintenance requirements.
- Reviews technical products for consistency with applicable host-country, U.S., and international standards, including relevant cybersecurity and data-protection standards.
- Compares technical and commercial alternatives and provides recommendations to the FAU on their relative feasibility, risks, lifecycle implications, and expected performance.
- Identifies technical gaps and potential implementation risks—including cybersecurity vulnerabilities—and recommends corrective actions or additional analysis.
- Reviews quality-assurance and quality-control approaches, testing requirements, commissioning arrangements, maintenance plans, and other measures necessary to support reliable digital-infrastructure performance.
- Provides technical input during proposal reviews and other procurement or assistance processes, as requested and consistent with applicable procedures and conflict-of-interest safeguards.
- **Conducts technical reviews for** GORs (Grant Officer’s Representatives), CORs (Contract Officer’s Representatives), and FAU leadership on whether technical products appear responsive to applicable requirements while preserving formal acceptance authority for designated USG officials.
- Confirms that designs, certifications, and other regulated technical products are prepared or approved by appropriately qualified professionals when required.

**3. Digital Infrastructure Portfolio Planning and Strategic Analysis (25%)**

Under Programs Team Lead guidance, provides analysis and planning support to guide the FAU's digital-development and connectivity portfolio. Responsibilities include:

- Maintains visibility over proposed, active, and emerging digital-connectivity initiatives supported by the FAU.
- Develops and maintains a digital-development opportunity pipeline that captures project status, technical-preparation needs, strategic relevance, principal risks, and required next steps.
- Provides analysis and recommendations to inform prioritization of large strategic connectivity investments and community-level digital-inclusion activities based on policy relevance, feasibility, readiness, and potential results.
- Conducts technical assessments of how individual digital-infrastructure activities contribute to broader economic-security, digital-inclusion, or strategic-competition objectives, including trusted-vendor and secure-supply-chain considerations.
- Identifies opportunities to connect digital-connectivity investments with complementary programming managed by other FAU specialists, including training, sustainability, and wraparound services needed to achieve public policy goals alongside commercial viability.
- Identifies recurring technical and management risks across the digital-infrastructure portfolio and recommends improvements to future program design.
- Captures and shares lessons from completed and ongoing activities to strengthen technical quality, implementation, and sustainability.
- Prepares technical briefing materials, analytical memoranda, talking points, and recommendations for FAU and Embassy leadership.

**4. Program Quality, Monitoring, and Reporting (15%)**

Supports GORs and CORs in monitoring assigned programs and awards, and assessing their continued strategic relevance and performance. Responsibilities include:

- Reviews program reports, work plans, technical deliverables, deployment updates, schedules, cost information, and performance data as requested by the responsible GOR or COR .
- Collaborates with the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Specialist to gather, validate, analyze, and synthesize information from assigned programs.
- Participates alongside the responsible GOR or COR in site visits, monitoring activities, portfolio reviews, and meetings with implementers, contractors, government counterparts, private-sector partners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders.
- Analyzes implementation progress and identifies technical, quality, cost, schedule, management, sustainability, cybersecurity, and operations and maintenance concerns.
- Reviews information on network quality, testing, contractor quality-control processes, security posture, commissioning, and readiness for intended use, as applicable.
- Provides recommendations to GORs and CORs when independent technical review, testing, cybersecurity assessment, or other specialized support may be required.
- Prepares monitoring observations, technical analyses, and evidence-based recommendations for consideration by the GOR, COR, and FAU leadership.
- Supports performance-management processes and internal reporting on program results, implementation risks, lessons, and strategic alignment.
- Supports assessments of whether programs require technical adjustment, additional analysis, specialized assistance, or revised implementation approaches.

All monitoring and award-support functions shall be performed under the direction of the responsible GOR or COR. The Specialist shall not direct recipients or contractors, approve or reject deliverables, certify technical products, modify award requirements, commit USG funds, or exercise responsibilities reserved for authorized USG officials.

**Supervisory Controls**

The Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist exercises independent technical judgment in assessing digital-infrastructure concepts, reviewing network and connectivity designs, evaluating cybersecurity considerations, developing technical requirements, and recommending approaches to address implementation challenges. The Specialist consults with the Programs Team Lead, responsible GORs or CORs, and other technical personnel when assignments involve significant policy, procurement, financial, security, or specialized technical considerations.

Work is reviewed for technical soundness, responsiveness to program requirements, compliance with applicable procedures, alignment with USG priorities, and contribution to effective program performance.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Minimum Education:** One of the following combinations of education and professional experience is required:

- Master's degree in telecommunications engineering, information and communications technology, computer science, cybersecurity, digital development, or another closely related discipline, plus at least six years of relevant professional experience; or
- Bachelor's degree in one of these disciplines, plus at least 10 years of relevant professional experience.

Telecommunications, ICT, computer science, and digital-development degrees are equally acceptable. A professional certification (e.g., PMP, CISSP, or equivalent) is not required but is beneficial.

**Professional Experience:**

- Progressively responsible experience designing, reviewing, deploying, managing, or monitoring ICT and connectivity infrastructure projects.
- At least two years of direct experience with digital-connectivity projects of different sizes, technologies, and sectoral focus.
- Experience in aligning digital communications projects to social and economic development goals.
- Experience conducting market research and evaluating proposals for pricing, competitiveness, and commercial viability.
- Experience assessing cybersecurity considerations relevant to digital infrastructure and connectivity deployments.
- Experience preparing technical scopes of work and assessing project feasibility, implementation risks, quality, sustainability, and operations and maintenance requirements.
- Experience structuring subcontracted training, sustainability, and wraparound services to support public policy goals alongside commercial viability.
- Experience supporting project implementation, site monitoring, and multidisciplinary teams through clear technical analysis and recommendations.

**Preferred Professional Experience:**

- Experience supporting digital-development or connectivity programs funded by the U.S. Government, multilateral organizations, bilateral donors, or international development institutions.
- Experience working with the Department of State, USAID, MCC, USTDA, DFC, another U.S. Government agency, or a multilateral development institution.
- Experience with digital-inclusion strategies targeting underserved or rural populations.

**Language:** Level IV (Fluent) English and Level V (Fluent) Spanish required.

**Skills and Abilities:**

- Design complex international digital-development programs
- Lead proposal development efforts
- Build relationships with private-sector telecommunications and technology companies
- Translate policy into operational programming
- Integrate technical input into coherent program designs
- Develop strategic partnerships
- Communicate effectively with executive audiences
- Manage competing priorities under tight deadlines
- Produce high-quality analytical and written products
- Evaluate commercial pricing and competitiveness of technical proposals

**Comprehensive knowledge of:**

- ICT infrastructure deployment and connectivity-expansion planning
- Digital inclusion strategies and approaches
- Cybersecurity considerations for critical digital infrastructure
- Program design methodologies and proposal development
- Results-based management
- Digital-infrastructure program design and project-management methodologies
- Market research and competitiveness analysis
- Technical risk identification and mitigation

**Working knowledge of:**

- U.S. foreign policy objectives
- Environmental and social considerations applicable to digital-infrastructure activities
- Government digital-infrastructure planning and public-investment processes
- Procurement and implementation models
- Subcontracting structures for training, sustainability, and wraparound services

**Other Requirements**

- **Candidates must be authorized and able to work daily in Bogotá.**

jobs.title: Project Manager (Kenya Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
**Company/Division:** [inSupply Health](https://insupplyhealth.com/)

**Domain/Unit:** Project Management Unit

**Application Deadline: October 19, 2026**. Shortlisting will be on a rolling basis

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Reports to:** Project Director

**Expected Project Start:** 1 January 2027

**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya

**Organization Overview:**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with offices in Dar es Salaam and across East Africa, and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). We collaborate closely with public and private-sector clients to design optimized, responsive, and resilient supply chain systems. Our dynamic team of local consultants delivers critical services supporting essential health products, adapting proven methodologies to local contexts for long-term impact.

**Job Summary**

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced **Project Manager** to lead the day-to-day delivery of a prospective donor-funded, multi-country and multi-partner project expected to commence on **1 January 2027.**

The Project Manager will be a central delivery role within inSupply Health's Project Management Unit (PMU), responsible for translating project contracts, proposals and results frameworks into integrated workplans, schedules, budgets, staffing plans and clear accountabilities.

Working under the strategic direction of the Project Director, the Project Manager will coordinate day-to-day execution across matrixed technical and country teams, monitor progress and performance, manage risks and dependencies, and drive corrective action to keep delivery on track.

The role will coordinate across seven country teams and five consortium partners, working closely with technical leads, country teams, Finance, MERL, Operations, Procurement, Communications and other PMU functions.

**IMPORTANT:** Appointment to this position is contingent upon the project being awarded and the position being confirmed in the final project staffing plan. Further details about the project and donor will be shared with candidates who reach the final stages of the selection process.

**Responsibilities:**

**Project Planning & Mobilisation**

- Translate contracts, proposals, budgets and results frameworks into integrated annual, quarterly and monthly workplans.
- Establish clear milestones, owners, dependencies, costs and delivery expectations.
- Lead project start-up and close-out activities, including team onboarding, governance arrangements, RACI development and delivery calendars.
- Maintain project baselines covering scope, schedule, budget, resources, risks and benefits.

**Day-to-Day Project Delivery**

- Direct day-to-day execution across project workstreams and matrixed teams.
- Set priorities and ensure clear ownership of actions and deliverables.
- Lead regular project delivery meetings and follow up on actions, dependencies, decisions and delays.
- Track planned versus actual progress and take early action to address delivery challenges.
- Coordinate technical, MERL, Finance, Operations, Procurement, Communications and partner inputs to resolve dependencies.
- Manage changes to scope, schedule, resources and budget through approved change-control processes

**Financial & Resource Management**

- Maintain budget-linked workplans and review project financial performance with Finance.
- Monitor burn rate, expenditure, commitments, forecasts and budget variances.
- Support rolling forecasts and budget rephasing or reallocations where required.
- Monitor staff level of effort and resource utilisation against project requirements.
- Identify resource gaps, competing demands and opportunities for cost efficiency while protecting project scope, quality and results.

**Performance Monitoring & Reporting**

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date project information through project dashboards and reporting systems.
- Prepare monthly project performance reports covering delivery, financial performance, results, risks and priorities.
- Lead project reviews and consolidate project performance for PMU and portfolio reviews.
- Coordinate timely and accurate donor and client reporting.
- Maintain complete and auditable project records.

**Risk, Quality & Compliance**

- Maintain live risk, issue, assumption and dependency registers.
- Resolve operational issues within delegated authority and escalate material issues appropriately.
- Coordinate milestone-based technical reviews and track actions through closure.
- Ensure project delivery complies with contracts, donor requirements, organisational policies, safeguarding requirements and applicable regulations.
- Track audit, client and internal review actions through closure.

**Client, Partner & Stakeholder Coordination**

- Serve as the operational focal point for routine client and partner coordination.
- Coordinate partner deliverables, dependencies and reporting obligations.
- Prepare agendas, decision points, progress updates and action logs for project and governance meetings.
- Identify emerging client needs and provide evidence-based options to project leadership.

**Matrix Team Leadership**

- Set project priorities, roles, deadlines and delivery standards for matrixed team members.
- Hold team members accountable for agreed project deliverables and timelines regardless of their primary reporting line.
- Provide timely feedback and work with Practice Leads, HR and project leadership to address allocation, performance and role-related challenges.
- Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, responsiveness and learning.

**Learning & Continuous Improvement**

- Lead project after-action reviews and close-out retrospectives.
- Capture lessons, adaptations, efficiencies and reusable project management practices.
- Contribute project management insights, schedules, staffing plans, budgets and risk analysis to proposals and project extensions.
- Support organisational learning and contribute to project case studies at close-out.

**Qualifications & Experience**

## **Education**

- Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Project Management, Social Sciences, International Development or a related discipline.
- A Master's degree in a relevant discipline is an added advantage.

## **Professional Certification**

- Professional project management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2 or an equivalent credential is preferred.

**Professional Experience**

- At least **7 years** of progressive experience managing complex, multi-country and multi-partner projects or programmes in global health, development or advisory services.
- At least **3 years** of direct responsibility for integrated workplans, budgets, schedules, teams, partner dependencies, risks and client reporting.
- Demonstrated experience managing donor-funded or client-funded projects across multiple workstreams, partners, geographies or technical disciplines.
- Demonstrated experience leading matrixed teams where project authority and formal line management sit in different roles.
- Strong experience in integrated workplanning, budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, resource planning and results tracking.
- Experience coordinating with ministries of health, county governments, donors, implementing partners, consultants and private-sector actors is preferred.

**Key Competencies**

We are looking for a Project Manager who demonstrates:

- Strong delivery discipline and personal accountability for results.
- Sound financial judgement and understanding of budgets, forecasts, burn rates and resource trade-offs.
- Strong planning, prioritisation, sequencing and dependency management.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
- Effective matrix leadership, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills.
- Clear communication and strong meeting facilitation skills.
- Confidence to constructively challenge weak plans, missed commitments and unsupported assumptions.
- Proficiency with digital project management, collaboration, spreadsheet and reporting tools.
- Strong client and stakeholder orientation.
- High integrity and sound judgement.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining attention to detail and deadlines.
- Commitment to collaboration, inclusion, continuous improvement and inSupply's values.

**IMPORTANT:** Appointment to this position is contingent upon the project being awarded and the position being confirmed in the final project staffing plan. Further details about the project and donor will be shared with candidates who reach the final stages of the recruitment process.

**Responsibilities:**

**Grant Management & Budget Operationalisation**

- Conduct grants and financial compliance reviews and coordinate corrective actions.
- Maintain grants and financial risk trackers.
- Support internal and external grant audits and follow up on audit findings.

**Donor Reporting & Documentation**

- Coordinate financial and grants management inputs into donor reports.
- Ensure consistency between project activities, reported results, expenditure and approved budgets.
- Maintain complete, secure and audit-ready grant documentation.
- Support responses to donor financial and grants management queries. Senior Grants and Finance Offic…

**Subaward & Partner Financial Management**

- Support the onboarding and financial management of subrecipients and implementing partners.
- Support partner capacity assessments and risk-based financial and grants compliance reviews.
- Review subaward agreements, budgets, amendments, fund requests and partner financial reports.
- Monitor partner expenditure, burn rates, forecasts and fund utilisation.
- Support risk-based verification of partner expenditure and follow-up on identified gaps.
- Contribute to targeted financial and grants management capacity strengthening for partners.

**Multi-Country & Consortium Coordination**

- Support consistent application of grants and financial management requirements across participating countries and consortium partners.
- Coordinate financial and grants inputs from country and technical teams.
- Support consolidated analysis of budgets, expenditure, forecasts, commitments and financial risks across countries.
- Work closely with Finance, Programme, Procurement, Operations and MEL teams to integrate grant and financial requirements into implementation planning.

**Systems Improvement & Business Development**

- Provide technical guidance to staff and partners on donor compliance, grant management and financial procedures.
- Strengthen grant trackers, templates, SOPs, workflows and reporting tools.
- Support continuous improvement of financial management and grant management systems.
- Support proposal development, including financial sections, budget reviews and donor compliance checks.
- Contribute to funding opportunity analysis and business development activities.

**Qualifications & Experience**

## **Academic & Professional Qualifications**

- A Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Management, Economics or a related field from a recognised university.
- A recognised professional accounting qualification such as CPA(K) or ACCA.
- Current membership in good standing with the relevant professional accounting body, such as ICPAK or ACCA.

**Professional Experience**

- At least 5 years of relevant experience in grants management, donor compliance, programme finance or a related role within donor-funded organisations.
- Experience managing and monitoring multiple donor-funded grants across different funding streams.
- Experience working with major institutional donors such as USAID, FCDO, Global Fund, BMGF, EU and UNITAID.
- Experience supporting donor reporting and internal/external audits.
- Strong experience in grant budgeting, expenditure monitoring, burn-rate analysis and donor financial compliance.
- Experience in subaward management, partner financial oversight and capacity strengthening.
- Experience supporting proposal development and business development processes.
- Experience working collaboratively across Finance, Programmes, Procurement, Operations and MEL functions.

## **Key Competencies**

We are looking for a professional who demonstrates:

- Strong knowledge of donor compliance requirements, grant regulations and contractual obligations.
- Strong financial analysis, problem-solving and risk-management skills.
- Excellent budgeting, forecasting, expenditure monitoring and variance analysis skills.
- Strong planning, organisation and documentation management, with exceptional attention to detail.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
- Ability to facilitate and strengthen the capacity of staff and partners.
- High levels of integrity, accountability and professionalism.
- Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and deliver within deadlines.
