jobs.title: Coordinator and legal institutional representant of the programme in Brazil
jobs.description:
HEKS/EPER has been engaged in **Brazil** since the 1980s and focuses its interventions on the Cerrado region (Minas Gerais and Bahia). HEKS/EPER works currently with five local partner organizations which cooperate among each other, supporting key networks of family farming and Traditional Peoples and Communities regarding access to land, sustainable natural resources management, agroecology, bioeconomy and inclusion to markets. Special attention is given to the inclusion of young people and women. The programme is closely supported by global staff: the head of programmes Latin America and Caribbean, a thematic advisor specialized in biodiversity, land governance and sustainable food systems, an M&E-advisor, a finance controller, and others.

For our programme in Brazil, we are looking for an experienced, strategically minded and inspiring coordinator to take up this position on 1rst of December 2026 or by agreement:

## **Coordinator and legal institutional representant of the programme in Brazil**

### **Your responsibilities:**

- Assume the institutional legal representation of the HEKS/EPER Swiss branch in Brazil, via power of attorney.
- Lead the forward- thinking and creative strategic development of the programme in cooperation with the local and global teams and local actors within the financial framework.
- Ensure the effective and efficient implementation of the programme through participative monitoring, evaluation, learning and steering of the projects.
- Support the partners in drawing up annual and phase project-reports and write annual programme-reports, based on the reports of the partners.
- Support fundraising for the projects with Swiss donors by contributing to the drafting of projects and writing of reports and presenting them to the donors.
- Prospect for funding opportunities and lead the acquisition of national, regional and international funds through engagement with donors and the development of proposals.
- Represent HEKS/EPER towards the government, the public and international, regional and local organisations and networks including the Act Alliances structures.
- Establish and maintain close cooperation with other actors in Brazil, incl. international and local NGOs, public authorities and research institutions, businesses, for joint activities and resource mobilization in consortia.
- Supervise and assume final responsibility for financial and administrative matters, in accordance with HEKS/EPER standards.
- Supervise the finance officer and ensure compliance with local laws and obligations, the guidelines, and the institutional governance of HEKS/EPER.
- Contribute to reflection and learning with the other teams of HEKS/EPER in Latin America and the Caribbean and with Global Cooperation of HEKS/EPER.

### **To be successful you bring:**

- Minimum of 10 years of experience in the development sector, including 5 years in a similar position, ideally for international NGOs in Brazil.
- Excellent conceptual, strategic development, monitoring and evaluation skills.
- Excellent communication and networking skills.
- Strong financial management skills.
- Successful track record in the acquisition and implementation of internationally funded projects.
- Cultural sensitivity, flexibility, initiative, commitment.
- University degree or equivalent in a relevant field (agricultural, environmental or social sciences).
- **Excellent skills of oral and written English and Portugues** are compulsory, good knowledge of Spanish an asset.
- **We are looking exclusively for a Brazilian resident (this is not an international/expat position).**

### **What you can expect from us:**

- A varied and multidisciplinary position.
- Attractive employment conditions.
- The position may be contracted either under Brazil’s Consolidation of Labor Laws (Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho – CLT), the country’s statutory employment regime, or through a service agreement with an independent contractor registered as a legal entity (Pessoa Jurídica – PJ).
- Duty station: preferably Brasilia, with regular visits to the projects in Minas Gerais and Bahia and occasional international traveling.
- Contract of indefinite duration.

jobs.title: Consultoría de asistencia técnica especializada en Monitoreo, Evaluación, Investigación y Aprendizaje (MERL) - Venezuela
jobs.company: Plan International Latin America and the Caribbean
jobs.description:
Consulta los términos de referencia en el siguiente vínculo:

[https://plan-international.org/uploads/sites/56/2026/10/TdR_Consultoria_MERL_Venezuela.pdf](https://plan-international.org/uploads/sites/56/2026/10/TdR_Consultoria_MERL_Venezuela.pdf)

1\. La organización A través de su trabajo en 80 países con economías en desarrollo en África, Asia y las Américas, Plan International busca alcanzar a la mayor cantidad posible de niñas, niños y adolescentes, particularmente a quienes se encuentran en situación de exclusión o marginación, mediante programas de calidad que generen beneficios duraderos, el trabajo en asocio y una operación efectiva. Plan International promueve los derechos de la niñez y está comprometida con la protección de niñas y niños y con la igualdad de género. La organización adopta medidas para que sus intervenciones y la actuación de las personas vinculadas a ellas sean coherentes con sus políticas de salvaguarda, igualdad de oportunidades y no discriminación.

2\. Antecedentes Los terremotos ocurridos el 24 de junio de 2026 en Venezuela generaron necesidades humanitarias para niñas, niños, adolescentes y personas cuidadoras. Plan International Venezuela implementa una operación nacional de respuesta y recuperación con un modelo operativo ligero, liderado por socios locales, que combina respuesta humanitaria, recuperación temprana y fortalecimiento de capacidades en protección, educación, WASH, medios de vida/estabilización de hogares y fortalecimiento de socios. En este contexto, Plan International requiere servicios especializados y de duración definida para liderar y asegurar la calidad del sistema de monitoreo, evaluación, investigación y aprendizaje (MERL) de la operación, generando evidencia útil, segura y oportuna para la toma de decisiones, la rendición de cuentas, el aprendizaje programático y el reporte a donantes.

3\. Objeto de la consultoría Brindar asistencia técnica especializada, con autonomía técnica y organizativa, para diseñar, implementar y asegurar la calidad del sistema de monitoreo, evaluación, investigación y aprendizaje (MERL) de los programas multisectoriales de Plan International Venezuela y sus organizaciones socias, en el marco de la respuesta humanitaria y de recuperación.

4\. Alcance de los servicios • Diseñar y actualizar marcos MERL, planes de monitoreo, matrices de indicadores, flujos de datos y herramientas de recolección, alineados con la Política y los Estándares Globales de MERL de Plan International. • Asegurar datos desagregados por edad, género, discapacidad y otros criterios relevantes, cuando sea seguro y factible. • Implementar controles de calidad de datos, incluyendo validación, revisión de bases, consistencia, integridad, oportunidad y trazabilidad. • Consolidar avances de indicadores, reportes narrativos, tableros internos y aportes MERL para informes a donantes y espacios de coordinación. • Apoyar evaluaciones, líneas de base/finales, revisiones en tiempo real, estudios rápidos y análisis de necesidades. • Implementar mecanismos seguros, accesibles y confidenciales de retroalimentación y quejas (AAP), con enfoque sensible a edad, género, discapacidad y seguridad. • Facilitar espacios de aprendizaje, revisión de datos, documentación de buenas prácticas, estudios de caso y lecciones aprendidas. Plan International | TdR de consultoría | MERL Plan International | TdR de consultoría | MERL • Fortalecer capacidades MERL de socios, equipos de campo y personas recolectoras de datos mediante acompañamiento, inducciones y herramientas simples. • Emitir recomendaciones técnicas sobre consentimiento informado, salvaguarda, do no harm, protección de datos y uso responsable de la evidencia. • Participar, cuando sea expresamente solicitado y dentro del alcance de la consultoría, en espacios técnicos de coordinación. Dicha participación no confiere facultades de representación legal, laboral, financiera ni contractual de Plan International.

5\. Entregables

- Plan de trabajo y metodología de la consultoría, incluyendo plan MERL nacional inicial, matriz de indicadores, mapeo de necesidades de datos y protocolo de manejo seguro de información.
- Diagnóstico técnico breve del sistema MERL vigente, con brechas priorizadas, plan de calidad de datos y recomendaciones aplicables.
- Paquete de herramientas y tableros de seguimiento (matriz de indicadores, flujos de datos, mecanismos de retroalimentación y quejas/AAP) contextualizados para las líneas de intervención priorizadas.
- Plan y materiales de fortalecimiento de capacidades MERL para socios y equipos de campo, junto con evidencia de las sesiones facilitadas.
- Producto mensual consolidado de asistencia técnica MERL, que incluya: actividades y productos desarrollados durante el mes; estado de indicadores y calidad de datos; hallazgos del mecanismo de retroalimentación/AAP; evaluaciones o estudios en curso; herramientas o notas técnicas elaboradas; sesiones de fortalecimiento de capacidades realizadas; y plan de trabajo actualizado para el mes siguiente.
- Informe final consolidado, presentado como parte del producto mensual correspondiente al último mes de la consultoría, que reúna los productos MERL desarrollados, bases de datos limpias, resultados, brechas pendientes, aprendizajes y recomendaciones.

6\. Modalidad de prestación y coordinación técnica documentación final completa y organizada. La persona consultora prestará los servicios con autonomía técnica, metodológica y organizativa, sin sujeción a jornada laboral ni integración en la estructura jerárquica de Plan International. La contraparte técnica revisará los productos exclusivamente para verificar su conformidad con estos TdR, los criterios de calidad acordados y las políticas aplicables al servicio. Las reuniones de coordinación se acordarán en función de los entregables y no implicarán control de asistencia, horario ni subordinación. La persona consultora organizará los medios y la metodología necesarios para producir los entregables. Cualquier recurso que Plan facilite deberá documentarse y utilizarse exclusivamente para la prestación contratada. La consultoría no otorga autoridad para contratar, comprometer fondos, emitir instrucciones laborales, aprobar gastos ni asumir obligaciones en nombre de Plan International. Cualquier ajuste sustantivo al alcance, los productos o los plazos deberá formalizarse por escrito entre las partes.
- 7. Estándares y referencias técnicas • Política y Estándares Globales de MERL de Plan International. • Guía global del Proceso MERL. • Lineamientos de calidad y manejo seguro de datos. • Política global de salvaguarda. • Política global de igualdad de género e inclusión. • Documentos estratégicos internos de Plan International Venezuela sobre respuesta, recuperación, localización, AAP y MERL.
- 8. Perfil requerido • Título universitario en ciencias sociales, estadísticas, desarrollo, educación, salud pública, gestión humanitaria o campo afín. • Mínimo cinco años de experiencia en MERL/MEAL, preferiblemente en contextos humanitarios o mixtos (humanitario-desarrollo). • Dominio de marcos lógicos, teoría de cambio, indicadores, recolección cuantitativa/cualitativa, análisis y reporte. Plan International | TdR de consultoría | MERL • Experiencia técnica en al menos tres de las siguientes áreas: diseño de sistemas MERL, evaluaciones, gestión de calidad de datos, mecanismos de AAP, fortalecimiento de capacidades o coordinación técnica. • Manejo de Kobo/ODK u otras herramientas digitales de recolección, Power BI, Excel avanzado y visualización de datos. • Experiencia de trabajo con organizaciones no gubernamentales, socios locales, consorcios o mecanismos de coordinación humanitaria. • Conocimiento de protección de la niñez, educación en emergencias, WASH, género e inclusión, AAP y salvaguarda. • Experiencia previa con Plan International, sistemas PMERL o marcos globales humanitarios (deseable). • Inglés funcional para coordinación, revisión de guías globales e informes a donantes (deseable). • Excelente capacidad de análisis, redacción y síntesis de evidencia en español.
- 9. Propuesta técnica y económica • Propuesta técnica que describa la comprensión del servicio, metodología, plan de trabajo y disponibilidad para cumplir los entregables. • Propuesta económica desglosada por producto mensual, indicando el valor de cada cuota mensual e incluyendo honorarios, impuestos y cualquier costo necesario para la prestación del servicio. • Currículum vitae actualizado y referencias profesionales pertinentes. • De ser aplicable, muestras de productos MERL similares desarrollados previamente.
- 10. Honorarios, pagos y gastos Los honorarios se establecerán en el contrato y se pagarán en cuotas mensuales, contra la entrega y aprobación escrita del producto mensual consolidado definido en la sección 5, previa presentación de la documentación fiscal correspondiente. Calendario de pago: se realizará un (1) pago por cada mes de consultoría, una vez aprobado el producto mensual correspondiente. El pago del último mes incluirá la aprobación del informe final consolidado y la entrega organizada de todos los productos y archivos de la consultoría. Cada pago mensual estará condicionado a la conformidad escrita de la contraparte técnica. El valor de cada cuota será el establecido en el contrato y corresponderá al producto mensual aprobado, no a periodos de asistencia, jornadas u horas trabajadas. Los entregables específicos previstos en el cronograma deberán incorporarse como anexos o componentes del producto mensual correspondiente. Los gastos de viaje que sean indispensables deberán contar con autorización previa y escrita de Plan International y se gestionarán conforme a las condiciones establecidas en el contrato. La persona consultora será responsable del cumplimiento de sus obligaciones fiscales, administrativas y de seguridad social como contratista independiente, conforme a la normativa aplicable. Plan International | TdR de consultoría | MERL
- 11. Salvaguarda, conducta y confidencialidad La persona consultora deberá cumplir las políticas y códigos de conducta de Plan International aplicables a terceros, incluyendo salvaguarda, PEAS, prevención del fraude, protección de datos y seguridad de la información. Toda información obtenida durante la consultoría tendrá carácter confidencial y únicamente podrá utilizarse para el cumplimiento de los productos contratados. El acceso a datos de niñas, niños, adolescentes y familias generados por el sistema MERL deberá limitarse a lo estrictamente necesario, aplicando principios de minimización de datos, consentimiento informado, seguridad y acción sin daño. Los productos y bases de datos elaborados deberán entregarse sin datos personales identificables, salvo autorización expresa y existencia de una base legítima para su tratamiento.
- 12. Propiedad de los productos La titularidad, uso y entrega de los productos desarrollados en el marco de esta consultoría (incluyendo herramientas, bases de datos, informes y materiales de capacitación) se regularán en el contrato. La persona consultora deberá declarar cualquier material preexistente o de terceros incorporado y garantizar que cuenta con las autorizaciones necesarias para su utilización.
- 1. Naturaleza de la relación contractual La contratación tendrá naturaleza civil o mercantil, según determine el contrato aplicable, y corresponderá a una prestación independiente orientada a resultados. Estos TdR no crean por sí mismos una relación laboral, cargo, puesto, jornada, exclusividad, línea de reporte, facultad disciplinaria ni derecho a beneficios laborales. La ejecución práctica del servicio deberá ser coherente con esta naturaleza y con el contrato suscrito.
- 14 Criterios indicativos de evaluación de propuestas
\- Experiencia y conocimientos técnicos en MERL: 40%
\- Calidad y pertinencia de la propuesta técnica: 35%
\- Coherencia del plan de trabajo y disponibilidad: 15%
\- Propuesta económica: 10%

jobs.description:
Are you an experienced and qualified Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer? Tearfund Eurasia and North Africa has an exciting opportunity for a professional and qualified MEAL Officer to support our programmes in Iraq. The MEAL Officer will provide technical support in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning across operations in Iraq, specifically coveringErbil and Basra.

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer is responsible for leading and implementing in country project monitoring and data collection as well as technical input and support in managing the MEAL components of the Iraq programme and projects. Working under the guidance of the Programme Quality Director (PQD) and Regional MEAL unit, the position holder will work with regional and project team members to ensure the effectiveness, efficiency, desired outcomes and progress towards impact according to the project design, donor guidelines and law of the land. Travel to and within multiple Governorates in Iraq (KRI and GOI) will be required.

**We are looking for someone who has:**

- A Bachelor's degree in a relevant field.
- At least 3 years of experience in humanitarian and community development projects, specifically within MEAL.
- Proven experience of working in and with small and diverse teams
- Proven experience of field work and community & stakeholder engagement for working in the field of monitoring and evaluation of development projects;
- Proven experience in developing and strengthening MEAL frameworks and accountability systems;
- Strong knowledge and understanding of indicator refinement, tool development and assessment leading;
- Experience of working on institutionally funded projects and proposals and reports (including DG-ECHO, GIZ and FCDO)
- Evidence of facilitating or leading M&E trainings for staff and local partners
- Full proficiency in both English and Arabic (written and spoken).
- Willingness to travel across Iraq (Erbil and Basra/federal Iraq) up to 50% of the time.

**Skills/Abilities required:**

- Strong qualitative and quantitative data analysis, interpretation, and articulation skills.
- Demonstrated capability in proposal writing, reporting, and indicator refinement.
- Excellent organizational skills with the ability to work independently, multitask, and manage enumerators/contractors.
- Strong IT skills and proficiency in data management systems (Google Workspace / data tools).
- Outstanding communication, diplomacy, and cross-cultural interpersonal skills.
- Emotional maturity, adaptability, and the ability to maintain composure under pressure in fast-changing field environments.

If the above describes you then please have a look at the attached and do apply!

This position will be based in Iraq (Erbil or Basra). Please note that we can only accept applications from candidates who have the right to live and work in Iraq. **National candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.**

*Applicants must be in sympathy with Tearfund's beliefs and Values.*

The recruitment process will include specific checks related to safeguarding issues. In addition, personal identification information will be submitted against a Watchlist database to check against criminal convictions as a counter-terror measure.

jobs.title: Pediatrician
jobs.description:
**PAEDIATRICIAN – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

**PURPOSE**

Providing outpatient and/or inpatient paediatric care to patients/beneficiaries according to adapted and updated medical knowledge, MSFprotocols, values and universal hygiene standards to improve the new-born and child/beneficiaries health conditions

**WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PAEDIATRICIAN IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

- Available for deployment within the next 3 months for your first rotation of 12-16 weeks, followed by a mandatory 21-day post-deployment monitoring period.
- French proficiency (at least B2)
- Experienced in Ebola response, VHF, outbreak, or emergency response (strong asset)
- Flexible and adaptable in fast-changing environments
- Resilient under high-pressure humanitarian conditions
- Committed to teamwork and MSF principles
- Ready for remote and resource-limited field settings
- Medical Doctor diploma in a recognized university
- Paediatrics qualification preferred
- 2 years’ experience minimum as a Medical Doctor in paediatric hospital

**Accountabilities**

- Applying medical knowledge and skills to prevention, diagnosis and treatment of children, ensuring integrated new-born and paediatric care through Emergency, OPD, and IPD services in New-borns and cases of malnutrition. Prescribing the necessary treatment, respecting MSF protocols.
- Collaborating closely with the different department of the hospital (e.g. Maternity), Knowing and ensuring all updated MSF medical protocols and universal precautions are followed and implemented, reducing bio-hazard risks and improving infection control.
- As an expert in paediatrics, proposing strategy (modification on current new-born and paediatric care management) and implementing them after validation of Operation and Paediatric Advisor.
- Ensuring on-going new-born and paediatric training (formal and bedside) of the medical/paramedical multidisciplinary team in order to optimize the new-born and paediatric quality of care. Reviewing and discussing selected complicated cases or mistakes and giving technical input.
- Keeping patients and their families informed of the illness and the treatment to follow, checking that they have been understood. Ensuring professional autonomy and confidentiality are respected and a good attitude and proper bedside manner towards the patient and their care takers and the rest of the medical team.
- Following up the evolution of the hospitalized/IDP patients through daily visits, consultations and examinations, prescribing the necessary treatment following MSF protocols, deciding whether they can be discharged or transferred to other departments – in collaboration with other doctors- and informing their family about the patient’s evolution.
- Monitoring the proper functioning of the department, equipment or material and addresses the list of the missing item for new-born and paediatric activities. Providing inputs about general organization of the different paediatric wards, including the admission, transfer and discharge criteria + referral procedure from Maternity and post-delivery wards
- Checking and controlling the rational distribution of medicines and equipment under his/her responsibility and taking care the quality, disinfection and sterilization of the medical material. Assuring general compliance with standing hygiene standards.
- Participating in the introduction / improvement of the collection and analysis of epidemiological new-born and paediatric data, checking its validity and informing the line manager or project coordinator about any problems or complications of the patient’s illness and medical errors. Collecting Clinical cases for further trainings and list a series of comments to improve the current MSF protocols
- Managing the team under his/her direct responsibility according to MSF HR policies and procedures, supervising their performance, organizing and scheduling shifts and rotations, directly participating in emergencies and on calls if necessary.
- Designing and providing training to staff as required.
- Debriefing with coordination, Headquarter (including Paediatric Advisor) and providing written report on main findings, activities, conclusions and further recommendations.

**What MSF Offers:**

- A fixed-term contract for deployment assignments and additional 21 days
- Travel, accommodation, and medical coverage during missions.
- Daily allowances in line with MSF policies.
- Access to training and professional development opportunities.

jobs.title: Consultancy services to facilitate and to prepare the report for the Asia Leadership Team Meeting (ALT) and the Asia Leadership Forum (ALF) - F2F Meet
jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference**

**Consultancy services to facilitate and to prepare the report for the Asia Leadership Team Meeting (ALT) and the Asia Leadership Forum (ALF) - F2F Meeting or “ALT+ALF Meeting”, in Bangkok, Thailand**

***Shaping a stronger Oxfam for people living in poverty***

**DEPARTMENT PURPOSE**

Oxfam is an international confederation of 21 organizations networked together in 87 countries. As part of a global movement for change, we are working together to end world poverty and injustice. We work with thousands of partners in countries around the world and employ staff in a wide variety of posts. We work directly with communities, and we work with the powerful to enable the most marginalized to improve their lives and livelihoods and have a say in decisions that affect them.

The Oxfam in Asia regional platform contributes to and implements Oxfam’s Global Objectives and Strategy and leads the implementation of Oxfam in Asia Strategic Framework, by providing vision and strategic direction to all of Oxfam’s work in Asia. This includes Oxfam’s humanitarian responses and the localisation of humanitarian leadership, long-term development programming and influencing, and public campaigning work. Responsible and accountable for the strategic direction and effective management of the programming in Asia, effective management of financial and human resources in line with Oxfam policy and provide high-level support and representation for advocacy, fundraising and any other representational purposes in support Oxfam’s work and interest while ensuring gender justice and feminist principles are adopted.

**MEETING BACKGROUND AND STRUCTURE**

The Asia Leadership Team Meeting (ALT) and the Asia Regional Leadership Forum (ALF), or the **ALT+ALF Meeting**, will be held from 16-20 November 2026 at Bangkok, Thailand.

The ALT is composed of the Asia Regional Platform Core Group, Asia Country Directors, and Asia National Directors. Meanwhile, the ALF is composed of Oxfam Affiliates (based in Asia and/or working in Asia); Oxfam Asia Regional Director and Representative/s; Oxfam Asia Country and National Directors; and regional NGO partners and organizations. In this regard, the ALT+ALF meeting hopes to build on the learnings from the 2025 ALT+ALF Meeting, and will have the following objectives—

- Update progress and report back on the previous meeting decisions
- Identify priority strategic issues (both programmatic and operational) and agree upon collective solutions.
- Strengthening Asia leadership’s role for strategic decision and coherence
- Share updates on the Revised Oxfam Asia Regional Strategy
- Strengthening impact, expanding our footprint, and diversifying funding

The Asia Regional Director will provide strategic leadership and overall guidance to the meetings. Select members of the ALT and the ALF will create two (2) Steering Committees that will plan the separate ALT and ALF meeting agenda.

The 5-day meeting would be organized in two parts, specifically—

- 2.5 Days for the ALT (Nov. 16 to half-day of Nov. 18)
- 1.5 days for the ALF (Nov. 19 to half-day of Nov. 20)

Half-day sessions on Days 3 and 5 were created to allow time for separate 1-1 sessions, which participants can arrange amongst themselves based on need.

## **Objectives of the meeting:**

The objectives of the meeting are to:

- **Update progress** and report back on the previous meeting decisions
- **Identify priority strategic issues** (both programmatic and operational) and agree upon collective solutions.
- **Strengthen Asia leadership’s role** for strategic decision and coherence
- **Understand digital security** challenges and strategies to tackle those threats.
- **Enhance impact**, expanding our footprint, and diversifying funding

This ALT+ALF meeting is **expected to deliver** the following outputs:

- Agreements on the Asia Leadership Forum Ways of Working and Next Steps
- Oxfam in Asia’s Strategic Priorities: FY 2025-26 Updates
- Separate ALT and ALF Communiques for circulation in the Oxfam Confederation and external audience

**JOB PURPOSE**

The Asia Regional Platform is looking for a consultant/team of consultants to facilitate the ALT and ALF meetings; finalise the meeting documentation reports; and finalize the ALT and ALF communiques. Oxfam will cover travel, accommodation, and meals of the consultant/s during the meetings.

**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

1. Develop the meeting agenda and plan the sessions in collaboration with the ALT and ALF Steering Committees.
2. Work with session leads/facilitators/rapporteurs to identify key learning questions, conduct the sessions, and capture the main findings/lessons.
3. Develop the final meeting reports, including key action points and takeaways
4. Finalize the ALT and ALF communiques in collaboration with respective Steering Committees.

**DELIVERABLES**

1. ALT and ALF Meeting Agenda and session plans
2. Pre-Meeting consultations with the ALT and ALF steering committees and/or participant groups so they are able to understand expectations (anticipating 3 preparation meetings before the event proper on 16-20 November 2026)
3. Facilitation of sessions
4. ALT+ALF meeting documentation reports (with agreed structure, workshop notes and pictures)
5. ALT and ALF Communiques

**TIMELINE**

The consultancy assignment timeframe starts on October 2026 and is expected to conclude by December 2026. The expected total days to complete this assignment is **15 working days**.

**APPLICATION REQUIREMENT**

Applications must include:

- Technical proposal
- Itemised financial proposal.
- CVs of the consultant or proposed team members.
- Relevant sample work
- Contact details for two recent and relevant professional references.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

We are looking for a consultant/team of consultants who can work with the Steering Committees and deliver all the required outputs within the prescribed timeline.

**Essential**

- Technical writing skills to distil content from various sessions. Ability to summarize key points, capture quotes and document main messages delivered.
- Action learning, training and content development, and high-level facilitation skills.
- Must be proficient in English and able to produce qualitative reports from live and recording of online sessions.
- Have good knowledge of Oxfam’s processes, historical context, and regional perspectives.
- Previous experience of producing events/meeting reports, learning brief, and communiques.

**Desirable**

- Experience working with and/or knowledge of Oxfam or similar organizations, universities, other development setups.
- Relevent qualifications in social sciences or a related field
- Excellent computer skills and working knowledge of interactive apps (e.g. Mentimeter, Miroboard, etc.) to consolidate participants’ feedback.

**Other Key Attributes**

- Ability to demonstrate sensitivity to cultural differences and gender issues
- Commitment to Oxfam’s safeguarding policies to ensure all people who come into contact with Oxfam are as safe as possible

This consultancy is open to postgraduates, young professionals, experienced development practitioners, and communication experts. Women are highly encouraged to apply.

1.*Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behavior at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, and adults. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.*

jobs.title: Partnerships Senior Officer - Damascus
jobs.description:
**Job Overview/Summary:**

The Partnerships Officer will support IRC Syria in developing and managing effective, equitable and sustainable partnerships with local and national organizations and other relevant stakeholders. The position will contribute to the effective management of partnership initiatives across the partnership lifecycle, while strengthening partners’ organizational, programmatic and project management capacities.

The role will work closely with the Partnership, Program, Grants, Finance, MEAL and other relevant teams to facilitate effective coordination, partner engagement, capacity strengthening and delivery of agreed partnership and capacity-sharing plans.

The position will also support strategic partnership initiatives and collaborative platforms, including initiatives aimed at strengthening the capacity, leadership and organizational effectiveness of local and women-led organizations. This will include supporting planning, stakeholder engagement, coordination, implementation follow-up, documentation and learning.

The role requires strong project management, stakeholder engagement, communication and coordination skills, alongside an understanding of partnership principles and capacity strengthening approaches.

**Responsibilities:**

Follow IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) that sets out efficient and responsive processes, delineates clear roles and responsibilities, and articulates IRC’s strategic approach to partnerships. Assist the partnership team for quality sub-award management, including sub-award start-up, sub-award implementation monitoring, capacity sharing and appropriate sub-award close-out.

**Project and Partnership Initiative Management**

Support the planning and coordination of partnership, capacity-strengthening and other collaborative initiatives, ensuring activities are aligned with agreed objectives, workplans, timelines and available resources.

- Develop and maintain activity plans, implementation trackers and action plans, ensuring timely follow-up on agreed deliverables and milestones.
- Coordinate inputs from relevant IRC teams, partners and stakeholders to facilitate effective implementation of agreed activities.
- Organize and facilitate meetings, workshops, consultations and other collaborative activities, including preparation of agendas, materials, minutes and follow-up actions.
- Track progress against agreed activities and deliverables, identify implementation challenges and support timely follow-up or escalation through the appropriate channels.
- Support the preparation of progress updates, presentations, learning products and other materials required for internal and external stakeholders.
- Contribute to documenting lessons learned, good practices and recommendations to inform future partnership and capacity-strengthening initiatives.

**Partnership Facilitation:**

- Follow IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS), supporting efficient and responsive partnership processes and clear roles and responsibilities across the partnership lifecycle.
- Assist in identifying, assessing and developing potential partnerships with local and national organizations, in coordination with relevant IRC teams.
- Develop and maintain constructive working relationships with partners, ensuring regular communication, coordination and follow-up.
- Support monitoring of partner performance and, through the Partnership team and relevant technical colleagues, facilitate appropriate technical support and guidance to address partnership-related issues.
- Support stakeholder and partner mapping and analysis to inform partnership engagement and capacity-strengthening approaches.
- Support pre-award due diligence processes for sub-awards, including appropriate vetting, risk analysis and identification of measures to manage identified risks, working with relevant departments as appropriate.
- Support the preparation and processing of sub-award agreements and related documentation in line with IRC procedures and required approvals.
- Support monitoring of partnership activities through partner engagement and field visits, ensuring implementation is aligned with agreed workplans, budgets and partnership agreements.
- Support grant opening meetings and partner briefings, in coordination with Program, Finance, Grants and other relevant functions, to establish clear expectations, roles, responsibilities and compliance requirements at the start of partnerships.
- Support the Partnership team in following up on partnership agreements and completing relevant internal processes, including OTIS.

**Partner Support and Capacity Sharing**

- Support capacity assessments of partners and contribute to the development of practical, jointly agreed capacity-strengthening plans.
- Coordinate with the Partnership team, Capacity Sharing focal point and relevant technical colleagues to facilitate implementation of capacity-strengthening plans.
- Support the organization and delivery of training, workshops, mentoring, coaching and peer-learning activities aimed at strengthening partners’ organizational, programmatic and project management capacities.
- Support partners to strengthen practical systems and processes related to project planning, implementation, coordination, reporting and organizational management, in coordination with relevant IRC teams.
- Monitor progress against agreed capacity-strengthening actions and support partners and IRC colleagues in identifying and addressing implementation challenges.
- Document capacity-strengthening progress, lessons learned and good practices to inform future partnership approaches.
- Provide appropriate support and guidance to partners while maintaining clear roles, responsibilities and mutual accountability between IRC and partnepartners, sharing best practices and ensuring adherence to IRC and donor requirements.

**Documentation and Reporting:**

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date partnership records, including partner communications, agreements, deliverables, action points and relevant documentation throughout the partnership lifecycle.
- Maintain and update relevant partnership trackers, ensuring key milestones, deliverables, payments and other requirements are appropriately recorded and followed up.
- Document meetings and engagements with current and potential partners and relevant stakeholders, and share agreed actions with responsible colleagues.
- Prepare regular updates for the Partnership team on partnership activities, progress, challenges and outstanding actions.
- Support relevant IRC teams in reviewing partner reports and consolidating partner inputs into internal and donor reporting, as required.
- Ensure relevant partnership and capacity-strengthening documentation is appropriately filed and accessible in accordance with IRC procedures.

**Required Experience/qualification/Skills:**

- Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, such as international development, business administration, social sciences, project management or a related discipline.
- 3–5 years of progressively responsible experience in partnership management, project coordination/management, capacity strengthening, stakeholder engagement, grants management or a related field, preferably within the humanitarian, development or civil society sector.
- Strong understanding of stakeholder analysis and partner mapping techniques.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating projects or multi-stakeholder initiatives from planning through implementation, monitoring, follow-up and reporting.
- Experience working with local and/or national organizations, civil society organizations and/or community-based organizations.
- Experience conducting organizational or programmatic capacity assessments and supporting the development and implementation of capacity-strengthening plans.
- Demonstrated experience in stakeholder mapping, engagement and coordination.
- Experience facilitating workshops, consultations, training, mentoring or other collaborative learning activities.
- Strong organizational and project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple activities, deadlines and stakeholders simultaneously.
- Experience working with ECHO, GFFO, BMZ, FCDO or other institutional donor-funded projects is an advantage.
- Excellent communication, facilitation, negotiation and interpersonal skills.
- Proven ability to work effectively with diverse teams, partners and stakeholders.
- Fluency in Arabic and English required.
- ***Female candidates are encouraged to apply***

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values and IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- Credible written, presentation and verbal communication skills
- Validated sense of professional discretion, integrity, and ability to handle complex situations diplomatically and to effective resolution.
- Validated ability to plan long-term, organize priorities and work under administrative and programmatic pressures with detail orientation and professional patience.
- Highly collaborative and resourceful; ability to establish positive working relationships with senior level management and all other partners to maximize cooperation and productivity.
- Curiosity, a desire to continually learn and develop is a must.
- Analytical ability in creating effective solutions to complex matters.

**Language/Travel:**

- Fluency in English and Arabic is required.
- Travel: 50% to field sites

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Partnership Manager
**Position directly supervises: N/A**

**Indirect Reporting (If applicable):** Partnership Coordinator
**Key Internal Contacts: IRC Programs**

**Key External Contacts: Partners**

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based and are currently located outside of your home country and possess over two years of international work experience, the Middle East Region has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

IRC is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

jobs.title: Partnerships Manager-Damascus
jobs.description:
**Background/Context:**

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 350 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery.

Our longstanding experience in the country to date provides a strong foundation for the IRC to further adapt and expand its programming across Syria, in order to respond to the new realities, with a greater focus on resilience and recovery initiatives. Alongside this, the IRC also It plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and actively engaging in advocacy efforts.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The Partnership Manager is responsible for the management and implementation of IRC’s approach to partnering with local and national civil society and other local organizations in Syria. Under the guidance of the Partnerships Lead, Whole of Syria, and in close collaboration with field management teams (FMTs), the Partnership Manager will lead the Hub Partnership Department to ensure strong, collaborative partnerships that deliver effective and efficient program outcomes in accordance with IRC Strategy 100 (S100) and IRC Syria’s Strategic Action Plan.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Follow IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) that sets out efficient and responsive processes, delineates clear roles and responsibilities, and articulates IRC’s strategic approach to partnerships. Ensure quality sub-award management, including sub-award start-up, sub-award implementation monitoring and management, and appropriate sub-award close-out.

**Partnership Management**

- Support Partnerships Lead to establish and maintain the six core building blocks of partnership success – self-assessment, working group, defined and resourced role, training, stakeholder analysis, and collaborative design.
- Contribute to the business development process by supporting proposal development through integrating partnerships inputs
- Actively engage in and help drive IRC partnership initiatives, including participating in the Syria Partnership Working Group and thematic meetings on partnership approaches and practices, identifying opportunities for systems improvements, and coordinating to ensure a coherent, efficient, and effective joint approach to partnerships.
- Oversee all aspects of partnership management in Syria - from identification, development, risk management, project and agreement development, sub-award management, monitoring and accountability, through to closure – ensuring cross-collaboration with the partnerships team and all program, operations, and finance components.
- Facilitate and lead the development of the portfolio structure and approach to individual partner relationships with SYRIA-based team – including the selection of the appropriate funding mechanism and the development of appropriate reporting, monitoring and advance terms - based on the findings of due diligence, donor regulations and in line with IRC policy, appropriately analyzing and mitigating risks, in collaboration with SYRIA FMT and program leads.
- Collaborate with Grants and program leads to ensure that we maximize partner collaboration in program design and development, including with respect to budget allocation, ensuring that we maximize resources for those leading delivery.
- Oversee the systematic partner feedback on IRC’s management of and performance in partnerships in Syria, as well as appropriate action in response to the feedback.
- Oversee the effective partnership project close-out processes, incorporating reflection and lessons learned across Syria.
- Ensure all partners have collaboratively developed project support plans in place where relevant and oversee the delivery of timely and effective support, in close collaboration with the Partnership Lead, FMT, and Syria Capacity sharing focal point.
- Ensure IRC understands the capacity strengthening priorities of its partners in SYRIA, including through Organizational Capacity Assessment processes where appropriate, and identify opportunities for IRC to support partner capacity strengthening efforts where aligned with prime award objectives.
- In collaboration with the Capacity sharing focal point, support IRC’s delivery of organizational capacity strengthening support, appropriately coordinated and integrated with technical capacity strengthening support.

**Pre-award phase:**
- Lead the mapping process for selecting partners, work closely with the program units to identify selection criteria, and make sure selection is transparent and well documented.
- Work with the Partnerships Lead and the Award Management Unit in headquarters to ensure that the appropriate funding mechanism is identified for each sub-award, and that appropriate special conditions are incorporated in each award.
- Liaise with IRC units to collect inputs on partners’ project proposals and work collaboratively with partners to finalize project descriptions, budgets, work plans, and monitoring and evaluation plans.

**Sub-Award Management**

- Ensure that all partners’ program deliverables are received, tracked, filed, and in compliance with donor objectives and requirements, coordinating with program teams and other units within the IRC. Ensure that partners’ contractual reports are reviewed and internal feedback is compiled and sent to partners in a timely manner. Notify the Partnerships Lead, compliance, and finance staff of any issues, and provide timely feedback to partners.
- Serve as a pivot and communication point for coordination of daily inputs of program, operations, and finance support to the partners.
- Ensure that projects are monitored robustly, following up on implementation of partner-specific compliance, programmatic monitoring work plans, procurement plans, budget spending, and more. Notify the Partnership Lead and other relevant staff of any issues, and provide timely feedback to partners.
- Chair case management meetings for sub-awards, address specific issues as they arise, and escalate issues to the Partnership Lead or other relevant forum as required.
- In collaboration with relevant IRC staff, coordinate inputs and review of sub-award progress for donor reporting and grant review meetings to ensure that donor commitments are met.
- Develop and process sub-award amendments in a timely manner, ensuring that the relevant IRC units (in-country and at the HQ) provide their inputs and approve the modification.
- Assist the Deputy Director of Programs or Partnership Lead on preparing management response and plan of actions of Internal and/or External audit and follow up on all sub-award compliance issues and audits, and document resolutions.

**Staff Performance Management, Learning & Development:**

- Hire, supervise, and build the capacity of team members in relevant technical and management competencies.
- Coach, train, supervise, and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting annual performance objectives, providing regular and timely positive and constructive performance feedback, and providing documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Approve and manage time, attendance, and leave requests to ensure adequate departmental coverage; ensure monthly, accurate timesheet submission and carry out probationary reviews.
- Hold high-quality meetings with each direct report on a regular and predictable basis, minimally on a monthly basis.
- Provide a measurable development plan including on-the-job learning with the aim of strengthening technical capacity, exchanging knowledge within the team, and providing guidance on career paths.
- As required, identify staff performance issues and work with Human Resources to document and address these in accordance with the National Staff Employment Policies.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.
- Look for opportunities to support staff in their career growth, where appropriate.
- Adhere to and act in accordance with the IRC Global HR Policies and Procedures and communicate through word and example a high standard of compliance with all applicable policies and regulations.

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience & Education:**

- Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in International Development or Affairs, Finance, Business, or related field, or equivalent years of experience.
- 6 years of work experience in partnership and grants management with INGOs or NGOs in the Middle East Region.
- 2 years of staff management experience
- Proven experience in sub-grants management is required
- Direct experience with GFFO, BMZ USAID, and/or OFDA funding plus FCDO funding, & ECHO experience desired.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values, and IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
- Proven ability to work well in and promote teamwork, thrive in a multi-cultural environment
- Flexibility
- Commitment to team building, mentoring, and staff development
- The position regularly corresponds and attends meetings with external and internal audiences; thus, a strong ability to communicate and maintain positive working relationships is highly desirable for this position

**Language/Travel:**

- Excellent written and spoken English and Arabic are required.
- The position is based in Damascus with a standard office work environment, with around 60% regular travel to field sites.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Partnership Coordinator
**Position directly supervises:** Partnership Officers, Partnerships Assistant

**Indirect Reporting:**
**Key Internal Contacts:** Technical Coordinators, Partnerships Department, Grants team, Finance team, Supply Chain team, M&E team

**Key External Contacts:** Partner staff, occasional coordination meetings with other INGOs; Relevant stakeholders, both INGOs and NGOs.

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

jobs.title: MEAL Enumerator
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
ACTED is committed to immediate humanitarian relief to support those in urgent need and protect people’s dignity, while co-creating longer term opportunities for sustainable growth and fulfilling people’s potential. ACTED endeavours to respond to humanitarian crises and build resilience; promote inclusive and sustainable growth; co-construct effective governance and support the building of civil society worldwide by investing in people and their potential. The commitment of ACTED and that if our teams is guided by 4 core values: (1) Responsibility: we ensure the efficient and responsible delivery of humanitarian aid with the means and the resources that have been entrusted to us. (2) Impact: we are committed to having the most sustainable impact for the communities and the people with whom we engage. (3) Enterprising-spirit: we are enterprising and engage in our work with a spirit that creates value and overcomes challenges. (4) Inspiration: we strive to inspire all those around us through our vision, values, approaches, choices, practice, actions, and advocacy.

**Greening strategy:**

ACTED’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each ACTED employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities:

- Contribute towards the adherence and development of the greening strategy plan.
- Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles
- Encouraging and promoting environmental safeguarding processes and environmental programming standards in accordance with SOPs and technical guideline notes

**Acted PSEAH Policy**

The area MEAL enumerator has the responsibility to adhere to the PSEAH Policy (Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment). The MEAL enumerator has the obligation to complete all mandatory trainings related to the Code of Conduct and the PSEA policy and report any safeguarding concern such as breaches of organisational policies or codes of conduct according to Acted’s procedures. The MEAL enumerator carries out work duties in a way that does not harm children, vulnerable adults or other staff or volunteers.

**Location:** Idleb office

**Start Date:** TBD

**Job Purpose**

The Area MEAL enumerator is responsible for assisting the Area MEAL Officers to implement all MEAL field activities and tasks including assessments, beneficiary verification, data entry, reporting, collection of and ensuring adherence to lessons learned and best practices, and any other tasks as required.

## Objectives

1. Implement MEAL assessments in the field in a reliable, accurate and transparent manner, including collecting primary and secondary data, reporting on findings, and supporting the development of tools and methodologies.
2. Support organizational learning by ensuring adherence to MEAL technical guidelines, lessons learned, and best practices.
3. Ensure lessons learnt and best practices are discoursed and documented by reporting them in a timely manner.
4. Contribute to the effective functioning of beneficiary complaints and response mechanism and enhance the trust and confidence of beneficiaries, identify areas of our work which need to be improved and ensure that Acted learns from the feedback provided through this process.

### **Duties and Responsibilities**

1. **Monitoring and Evaluation Missions**
1. ***1 Field Data Collection***

- Coordinate with the Area MEAL Officer to carry out the assessments (including, but not limited to: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) surveys, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, baseline and endline surveys, as well as other types of assessments and data collection that is required);
- Check that material necessary to carry out the assessment is sufficient and appropriate;
- Write down the observations and answers in an ordinate and clear way, recording responses accurately;
- Record and forward all complaints and suggestions received while in the field to the appropriate Accountability Officer/Accountability assistant.
- Collect evidence where applicable
- Probe to clarify unclear answers;
- Write down the observations and answers in an ordinate and clear way, recording responses accurately

***1.2 Reporting***

- Report monitoring findings and any other findings and observation emerged during data collection activities frequently to the MEAL Officers so to communicate the progress of assessment activities;
- Recognize and give account of problems in obtaining data and provide useful feedback from field research activities;
- In the absence of a dedicated Data Entry Officer, enter all field data into appropriate databases on an accurate and timely basis;
- Cross-check the accuracy of data entry;
- Support the maintenance of an efficient and accurate filing system for all electronic and hard copy documents;
- Report monitoring findings at Daily/Weekly Area Meetings, as required by MEAL Officer;
- Collect high-resolution and good quality photos of Acted project activities in the field, featuring donor, partner and Acted logos, and delivery photos to the MEAL Officer (in line with Acted’s Child Protection Policy and Photo Guidelines).

***1.3 Support the Development of MEAL Tools and Methodologies***

- Support the MEAL Officer in designing appropriate information collection tools and methodologies, including assessment Terms of Reference, and questionnaires;
- Support the translation of tools and methodologies into local language(s) as required.

**2. Support to Organizational Learning**

***2.1 Collection of Lessons Learned and Best Practices***

- Collect lessons learned and best practices from beneficiaries, community leaders, partners, and other stakeholders during assessment/monitoring missions;

***2.2 Monitoring Adherence to Program Strategies and Guidelines***

- Cross-check that project implementation adheres to the technical guidelines for the program, as required by the MEAL Officer;
- Monitor the implementation of lessons learned and best practices;
- Cross-check the accuracy and relevance of beneficiary selection according to contractual criteria.

**3. Other**

- Participate in any meetings or conferences as required by the MEAL Officer;
- Perform any other related activities as assigned by immediate supervisor.

**Key Performance Indicators**

- % of data collection missions conducted that reached sufficient data accuracy (data accuracy criteria as per Acted standards and as assessed by MEAL Officer overseeing the activity)
- % of effective supervision of the data collectors (enumerators) in the field
- Number of lessons learned, and best practices collected over the past 6 months
- Number of photos of Acted projects collected during the past 6 months that meet Acted standards
- \# of data collections conducted
- \# of data collection trainings attended
- \# of effective communications done with programs during the OSM

**Qualifications**

- **Essential qualifications**
- At least one year of experience with NGOs and/or International Institutions in Monitoring and Evaluation
- High school
- Good command of using data collection tools/applications (Kobo, ODK)
- Ability to build and sustain relationships with team members and interviewees in the field as well as the local authorities, i.e., camp managers, etc.
- Flexibility and adaptability are essential, as well as the ability to plan, take initiative, and work under minimal supervision.
- Capability to work under pressure and travel to the targeted areas within Acted projects
- **Preferred qualifications**
- Previous experience within MEAL department
- Institute or College degree Diploma degree
- Basic English skills are an asset
- Good command of MS Excel and MS Word

jobs.title: HEAD OF DEPARTMENT GRANT AND PARTNERSHIP - AFGHANISTAN
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Created in 1979, Action contre la Faim is a non-governmental organization that fights against hunger. Its charter of humanitarian principals- independence, neutrality, non-discrimination, free and direct access to victims, professionalism, transparency - has been part of its identity for 45 years. Its mission is to save lives by eliminating hunger through the prevention, detection and treatment of under-nutrition, particularly during and after emergency situations linked to conflicts or natural disasters. Action contre la Faim focuses its actions on 7 main areas of expertise: Nutrition and Health - Mental Health, Psychosocial Support - Food Security and Livelihoods - Water, Sanitation and Hygiene - Advocacy - Climate - Research. In 2024, Action contre la Faim provided aid to more than 26 million people in 57 countries worldwide. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Deputy Country Director of Programs, your missions will be as follows :
Lead the development and implementation of grants management processes across the entire project cycle, ensuring quality, efficiency, and compliance.
Lead and coordinate high-quality proposal development with program and operations teams and support the funding strategy.
Lead all internal and external reporting processes
Manage the grants team and build the capacity of own team and all relevant staff involved in grant management
Engage with donors and maintain strong, long-term relationships
Provide strategic oversight of partnership and localisation activities
Demonstrate personal commitment in promoting Gender Equality and ACF Gender Minimum Standards

Profile :

You hold a University degree in a related field such as fundraising, public relations, communications, development, humanitarian aid, or international relations.
You have significant experience working with INGOs, and at least 5 years' experience in humanitarian and/or development fundraising from institutional donors in a fundraising or related NGO role.
You have technical skills in drafting and compiling project proposals, budget monitoring and grant management, as well as narrative and financial reporting for a variety of donors Considering your strong knowledge of donor guidelines and regulations. You are also able to establish and formalise partnerships, work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
Your flexibility and managerial skills enable you to lead, develop, support and motivate the grant team effectively but also to strengthen the skills of own team, other departments, and partners.
You have proven strong organisational skills, ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously, anticipate priorities and your are able to work autonomously with minimal guidance.
You are fluent in English, with excellent report writing in English, interpersonal and communication skills to foster collaboration and maintain positive relationships.

jobs.title: Gerente de Programas
jobs.description:
El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. DRC ha estado presente en Colombia desde 2011, pero 2018 amplía sus operaciones en respuesta a la crisis venezolana. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados. Actualmente incorpora actividades en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, Nariño y Norte de Santander.

**Descripción general del cargo:**
El/la Gerente de Programa es responsable de supervisar la implementación y calidad del programa multisectorial (Protección y Recuperación Económica) de respuesta de DRC a nivel de base, en el marco del programa, asegurando la entrega oportuna y efectiva de asistencia humanitaria y servicios de protección, en línea con los procedimientos de DRC, los estándares humanitarios y los requerimientos del donante.
Bajo la dirección del Área Manager y con orientación de las Gerencias Técnicas de la oficina de país, el/la Gerente de Programa liderará la implementación del programa mediante la supervisión directa del equipo programático de DRC, la coordinación con el área de soporte de la base de La Guajira. Deberá garantizar que las actividades a cargo de DRC, en el marco del programa, se ejecuten de manera eficiente, dentro de los tiempos establecidos y conforme a las prioridades operacionales.

**Responsabilidades:**
**Gestión de la implementación y calidad del programa**

- Liderar la implementación del programa a nivel de la base, asegurando que todas las actividades se ejecuten conforme a los planes de trabajo, presupuesto y metas definidas para el programa.
- Con el apoyo de las Gerencias Técnicas de la oficina de país, asegurar la entrega oportuna y de calidad de asistencia multisectorial, garantizando la adecuada articulación entre los componentes de Protección y Recuperación Económica.
- Dar seguimiento regular al avance de la implementación con el equipo de programas de la base, identificando, alertando y gestionando oportunamente retrasos o desviaciones al plan de trabajo.
- En coordinación con las Gerencias Técnicas de la oficina de país, asegurar la correcta aplicación de los lineamientos técnicos sectoriales, SOPs, guías operativas y herramientas programáticas, asegurando calidad y cumplimiento en todas las fases de la implementación.
- Asegurar el correcto seguimiento y actualización de las herramientas del PCM a nivel de la base, incluyendo desarrollo y actualización de planes de trabajo y plan de compras.
- Verificar la calidad técnica de las actividades implementadas en terreno del equipo de DRC, mediante acompañamientos periódicos a las actividades de Protección y de Recuperación Económica, revisión de los procesos de entrega de asistencia humanitaria, y del registro y validación de beneficiarios.
- Apoyar y realizar análisis continuo del contexto operativo y necesidades de la población objetivo en la zona de intervención, contribuyendo a la adaptación de la implementación en función de cambios en acceso, seguridad o dinámicas territoriales, en articulación con aliados locales y actores de la cooperación.
- Asegurar que la implementación del programa se realice conforme a los principios humanitarios y estándares de calidad, incorporando el enfoque de edad, género y diversidad.

**Monitoreo, Evaluación y Reporte**

- Asegurar el seguimiento regular al avance del programa a nivel de base, verificando el cumplimiento de metas e indicadores correspondientes.
- Garantizar la correcta implementación del flujo de información del programa, asegurando que todos los procesos y pasos definidos de las herramientas de recolección de datos sean cumplidos de manera completa y oportuna por el equipo de DRC en la base.
- Con el apoyo del Gerente MERA-UGI y su equipo, supervisar la calidad, consistencia y veracidad de la información registrada en sistema de información del programa, minimizando errores mediante la capacitación periódica del equipo a su cargo en la utilización de sistema de información, y de la validación y seguimiento a inconsistencia y errores que se presenten, asegurando la resolución a tiempo de estos errores para generar reportes de calidad y oportunos de la implementación del programa.
- Hacer seguimiento del sistema de gestión de la información de protección HumaniQ del programa, asegurando y/o reportando inconsistencias en relación con la información allí reflejada, de modo que sea actualizada y coherente.
- Asegurar la consolidación y entrega oportuna de reportes programáticos respecto a la implementación del programa, garantizando en ellos precisión y coherencia de la información.
- Garantiza su participación eficiente, en los tiempos establecidos, en la redacción del informe trimestral del Monitoreo de Protección.

**Gestión de equipos y personas**

- Gestionar las partidas presupuestarias de las actividades del programa, garantizando un uso eficaz y eficiente de los recursos, incluidos los financieros, los humanos y todos los activos.

**Requisitos en términos de Formación Académica y conocimientos técnicos:**

**Ofrecemos:**

jobs.title: Conductor
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
Acted es una ONG internacional sin ánimo de lucro con sede en París, Francia con operaciones en más de 40 países a nivel mundial. La misión de Acted es aportar asistencia humanitaria inmediata a aquellos que se encuentren en situación de necesidad al mismo tiempo que genera oportunidades a largo plazo para un crecimiento durable. Acted opera en contextos de catástrofe natural, conflicto armado y crisis socioeconómica.

Acted se encuentra en la búsqueda de un Conductor para integrarse a nuestro equipo en la misión de Venezuela.

El/la Conductor, brindará apoyo operativo directo en la ejecución de las actividades en terreno para la respuesta de emergencia post terremoto 24-06-2026 concentrando las acciones en la zona impactada de Morón, estado Carabobo. Sus responsabilidades principales se centrarán en ejecutar funciones de conducción de manera segura, eficiente y responsable, garantizando el cumplimiento de las normas de tránsito y los protocolos de seguridad establecidos por la organización. Asegurar el mantenimiento adecuado del vehículo, la correcta movilización del personal y el apoyo logístico necesario para el desarrollo de las actividades operativas, contribuyendo al buen funcionamiento de las misiones y al cumplimiento de los objetivos institucionales.

**Funciones**

- Observar las regulaciones del tránsito mientras esté desempeñando sus funciones de conductor, cuidando por la seguridad del personal que transporta.
- Conocer con exactitud las normas de seguridad de Acted, velar que el vehículo cumpla con los requisitos mínimos de seguridad en el país en cuanto a kit de primeros auxilios, extintor de incendios y kit de bioseguridad, entre otros; así como poseer los conocimientos básicos en la utilización de estos.
- Conocer de la agenda de actividades de misión y cualquier otro personal fuera de la oficina.
- Responsabilizarse por el mantenimiento del vehículo y reportar a la Administración el estado de este y su cronograma de mantenimiento; inspeccionar y mantener el nivel adecuado de todos los fluidos del vehículo (aceite, batería, combustible, etc.) así como revisar constantemente la presión de los neumáticos y reportar cualquier anomalía inmediatamente.
- Mantener diariamente actualizado el registro de kilometraje y llevar el registro de consumo de combustible.
- Velar y mantener diariamente limpio el vehículo a su cargo tanto por fuera como por dentro.
- Apoyar en trabajos de mensajería de reportes de movilización del personal en terreno.
- Realizar otras tareas inherentes a su cargo a solicitud del coordinador estatal.
- Mantener al día los documentos propios de identificación y el permiso de conducción nacional.
- Mantenerse apto física y mentalmente para conducir el vehículo, y no deberán haber consumido bebidas alcohólicas, otras sustancias que causen embriaguez o medicinas que afecten al sistema nervioso inmediatamente antes de conducir o durante la conducción.
- Someterse a los reconocimientos médicos periódicos necesarios para determinar su estado general de salud y en particular su visión.
- No permitir a personas ajenas a las actividades oficiales viajar en vehículo de la organización, los cuales son para uso del personal de la organización y de contraparte que participa en las actividades de la oficina a la que se ha asignado el vehículo.
- Respetar estrictamente y en todo momento los límites de velocidad y las normas de seguridad en carretera locales, tener en cuenta las condiciones locales concretas como la superficie de la carretera, el estado del tiempo, el tráfico, los peatones y animales, etc, y viajar a una velocidad acorde con la máxima seguridad.
- Informar al encargado de la Oficina de cualquier accidente en que intervenga un vehículo de la organización.
- Cumplir con las medidas que pueden adoptarse para prevenir accidentes y lesiones, en particular el uso obligatorio de cinturones de seguridad para quienes viajan en el vehículo.
- El conductor deberá obligatoriamente mantener al día la bitácora (track) o registro de movilización del vehículo que conduzca. En las anotaciones deberá incluirse información sobre los viajes realizados, el objeto y distancias de los mismos, el consumo de gasolina, aceite y otros lubricantes, y las revisiones y reparaciones. Las anotaciones deberán ser comprobadas, completadas en caso necesario y refrendadas por el personal al que se haya asignado la responsabilidad directa diaria de cada vehículo.
- Brindar apoyo al oficial logístico en diversas tareas como gestión de inventarios, coordinación de transportes, manejo del almacén, control de alimentos excedentes y otras actividades relacionadas al departamento de logística.

**Perfil deseado**

**Requisitos**

Obligatorios:

- Formación media y diversificada en cualquier área (requisito mínimo).
- Experiencia de al menos 3 años como conductor corporativo.
(Preferiblemente haber trabajado en organizaciones de cooperación internacional).
- Licencia como mínimo de 3ra.
- Certificado de Manipulación de Alimentos.
- Manejo básico-intermedio de herramientas digitales (Paquete Office y plataformas de recolección de datos móviles).
- Con buena dicción y presencia, con competencias para buen trato al usuario y relaciones interpersonales.

**Competencias:**

- Excelentes habilidades interpersonales y de resolución de problemas, habilidades diplomáticas, flexibilidad y proactividad.
- Transparencia y rendición de cuentas.
- Habilidades de planificación y gestión del tiempo.
- Sólida capacidad de comunicación escrita y oral.

**Condiciones**

- Contrato de prestación de servicios bajo la figura de honorarios profesionales durante 3 meses con posibilidad de renovación según disponibilidad presupuestaria y desempeño.
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina de Acted en Carabobo.
- Honorarios profesionales según la escala de la organización.
- Prestación de Servicios de forma presencia y traslados frecuentes a zonas afectadas por el doblete sísmico.
Moron – Carabobo.
