jobs.title: حلب /مدير مشروع الإسكان
jobs.description:
## هدف الوظيفة

يحدد هذا الوصف مسؤولية مدير المشروع عن إدارة دورة المشروع كاملة، وتحقيق النتائج ضمن النطاق والميزانية والجدول المعتمد، مع ضمان جودة البناء وسلامة الأسر ووضوح حقوق الإشغال.

يقود مدير المشروع فريق التنفيذ وينسق مع الوزارة والسلطات ومقدمي الخدمات والأقسام المساندة في وطن لضمان تسليم مساكن آمنة وقابلة للإشغال

. ويتابع إحالة الأسر إلى خدمات التعليم والصحة والحماية وسبل العيش؛ وتبقى المساعدات التكميلية مرتبطة بالتزامات الشركاء وتوافر التمويل

## المهام والمسؤوليات

## إدارة المشروع والتخطيط

- إعداد خطة تنفيذ تفصيلية تربط المخرجات والأنشطة والجدول والموازنة والمسؤوليات؛ وتحديث الخطط الشهرية والأسبوعية ومتابعة المسار الحرج
- قيادة مراحل تأكيد المواقع والاتفاقيات، التصميم والاعتماد، المشتريات والتحقق من الأسر، البناء والخدمات، التسليم، والمتابعة وإصلاح العيوب
- إدارة نطاق المشروع والتغييرات وتأخر الأنشطة؛ واقتراح إجراءات تصحيحية ورفع التغييرات التي تتطلب موافقات إدارية أو موافقة المانح قبل تنفيذها
- توزيع مهام الفريق وتحديد أهداف الأداء والإشراف على الموظفين وتقييمهم، وتنظيم اجتماعات تقدم منتظمة مع المهندسين والمقاولين والأقسام المساندة

## تأكيد المواقع والتنسيق الحكومي
- •متابعة توثيق تخصيص الأرض وصلاحية استخدامها والاتفاقيات اللازمة مع الوزارة والجهات المختصة قبل بدء الإنشاء
- قيادة تقييم المواقع بالتعاون مع المختصين، بما يشمل السلامة وظروف التربة والمخاطر وإمكانات الربط بالخدمات والوصول الميسر إلى المدارس والصحة والأسواق والنقل.
- تنسيق إعداد واعتماد التصاميم والمواصفات وجداول الكميات والتراخيص مع مهندسي الوزارة وفريق وطن، وفق المتطلبات الفنية السورية المعتمدة

• استكمال مراجعة ترتيبات الإشغال مع الجهات المختصة والمشورة القانونية؛ وتوثيق الحقوق والمدة والتكاليف والمسؤوليات وآلية تسوية النزاعات قبل انتقال الأسر

## إدارة الإنشاء والجودة والسلامة

• اعتماد خطة متابعة الجودة ضمن الصلاحيات ومتابعة تطبيقها بواسطة المهندسين المؤهلين، بما يشمل فحص المواد والاختبارات ونقاط قبول الأعمال قبل إخفائها

• متابعة أداء المقاولين ونسب الإنجاز مقارنة بالعقود والخطة، والتحقق من معالجة الأعمال غير المطابقة وحفظ سجلات الفحوصات والزيارات وقرارات التصحيح

• ضمان تطبيق اشتراطات السلامة المهنية وحماية الأسر والمجتمعات المحيطة، ورفع الحوادث فوراً حسب الإجراءات؛ وتعليق الأعمال المتأثرة عند وجود خطر وشيك بالتنسيق مع الجهات المسؤولة

• عند الاشتباه بمخلفات متفجرة، إيقاف الأعمال في المنطقة المتأثرة وإحالة الأمر إلى الجهات المؤهلة؛ وعدم استئنافها قبل تأكيد السلامة

• متابعة اكتمال وربط واختبار المياه والصرف الصحي والكهرباء والتصريف والوصول الآمن؛ وعدم التوصية بإشغال أي وحدة قبل إثبات جاهزيتها ومعالجة العيوب الأساسية

## إدارة الميزانية والمشتريات والعقود

• إدارة الموازنة بالتنسيق مع المالية، ومراجعة المصروفات والالتزامات والتوقعات والتدفقات النقدية شهرياً، وتفسير الانحرافات واقتراح التصحيح

• إعداد خطة مشتريات مرتبطة بالجدول، وتنسيق الوثائق الفنية والطلبات والتقييم الفني مع الهندسة والمشتريات، وفق المنافسة والشفافية وسياسات وطن ومتطلبات المانح.

• متابعة تنفيذ العقود والتأخيرات والضمانات والاحتجازات والأوامر التغييرية، ضمن الصلاحيات والإجراءات المعتمدة

• مراجعة طلبات الدفع على أساس كميات وأعمال تحقّق منها المهندسون والوثائق التعاقدية؛ ورفعها للاعتماد المالي دون تجاوز الفصل بين الطلب والتحقق والاعتماد والصرف

## المهام والمسؤوليات متابعة

## اختيار الأسر والحماية والمساءلة

• تنسيق خطة التحقق من السجلات الحكومية مع فريق MEAL، وضمان تحقق مستقل من 100% من الأسر المقترحة قبل اعتماد قائمة المستفيدين وفق آلية الموافقة المعتمدة.

• توفير الموارد والوقت اللازمين لمعالجة التناقضات والتحقق من الأهلية ومنع الازدواجية؛ وصون استقلال نتائج MEAL وعدم تجاوزها أو تعديلها دون أدلة وإجراءات موثقة.

• الحفاظ على سرية الاختيار وعدم إجراء إعلان عام أو فتح باب تقديم خلال التحقق والاختيار، مع إبلاغ الأسر فردياً بأن التقييم لا يمثل وعداً بالمساعدة.

• ضمان الموافقة المستنيرة على جمع البيانات والمشاركة والانتقال، وشرح الموقع والخدمات وحقوق الإشغال والتكاليف المتوقعة بلغة مفهومة.

• ضمان قنوات شكاوى آمنة وسرية وميسرة، ومتابعة الشكاوى المتعلقة بالمشروع مع MEAL؛ وإحالة قضايا الحماية وحماية الطفل ومنع الاستغلال والانتهاك الجنسي وفق مسارات وطن المختصة.

• حماية بيانات الأسر وقصر الوصول عليها على المخولين؛ وعدم استخدام صور الأطفال أو بيانات الأسر في التقارير أو التواصل دون الموافقات والإجراءات اللازمة

## الشراكات والتقارير وإدارة المخاطر

• إدارة التنسيق التشغيلي مع HCI والوزارة والسلطات ومقدمي الخدمات، وتمثيل المشروع ضمن التفويض، وحفظ محاضر الاجتماعات والقرارات والالتزامات.

• تحديث سجل المخاطر والإجراءات والمسؤوليات؛ ومتابعة مخاطر الأرض والإشغال والتراخيص والتضخم والطقس وأداء المقاولين وتأخر الخدمات والتوترات المجتمعية.

• إعداد تقارير داخلية شهرية وتقارير المانح وفق الاتفاقية، تشمل الإنجاز الفعلي والمالي والجودة والأسر والمخاطر والإجراءات التصحيحية، بالتنسيق مع المالية وMEAL.

• تنسيق الإحالات والاتفاقات مع شركاء التعليم والصحة والحماية وسبل العيش، وتوثيق الالتزامات المؤكدة؛ وعدم تقديم وعود بمساعدات غير ممولة أو إدخال نشاط إضافي دون الاعتماد اللازم

## التسليم والمتابعة وإغلاق المشروع

• تنسيق فحص جميع الوحدات والخدمات، وقوائم العيوب ومعالجتها، ومحاضر الاستلام ووثائق الإشغال والتسليم الطوعي للأسر.

• الاتفاق على إدارة وصيانة المساحات والخدمات المشتركة وتكاليفها مع الجهات المعنية والسكان، وتوفير إرشادات الاستخدام الآمن والإبلاغ عن الأعطال.

• تنفيذ متابعة ما بعد الإشغال مع MEAL والهندسة، بما يشمل استمرار الإقامة والوصول إلى الخدمات والرضا والشكاوى وإصلاح العيوب خلال المدة التعاقدية.

• استكمال ملفات المشروع الفنية والمالية والتعاقدية ووثائق التنفيذ النهائي والاختبارات والضمانات، وإعداد التقرير الختامي والدروس المستفادة وخطة تسليم أي التزامات متبقية

## حدود الصلاحيات والمساءلة

يدير شاغل الوظيفة التنفيذ اليومي ويوجه الفريق ويتابع المقاولين ضمن التفويض المعتمد. تبقى المصادقة الفنية والتوقيع على الأعمال من اختصاص المهندسين المخولين، وتبقى الموافقات المالية والتعاقدية والاختيار النهائي للأسر وفق مصفوفة صلاحيات وطن. لا يلتزم المدير بتغيير جوهري في النطاق أو الموازنة أو المدة، أو بحقوق إشغال، أو بتمويل إضافي دون الموافقات المختصة. تُرفع العوائق والقرارات التي تتجاوز صلاحياته إلى مدير المشاريع في الوقت المناسب

## المخرجات المتوقعة ومعايير الأداء

• خطة بدء وتنفيذ متكاملة وجدول وموازنة وخطة مشتريات ومصفوفة مسؤوليات وسجل مخاطر، خلال الشهر الأول من المباشرة وتُحدّث دورياً

• ملف جاهزية لكل موقع قبل الإنشاء يتضمن تخصيص الأرض والاتفاقيات والتقييمات والتصاميم والكميات والتراخيص ومسؤوليات الخدمات

• تقارير تقدم شهرية موثقة تربط الإنجاز المادي بالمصروفات والالتزامات، مع متابعة الانحرافات والإجراءات التصحيحية؛ وتقارير مانح في مواعيدها

• قائمة 100 أسرة معتمدة بعد تحقق MEAL المستقل من جميع الأسر المقترحة، وحل التناقضات وتوثيق موافقتها المستنيرة وسرية بياناتها

• تسليم 100 وحدة ضمن النطاق والميزانية والجدول المعتمدين، مع سجلات فحص لكل وحدة، وخدمات أساسية عاملة وحقوق إشغال موثقة قبل الانتقال

• ملف تسليم وإغلاق يتضمن محاضر الاستلام، والاختبارات، والضمانات، وخطة الصيانة والمتابعة وسجل العيوب ومعالجتها والتقرير النهائي

## المؤهلات والخبرة المطلوبة

• بكالوريوس في الهندسة المدنية أو العمارة؛ وتُعد الدراسات العليا ذات الصلة أو شهادات إدارة المشاريع ميزة إضافية

• خبرة عملية لا تقل عن 7 سنوات في مشاريع الإنشاء أو الإسكان أو المأوى، منها 3 سنوات على الأقل في إدارة مشاريع تشمل فرقاً وميزانيات ومقاولين

• خبرة مثبتة في إدارة دورة مشروع ممول من مانح، والتخطيط والموازنة والمشتريات والعقود والتقارير؛ وخبرة البناء الدائم وربط البنية التحتية مطلوبة

• القدرة على مراجعة التصاميم والمواصفات وجداول الكميات وبرامج التنفيذ والمستخلصات، وإدارة الجودة والسلامة بالتعاون مع المختصين

• معرفة بالسياق السوري والعمل مع السلطات ومقدمي الخدمات والمجتمعات النازحة؛ وفهم مسائل حقوق الإشغال والحماية والمساءلة وحماية البيانات

• إتقان العربية، ومستوى مهني في الإنجليزية يسمح بإعداد التقارير والتواصل مع الشركاء.

• إجادة Excel وWord وبرامج الجدولة مثل MS Project أو ما يعادلها، والقدرة على قراءة المخططات واستخدام أدوات متابعة الإنشاء؛ ويُفضل الإلمام بـ AutoCAD.

• القدرة على السفر المنتظم إلى مواقع المشروع ادلب والعمل ميدانياً وفق ترتيبات الأمن والسلامة

## المهارات والالتزامات المهنية

قيادة الفرق والتفاوض وحل المشكلات واتخاذ القرارات المبنية على الأدلة، وتنظيم الأولويات والتواصل مع الأطراف المختلفة، والنزاهة وإدارة تضارب المصالح. يلتزم شاغل الوظيفة بمدونة السلوك وسياسات وطن وإجراءاتها، والمبادئ الإنسانية وعدم التمييز، وحماية الطفل ومنع الاستغلال والانتهاك الجنسي ومكافحة الاحتيال، والإبلاغ عن المخالفات عبر القنوات المعتمدة.

jobs.title: International call for MEAL consultancy - Outcome Harvesting Evaluation
jobs.description:
NOTE: only organisations registered outside of Denmark are eligible for this consultancy opportunity.

**Opportunity:** ActionAid Denmark (AADK) is seeking a consultant, or team of consultants, to complete an Outcome Harvesting Evaluation. This is a MEAL consultancy to support AADK to assess the impact of its programming and partnership with local organisations.

**About SPAII:** Since January 2022, AADK has implemented the Strategic Partnership Agreement II (SPAII) in partnership with 17 ActionAid countries as well as with partners at the international level. AADK made a significant change in programming strategy from SPAI to SPAII to align with the overall AADK strategy as well as the AA strategy, and the overall objective of the SPAII programme is ‘*Societies are transformed to become more just, feminist, green, and resilient.’* The thematic priorities are expressed through the following three strategic objectives:

- *Strategic Objective 1: Democracy Deliver* – young people, especially young women and those facing marginalisation or fragility, enjoy their rights to an open and enabling democratic space and access to well-resourced programmes and public services.
- *Strategic Objective 2: Resilient livelihoods and just transition* – young people, especially young women and those facing marginalisation or fragility, enjoy a just transition and their right to climate resilient livelihoods.
- *Strategic Objective 3: Youth Leadership in Crises* – young people, especially young women and those facing marginalisation, are resilient to shocks and enjoy their right to protection in fragile contexts, disasters, and protracted crises.

**Objectives of the Outcome Harvesting Evaluation:**

1. To provide AADK with a robust evaluation and verification of the breath of impact and outcomes, as ascertained from harvested outcomes and complementary desk research.
2. To provide data, evidence and impact pathways for a set number of in-depth, substantiated and verified harvested outcomes.
3. To provide a set number of case studies, derived from harvested outcomes, for external communication.
4. Identification of opportunities and strategic lessons for future outcome harvesting, outcomes and impact learning.

These objectives will support AADK in demonstrating accountability to right-holders, partners, donors, and other stakeholders in terms of evidence of results achievement as well as to contribute to evidence-based decision-making, fundraising, and support learning processes internally and with partners.

Based on the objectives above, the scope of this evaluation is a comprehensive review of outcomes harvested throughout the duration of SPAII and complementary desk research of SPAII evidences, case studies, etc. This should be completed for all outcomes harvested across the three strategic objectives, as well as cross-cutting outcomes.

The evaluation should draw lessons relating to the effectiveness, relevance, scalability and impact of the harvested outcomes. Attention should be given to principles of participation and inclusion, equality and non-discrimination, feminist leadership principles, feminist research principles as well as accountability and reciprocity as addressed in the programme interventions. Findings should be structured to inform the SPAII Final Narrative report and communicate both programme achievements and strategic learning.

**Evaluation Team:**

- Experience of outcome harvesting.
- Experience of feminist leadership processes, intersectional feminist analysis and understanding of decolonial and anti-racist approaches to evaluation.
- Proven experience in leading exercises similar in scope to the present task.
- Extensive experience in evaluations, reviews, and assessments or other formative exercises particularly for large-scale complex programmes, with evidence of understanding of global standards, theories, models, and methods related to assessing results achievements, effectiveness, and value-add of different actors.
- Experience of online group facilitation
- Experience and ability to communicate complex projects to a range of audiences.
- Experience with results assessing of human rights-based, policy-influencing and advocacy interventions and the work of NGOs, CSOs and social movements to influence change at various levels.
- Specific thematic experience in youth-led change, climate justice, humanitarian response and/or gender responsive public services.
- Ability to conduct participatory and inclusive collaborative processes across different organisations and countries – including the ability to engage with, listen to and learn from a broad range of stakeholders.
- Experience from working in context covered by the SPAII programme.
- Strong communication skills, both in writing and orally in English, and ability to produce high-quality products underpinned by rigorous critical analysis of collected data and assembled evidence. French and Arabic is an advantage.

This is a global competition open to bidders from all geographic areas except for Denmark, and following the technical review, the financial proposal will be reviewed for the best overall comparative value. The evaluation is expected to take place from October to December 2026.

jobs.title: Consultant.e Expert.e en Architecture et IA Générative – Projet HAVA
jobs.description:
**Titre : Consultant.e Expert.e en Architecture et IA Générative – Projet HAVA**
**Date : 11/09/2029**
**Projet :**
**Référence : ​HULO-TDR-BAR-2026-001​**

Cet appel à candidatures est ouvert à tous les consultants éligibles, en accord avec les procédures et principes de hulo.

**Contexte de la consultance :**

La **Coopérative hulo**, créée en juin 2021, est la première Société Coopérative Européenne (SCE) opérant dans le secteur de l’humanitaire. En décembre 2025, hulo compte 16 organisations membres : ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, la Croix-Rouge française (CRF), Fleet Forum, Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross, International Rescue Committee (IRC), INTERSOS, Médecins du Monde (MDM), Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Solidarités International (SI), et Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Son objectif est d'accroître l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant les liens et la solidarité entre les acteurs de la logistique humanitaire et en améliorant les performances grâce à la mise en commun des ressources et de l'expertise en matière de logistique et de chaîne d'approvisionnement. Les « initiatives mutualisées » de hulo, sont déjà en cours dans 7 countries (Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, RDC, Liban, Jordanie pour la crise syrienne, Colombie, et Tchad). Les activités sur le terrain sont composées d'achats mutualisés, de ressources humaines partagées, d’une plateforme web permettant la mise en commun de ressources, et d’initiatives environnementales mutualisées. Ces initiatives permettent d'économiser du temps et de l'argent, d'améliorer la qualité des biens et des services fournis, et donc de fournir une aide plus efficace à ceux qui en ont le plus besoin.

Hulo développe actuellement son écosystème Data autour de Microsoft Fabric, avec l'objectif de renforcer ses capacités en matière de Data Science, Business Analytics et Business Intelligence.
L'utilisation des outils d'Intelligence Artificielle Générative (GenAI) se développant rapidement en interne, cela crée de nouvelles opportunités pour les équipes de hulo, mais également des risques, notamment concernant le shadow AI.
Hulo souhaite donc étudier et préparer la mise en place de HAVA (Hulo AI for Value-added Assistance), un assistant d'IA générative d'entreprise, sécurisé et gouverné.
Le concept actuellement réfléchi repose sur une approche Hybrid Enterprise AI Assistant, combinant des modèles d'IA générative opensource et les documents et mécanismes de sécurité contrôlés par hulo.
L'architecture envisagée s'appuie notamment sur :

- Azure OpenAI Service
- Microsoft Fabric
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Microsoft Entra ID
- Microsoft Purview
- Microsoft Defender
- les bases de données et modèles analytiques de hulo

Le concept HAVA et ses annexes constituent le premier kit de travail qui servira de base à la présente consultance.

**Perimètre général du travail attendu du.de la Consultant.e :**

L'objectif principal de cette consultance est d'accompagner hulo dans la revue, la validation et la finalisation du cahier des charges fonctionnel et technique du projet HAVA.
Le.la consultant.e apportera une expertise indépendante en matière de :

- Generative AI
- Large Language Models (LLM)
- Architecture Cloud
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Sécurité des données
- Gouvernance de l'IA
- Microsoft Azure et Microsoft Fabric

Le.la consultant.e n'aura pas pour objectif de développer l'intégralité de HAVA pendant cette mission.

La mission devra permettre à hulo de disposer, à l'issue de 20 jours estimés (A confirmer dans la proposition), d'un cahier des charges suffisamment complet et robuste pour permettre la mise en œuvre ultérieure de HAVA, en interne et/ou avec l'appui d'un prestataire externe.

Cette mission de consultant sera mise en oeuvre en coordination avec le département Business Analytics & Research (BAR). Une personne ressource sera désignée par département pour identifier les enjeux et faciliter les échanges.

**Priorités et livrables :**

**Cahier des charges HAVA finalisé** **incluant** :

1\. Analyse de situation -

- Contexte et enjeux
- Besoins identifiés et priorisés par service
- Contraintes techniques et d’intégration
- Analyse de l'architecture existante, points forts, limites et recommandations
- Données disponibles et leur qualité
- Exigences éthiques, réglementaires et de gouvernance
- Budget, planning et modalités de collaboration

2\. Solution recommandée

- Périmètre -
- Objectifs
- Périmètre fonctionnel
- Proposition -
- Recommandation sur les modèles IA (Comparaison et recommandation des modèles et stratégie de modèles)
- Connexions / liens avec d’autres usages IA internes (ex. Usages spécialisés de certains départements)
- Modèle de coûts et ressources (Coûts d'implémentation, coûts récurrents et ressources nécessaires)
- Registre des risques (Risques techniques, sécurité, données, opérationnels et adoption)
- Spécifications sécurité et gouvernance (Identité, accès, confidentialité, RAG sécurisé, logs, gouvernance et guardrails)
- Architecture RAG (Ingestion documentaire, métadonnées, recherches web, embeddings)

3\. Préparation de la mise en oeuvre

- Déploiement - Livrables, calendrier et responsabilités
- Critères de réussites
- Maintenance, support et réévaluation après déploiement

**Qualifications et expérience:**

- Minimum 3 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la Data, de l'IA ou de l'architecture Cloud ;
- Expérience démontrée dans la conception de solutions Enterprise Generative AI ;
- Solide connaissance des LLM et architectures RAG ;
- Expérience de l'écosystème Microsoft Azure ;
- Bonne connaissance de la sécurité des données ;
- Expérience en gouvernance de l'IA ;
- Expérience dans la conception de solutions utilisant des documents internes ;
- Capacité à transformer des besoins métier en spécifications techniques ;
- Expérience avec des environnements humanitaire contenant des données sensibles ou confidentielles.

**Management et lignes hiérarchiques**

Ce · tte consultant·e sera placé·e sous la responsabilité du directeur du département « Business Analytics & Research » et travaillera de concert avec un Data Scientist.

**Calendrier**

Mi-octobre – décembre 2026

jobs.title: Técnico/a Sanitario/a. Campamentos Saharauis
jobs.description:
## Misión

El puesto tiene por objeto apoyar en el diseño, desarrollo y supervisión de las acciones en apoyo a los programas de salud sexual y reproductiva (PNSR) y salud infantil (PISIS) de los proyectos que la organización desarrolla en los Campamentos de personas Refugiadas Saharauis enTindouf.

## Ámbito geográfico deIntervención

Campamentos de Población Refugiada Saharaui, Tindouf, Argelia.

## Organigrama

Trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica de la Coordinación Sanitaria y trabajará junto con todo el equipo de Médicos del Mundo en terreno para el logro de los objetivos.

## Responsabilidades

1. En coordinación con la Coordinación Sanitaria, realizar evaluaciones de necesidades en salud en las áreas de intervención para los proyectos en curso o posibles nuevas intervenciones y contribuir a la formulación de proyectos.
- En coordinación con responsables del Ministerio de Salud Pública Saharaui (MSP), identificar las necesidades de productos farmacéuticos (medicamentos, material consumible y equipos médicos durables) para los programas PNSR PISIS.
- Apoyar técnicamente en los procesos de formulación con enfoque de marco lógico relacionados con Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR) / Salud Infantil (SI) de los proyectos de MdM en los CRS, asegurando la transversalización de los enfoques de género y antropológico
2. Promover, planificar y ejecutar actividades sanitarias y de fortalecimiento de los servicios públicos de salud:
- Acompañar a los equipos del PNSR(coordinaciones nacionales, coordinaciones regionales, secretaría) de acuerdo con un ciclo de mejora continua (planificar, implementar, verificar, actuar)
- Proporcionar apoyo técnico al personal de salud adherido al PNSR y PISIS de los tres niveles asistenciales: Hospital nacional, hospitales regionales y dispensarios.
- Liderar la realización de estudios de corte de los programas PNSR y PISIS. Acompañar la recogida de datos del Sistema de Información Sanitaria. En colaboración con la Coordinación Sanitaria contribuir al análisis de indicadores de salud y a la propuesta de proponer soluciones de mejora al MSP.
- Apoyar en la actualización, implementación y seguimiento de protocolos y procedimientos estándar del PNSR y PISIS para garantizar intervenciones de calidad. Monitorizar su implementación y acompañar a las responsables del MSP para fomentar su cumplimiento en los diferentes niveles asistenciales.
- Verificar técnicamente dosieres de compras de medicamentos, equipos médicos y material consumible.
- Promover el adecuado funcionamiento de herramientas de seguimiento y coordinación del MSP como la Plataforma del PNSR-PISIS, las reuniones de coordinaciones mensuales y con el resto de los programas prioritarios. Promover y acompañar la celebración del Comité de muerte materna. Participar en la organización de la Asamblea Anual de la Mesa de Concertación y Coordinación en salud y contribuir a la preparación de información para donantes.
- Contribuir a la transversalización de género en salud, de acuerdo con el Plan de Género y Salud del MSP, las políticas de MDM y la orientación de la Coordinación de Género y Derechos humanos.
- Apoyar técnicamente en el ciclo de gestión del voluntariado sanitario y pasantías en terreno.
- Contribuir activamente en la respuesta humanitaria en caso de emergencias y catástrofes.
3. Acompañamiento y monitoreo del componente sanitario de los proyectos en curso considerando la lógica de intervención de los proyectos, así como su coherencia y complementariedad con otras acciones, productos y actividades
- Dar seguimiento a las actividades sanitarias de los proyectos activos de la organización y en concreto en lo referido a laSSR ySI, incluyendo la malnutrición materno-infantil.
- Recoger y sistematizar los datos e indicadores de salud / sanitarios del sistema de monitoreo de MDM, en concreto en lo referido a la SSR,SI y malnutrición materno-infantil y los programas PNSR y PISIS. Participar en el análisis de indicadores junto a la Coordinación Sanitaria.
- Asegurar la disponibilidad de fuentes de verificación en especial en relación con SSR y SI. Contribuir a la justificación de los proyectos.
4. Apoyar en el ciclo de capacitación y formación del personal sanitario:

- Apoyar al MSP en la detección de necesidades de capacitación y formación del personal de salud, en relación con SSR/SI y Derechos sexuales y reproductivos (DDSSRR).
- Dar apoyo técnico y promover la realización de formaciones periódicas al personal de salud adherido al PNSR y PISIS.
- Apoyar en las evaluaciones de estudiantes de matrona y enfermería de la Escuela de Enfermería, y en su caso, en la revisión de programas y contenidos.
- Acompañar en el desarrollo de habilidades/sensibilización de temas relevantes respecto a la SSR y Salud Infantil. Fomentar la sensibilización e integración del enfoque de género en salud.

1. Contribuir activamente a la sistematización y adopción de buenas prácticas en MDM:

- Contribuir a la articulación y coordinación con el resto de las áreas, y en concreto con logística, administración, género y derechos humanos, farmacia e incidencia política, participando activamente en las reuniones de equipo
- Contribuir activamente a la transversalización de los enfoques de género, antropológico y medioambiental en las intervenciones de MDM.
- Contribuir al seguimiento de la estrategia de la misión y la coherencia entre los diferentes proyectos en marcha desde las diferentes áreas sanitarias.
- Participar en espacios técnico-sanitarios de discusión y coordinación regulares y transmitir a la Coordinación Sanitaria elementos que requieran atención y contribuir al análisis de alternativas.
- Apoyar en la implementación y seguimiento de los protocolos y procedimientos de seguridad y salud para el personal contratado y voluntario de MDM.
- Contribuir a la actualización de la Estrategia País.

Otras tareas que le puedan ser requeridas por la Coordinación Sanitaria en el ámbito de sus responsabilidades y funciones.

## Formación

### Titulación Académica:

Requerida: Enfermero/a especialista en Obstetricia y Ginecología/Matrona.

### Formación Adicional:

Altamente deseable: Formación complementaria vinculada al ejercicio de su profesión, género y antropología de la salud. Máster/Postgrado en Cooperación Internacional/ Acción Humanitaria/ Salud pública.

## Requisitos

**Idiomas**: Imprescindible excelente nivel de castellano Altamente deseable: inglés, francés y/o árabe

**Informática**: Imprescindible nivel usuario de Word, Excel, internet y correo electrónico. Deseable nivel medio de Excel.

## Experiencia

Imprescindible experiencia en terreno en cooperación internacional en las funciones mencionadas.

Deseable experiencia en contextos similares y contextos críticos de seguridad.

## Competencias

- Excelente capacidad de organización y planificación
- Capacidad de trabajo en equipo y en red
- Flexibilidad
- Capacidad de trabajo en condiciones difíciles
- Elevada capacidad de comunicación escrita y hablada
- Conciencia cultural y adaptabilidad. Facilidad para las relaciones interpersonales
- Cumplimiento estricto de los protocolos de seguridad establecidos para el país y la misión de MdM
- Identificación con principios y valores de Médicos del Mundo

## Retribución/Condiciones

Tablas salariales de Médicos del Mundo. Contrato Indefinido.

Jornada laboral: 40 horas.

Categoría: Grupo 1. Personalsanitario

Las personas interesadas pueden enviar el CV a través de nuestra página web:

**Nota:**

Médicos del Mundo promueve la igualdad de oportunidades de todas las personas y establece medidas de acción positiva para quienes por razón de diversidad funcional o de exclusión social y/o cultural pertenecen a grupos infrarrepresentados en los puestos que se ofertan. Por lo que ninguna candidatura con perfil válido será rechazada por su diversidad funcional o por estar cultural o socialmente excluida por razón de nacimiento, etnia, raza, sexo, género o cualquier otra condición o circunstancia personal, social o cultural.

jobs.title: Humanitarian Response Consultant
jobs.description:
**This assignment is only open to candidates already based in Venezuela and able to commence by 19 October 2026 at the latest (earlier is preferred).**

**Position Title:** Humanitarian Response Consultant

**Type of contract:** Consultancy contract

**Duty Station:** Caracas, Venezuela, with occasional travel within the country

**Duration:** As soon as possible, 2 months (100%)

**Reports to:** Desk Officer, Solidar Suisse Headquarters, Zurich, Switzerland

**BACKGROUND INFORMATION**

Solidar Suisse is a Swiss non-governmental organisation founded in 1936 (formerly Swiss Labour Assistance), committed to promoting social justice, decent work, and equal opportunities worldwide. Today, Solidar Suisse implements humanitarian and development programmes in 16 countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America, and Europe.

In Venezuela, Solidar Suisse has initiated a humanitarian response following the earthquake on 24 June 2026. Through a strong partnership-based approach, Solidar Suisse seeks to support the most vulnerable populations affected by the disaster through emergency relief, recovery, and rehabilitation interventions. The organisation is committed to localisation and works closely with national and local actors to ensure sustainable, context-appropriate, and effective humanitarian assistance.

**PURPOSE OF THE CONSULTANCY**

The consultant will support Solidar Suisse in the further development of its humanitarian engagement in Venezuela. The assignment will focus on the identification and assessment of suitable implementing partners, stakeholder engagement and coordination, project design and development, as well as the analysis of operational opportunities, risks and requirements for effective project implementation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Partner Identification and Assessment**

- Identify and assess potential national and local partner organisations.
- Conduct partner capacity assessments and due diligence processes in accordance with Solidar Suisse requirements.
- Analyse potential partners’ technical, operational, financial and organisational capacities, including relevant safeguarding and compliance capacities.
- Prepare a comparative assessment and provide a clear, evidence-based recommendation regarding partner selection and appropriate implementation modalities.
- Support initial discussions with the selected partner on roles, responsibilities, ways of working and implementation arrangements.

**Project Design and Development**

- Analyse humanitarian needs, response gaps and relevant intervention opportunities.
- Lead a participatory project design process in close collaboration with the selected partner and Solidar Suisse Headquarters.
- Develop the project concept, intervention strategy, implementation approach, results framework, indicators and workplan.
- Develop the complete project proposal, logframe, budget and required supporting documents in the applicable donor format.
- Ensure alignment with donor requirements, humanitarian standards, accountability commitments, safeguarding requirements and Solidar Suisse’s localisation approach.
- Integrate comments from Solidar Suisse and the selected partner and finalise the proposal package.

## **Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination**

- Establish and maintain relationships with relevant humanitarian actors, authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, civil society organisations and community stakeholders.
- Participate in relevant coordination mechanisms and information-sharing platforms.
- Represent Solidar Suisse in relevant meetings and consultations during the assignment.
- Strengthen Solidar Suisse’s understanding of the humanitarian context, coordination landscape and key actors relevant to the planned intervention.

## **Operational Analysis and Set-up**

- Analyse the operational environment, including access constraints, security considerations and contextual and implementation risks.
- Assess the operational requirements and feasible implementation arrangements for the planned project.
- Identify relevant risks and proportionate mitigation measures for project implementation.
- Support the establishment of appropriate coordination, security, presence and operational arrangements required for the implementation of the planned project.
- Clarify relevant operational roles and responsibilities between Solidar Suisse and the selected partner.

## **Coordination and Reporting**

- Maintain regular coordination with the Desk Officer at Solidar Suisse Headquarters and provide concise updates on progress, key findings, risks and decisions required.
- Promptly flag material concerns related to partner suitability, feasibility, compliance, safeguarding, security or project quality.
- Submit all final deliverables and supporting documentation in an organised and accessible format.

**Other Duties**

- Undertake other duties reasonably required to support the successful implementation of Solidar Suisse's humanitarian programme in Venezuela.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

**Education**

- Advanced university degree in environmental engineering, civil engineering, water resources management, psychology, social work, humanitarian action, international development, social sciences, or another relevant field.

**Professional Experience**

- Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian and/or development programming.
- Demonstrated experience in partnership management and localisation approaches.
- Demonstrated experience in conducting organisational capacity assessments and due diligence of partner organisations.
- Demonstrated experience in humanitarian needs assessments, project design and programme development.
- Extensive experience in developing high-quality humanitarian project proposals, budgets and logframes for institutional donors.
- Experience participating in humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
- Demonstrated technical experience in WASH and/or Protection programming.
- Experience providing technical support, quality assurance and capacity strengthening to partners.
- Previous experience in emergency response and start-up programmes is a strong asset.
- Extensive recent professional experience in Venezuela and a strong understanding of the humanitarian, political and operational context are required.

**Skills and Competencies**

- Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills.
- Excellent networking, negotiation, and representation skills.
- Demonstrated ability to work independently in complex and evolving environments.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- Strong commitment to humanitarian principles and localisation.

**Languages**

- Professional fluency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken.

jobs.title: Deputy Development Manager
jobs.company: The Center for People and Forests (RECOFTC)
jobs.description:
**Deadline for application:** 14 October 2026, with applications after this date reviewed until the role is filled

RECOFTC is an international nonprofit organization working towards a future where resilient communities with respected rights thrive in forest landscapes that they manage sustainably and equitably. We take a long-term, landscape-based, and inclusive approach in supporting local communities to secure their land and resource rights, stop deforestation, find alternative livelihoods and foster gender equality.

We have almost 40 years of experience working with people and forests and have built trusting relationships with partners at all levels. As a trusted, honest broker, we occupy a distinct position as an international organization that supports, informs, and brings together governments, communities, businesses, academia, and civil society organizations. Our innovations, knowledge and initiatives enable countries to foster good forest governance, mitigate and adapt to climate change and achieve the UN Global Goals.

We operate in the Asia-Pacific region, with country offices in Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand and Viet Nam.

RECOFTC is seeking a Deputy Development Manager to join the Resource Mobilization team at the Regional Support Office in Bangkok. Part of the Executive Office unit, the Resource Mobilization team secures and diversifies funding to support RECOFTC's strategic growth. It identifies and assesses funding opportunities, coordinates bids, tenders, proposals and budgets, and manages donor and opportunity pipelines. The team supports country offices and regional initiatives in pursuing new funding and cultivate relationships with existing and prospective donors, clients and partners. It also helps develop innovative and fundable approaches, and explores emerging sustainable and blended finance opportunities that can expand RECOFTC's work beyond conventional grant funding.

The selected candidate will be offered a 12-month contract with the possibility of extension, contingent on funding availability and satisfactory performance. The Deputy Development Manager reports to the Business Development Manager.

**Tasks and duties**

Our five-year Strategic Phase (2023–2028) is well underway. We are working to expand and diversify our funding and donor base while beginning to plan for the next phase. This position will play an integral role in strengthening resource mobilization now and in shaping our approach for the future.

The successful candidate will develop strategies and concepts, build relationships and manage a pipeline of partner and project opportunities, turning promising ideas into fundable initiatives that are locally led, tested and evidence-based.

The Deputy Development Manager works collaboratively across the organization, providing business development support where needed, as well as working on early solicitation, business intelligence, and marketing and communication products for business development.

Specific tasks and duties include:

- Develop pitches, bids, tenders and proposals: Prepare proposals, pitches and concept notes, with a strong focus on developing budgets and cost proposals, drawing on technical and institutional inputs from the Regional Support Office and country offices
- Coordinate submissions and compliance: Coordinate proposal development across offices, tracking progress in the CRM. This includes applying agreed go/no-go criteria, coordinating workplans, reviewing checkpoints and completing compliance checks to ensure timely, high-quality submissions that meet client, donor and tender requirements
- Support project design and innovation: Collaborate with technical teams, country offices and partners to design and test fundable approaches in service delivery, community enterprise, partnerships, financing and technology. Integrate budgets, theories of change, and lessons from pilots to support adaptation and scaling
- Develop sustainable and blended finance opportunities: Collaborate with colleagues to assess, design and structure financing strategies that use catalytic capital to increase commercial investments. Engage specialist partners where detailed financial assessment or structuring is required
- Research and assess funding opportunities: Monitor donor and industry priorities and opportunities across public, private, philanthropic and sustainable finance sources. Assess eligibility, strategic fit and RECOFTC's competitive position to support funding diversification
- Build donor, client and partner relationships: Cultivate new relationships with donors, development finance institutions, investors, businesses and other partners, coordinating engagement and identifying collaboration opportunities and appropriate roles for RECOFTC
- Support pipelines, targets and reporting: Collaborate on maintaining country and regional business development pipelines. Track funding sources and expected co-financing, contribute to quarterly reporting, and support RECOFTC in meeting financial targets
- Strengthen systems and information management: Collaborate on improving business development processes, standard operating procedures, templates and quality checks. Capture lessons from bids and innovation pilots and maintain organized, accessible files and records
- Provide team guidance and support: Mentor the Resource Mobilization team and undertake other tasks assigned by the Business Development Manager

**Qualifications and experience**

The Deputy Development Manager will have the following qualifications and experience:

**Essential**

- Bachelor's degree in finance, environmental studies, international development, business or a related field. Master's degree preferred
- At least eight years of professional experience in business development, fundraising, international development or a related field, including at least one year of experience working with sustainable finance, blended finance, nature and climate finance or other innovative financing approaches
- Demonstrated ability and success in fundraising, pitching and writing funding proposals
- Demonstrated ability in developing cost proposals or proposal budgets; budget management skills preferred
- Demonstrated professional experience working in the region

**Desirable**

- Preferably a national of an Asia-Pacific country
- Experience developing or designing climate finance or nature-based solution projects
- Experience designing and testing innovations in international development, including participatory problem definition, co-design, piloting, learning, and adaptation
- Working knowledge of sustainable finance and blended finance
- Good understanding of the environment and natural resource management sector, especially forestry, climate change, agriculture, governance, livelihoods, gender and social inclusion, and community tenure and resource rights
- Familiarity with family foundations and private sector actors
- Knowledge of an Asian language
- Knowledge of donors, funding trends and key actors in international development, preferably in the Asia-Pacific context
- Demonstrated management experience

**RECOFTC’s core values**

At RECOFTC, our core values are the foundation of our culture and guide all our work. In addition to job-specific skills and experience, the applicant should possess the following characteristics, attitudes and skills:

- Embrace innovation
- Adapt to and learn from challenges
- Nurture commitment, responsibility and ownership
- Collaborate with partners and stakeholders
- Commit to sustainability
- Cultivate participation, gender equality and social inclusion
- Prioritize well-being

**Commitment to RECOFTC policies and procedures**

- At RECOFTC, we uphold the highest standards of integrity, transparency and responsibility in all our operations. Our policies and guidelines are designed to ensure a safe, inclusive, sustainable and ethical environment for our staff, partners, consultants and the communities we serve.
- All consultants, staff and contractors engaged by RECOFTC are required to comply with RECOFTC’s policies and procedures while performing their roles with RECOFTC.

jobs.title: Fertilizer Procurement Strategy Associate
jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

Seeking a procurement professional to lead fertilizer procurement, ensuring cost-efficient sourcing and reliable on-time delivery. Drive strong individual execution and contribute to team success. In this role, your focus will be dedicated to deep-dive data analysis to determine optimal purchasing windows, and managing and executing the entire procurement process independently.

## **Responsibilities**

Execute Procurement with Excellence

- Strategy & Delivery: Support the creation and execution of seasonal procurement strategies to deliver +90% OTIF (On-Time, In-Full) delivery, market-competitive costs, and 5% year-on-year cost savings.
- Quality Assurance: Ensure absolute quality control, achieving 0 quality issues reaching the farmer, and maintain an +80% on-time payment rate for suppliers.
- Supply Chain Reliability: Proactively address future supply gaps by evaluating farmer needs against global market trends, supplier capacity, and current inventory levels.
- Process Optimization: Drive lead-time improvements through streamlined delivery and process automation. Regularly improve key operations like the goods receipt process and loading quality control.
- Data & Analytics: Spend time developing, maintaining, and continuously improving complex Google Sheets data models to track global market trends and landed costs. Use this data to provide crucial decision support on when to purchase (or not purchase) fertilizers to maximize cost savings.

Build Partnerships & Market Liaisons

- Strategic Relationships: Help build and maintain deep partnerships with fertilizer suppliers and industry organizations beyond seasonal procurement needs.
- Country Team Collaboration: Act as a critical business partner for our country operations teams, actively identifying and sharing opportunities to improve our offering to farmers.
- Industry Representation: Serve as a representative for One Acre Fund externally with suppliers and market actors to drive long-term, systematic supply chain improvements.

People Management

- People Management: Manage and mentor a small team, setting clear goals, providing timely feedback, and conducting high-quality career coaching and performance reviews.
- Team Growth:Contribute to staffing, recruitment, and succession planning to build a high-performing procurement unit.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Professional & Technical Competencies:

- Supply Chain Expertise: Solid foundational knowledge of global procurement processes, international shipping, and supply chain operations.
- Data Fluency: An advanced analytical mindset with high proficiency in Google Sheets to build pricing, forecasting, and decision-support models. Comfortable spending half of your time analyzing data to help make decisions.
- Language: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Management & Execution Skills:

- Relationship Builder: Exceptional collaboration and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence both internal stakeholders and external global suppliers.
- Project Management: Strong organizational skills with a proven track record of managing multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
- Solution-Oriented: An innovative thinker who approaches obstacles with a results-driven mindset and is comfortable making data-driven decisions under medium-risk conditions.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

16 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: FIELD COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Italian Teacher
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background**

In response to the increased refugee arrivals into Europe, the IRC established the program initially in Greece, which was expanded with programs in Serbia and wider Balkans and with programs in Germany. Following a first assessment conducted in January 2017 in Italy and another one in July 2017, several critical protection gaps were identified within assistance provided to refugees and migrants in Italy: mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), assistance to unaccompanied children, information provision and legal support. To respond to the identified gaps IRC established a small presence in Italy. The IRC in Italy provides essential safety, empowerment, education, livelihood and health services to migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. Our programs operate across the country, including in Trieste, Milan, Rome, Turin and various locations in Sicily and Calabria, with a strong focus on supporting the most vulnerable populations, such as women and children.

**Context of the Assignment**

IRC, in partnership with Ente Nazionale Acli Istruzione Professionale (E.N.A.I.P.) Piemonte, Ente Nazionale Acli Istruzione Professionale (E.N.A.I.P.) Friuli Venezia Giulia, Powercoders, Progetto Tenda, is implementing the **Digital Horizons projec**t in Turin and Trieste, since February 2025.
Digital Horizons helps young refugees and migrants in Italy accessing sustainable employment through free software development training, job support, individual guidance and social support. The project focuses on youth aged 16–25, arrived in Italy in recent years, who are seeking to break down integration barriers, improve mental health and build pathways to long-term work opportunities.

By working with public job centers (PES), vocational training providers (VET), IT companies and employers, the project prepares participants for high-demand digital careers and supports them with mental health services, individual job counselling and psychosocial support, job placement, a safe and quiet space to study, access to social services, language training, and childcare.

Simultaneously, it also builds the capacity of institutions and employers to create more inclusive opportunities for the target population.

The Digital Horizons intensive (5hs day, monday-friday) training in software development has been delivered in Trieste since mid October 2025, by IRC partner ENAIP FVG. To support the group of participants with heterogeneous knowledge of Italian language, IRC is seeking a teacher for **italian classes (A2-B1-B2),** includingspecific IT **vocational language,** to support students learning outcomes, before the start of the IT training.

**Purpose of the Assignment**

**Job Overview**

The Digital Horizons Italian Teacher will be based in Trieste and will design and deliver middle advanced (A2-B1-B2 as needed) Italian language classes and IT vocational language, to a group of Digital Horizons students, in person. Under the Economic Wellbeing Manager’s supervision and in collaboration with the IRC Italy Integration Counselor and ENAIP FVG staff, the Italian teacher will conduct classroom teaching activities in Trieste, ensuring no student is left behind.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

**Specific Duties and Responsibilities:**

- **Plan, design, and deliver lessons** in Italian at A2-B1–B2 level, integrating IT-related terminology and vocational language relevant to software development.
- **Develop tailored teaching materials** that combine general Italian language learning with specialized IT vocabulary and contexts.
- **Address student questions** and provide clarification on both general and IT-specific language content.
- **Help develop students’ confidence and learning skills**, encouraging students to use Italian effectively in technical and professional settings.
- **Identify learning gaps** and adapt teaching strategies to meet diverse linguistic needs within the group.
- **Promote intercultural communication** by clarifying information and bridging cultural differences that may affect learning.
- **Manage classroom dynamics** and handle any critical issues that arise during sessions, ensuring a supportive learning environment.
- **Encourage collaborative learning** through peer-to-peer support and group exercises for language practice with IT-related content.
- **Maintain accurate records** of attendance, progress, and outcomes to support monitoring and reporting requirements.
- Collaborate with the IT trainer, other ENAIP vocational training staff and IRC Integration Counselor to achieve the course objectives.

The **Digital Horizons Italian teacher** will deliver updates to IRC Staff, on the classroom learning process and possible challenges identified.

**Deliverables**

- Italian classes sessions conducted (40 hs)
- Attendance Sheets signed

**Timeframe**
The assignment will end upon completion of above-listed deliverables and in any case no later than on 16th November 2026. Classes schedule will be decided in agreement with IRC and ENAIP staff and will be held in the morning (Monday to Friday, between 9.00 and 13.00 am)

**Competencies and skills**

- Proven experience developing learning content and delivering Italian language group teaching activities
- Experience working with migrant population and/or youth is highly desirable.
- Experience or knowledge of IT Sector is an asset
- Bachelor's degree in language or social sciences
- Proven experience in multicultural work or educational environments
- Knowledge of strength-based education and participatory learning
- Understanding of fundamental educational and psychological principles related to learning and communication
- Strong organizational and planning skills.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- Problem-solving abilities
- Personal qualities: empathy and patience, works well in and promotes teamwork, comfortable in a multi-cultural environment, flexible, communicates clearly.
- Additional knowledge of English, Arabic, Spanish, French, Ukrainian, Urdu, Pashtu, Farsi are an asset

**Application Process and Requirements:**

**Application Documentation:**

CV in English OR Italian

**Agreement and payment terms**

The specific details of the agreement, including the scope of work, timelines, deliverables, intellectual property rights, and any other pertinent provisions, will be negotiated and outlined in the contractual agreement to ensure clarity, transparency, and mutual understanding between IRC and the consultant/group of consultants.

**Compensation:** (Total of 1200 EUR). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Country Director
jobs.description:
**The Organisation**

Plan International is a rights-based development and humanitarian organisation working for better lives for all children. We are independent of government and have no political or religious affiliation.

Our purpose is to strive for a just world that advances children’s rights and equality for girls.

We have been building powerful partnerships for children for more than 80 years, and are now active in more than 70 countries.

Our global strategy has a specific focus on girls, as they are often the most marginalised and most often left behind. We have committed ourselves to the ambitious target of reaching 100 million girls over 5 years, to ensure they can learn, lead, decide and thrive. This is our contribution to reaching the sustainable development goals, and in particular the goals on gender equality.

Our organisation is transforming itself to meet this enormous challenge everywhere we work.

We need bold, forward-thinking and innovative individuals to lead our country operations, driving change and delivering results that will allow us to reach our target of 100 million girls.

**The Opportunity**

Plan International is seeking an experienced, values-driven and strategic leader to serve as Country Director for Cambodia. This is a pivotal leadership role, responsible for setting the overall direction of Plan International’s work in Cambodia and ensuring strong programme delivery, influencing impact and sustainable organisational performance.

As Country Director, you will lead a team of about 80 staff and oversee a country programme with an annual budget of approximately USD 8 million. You will represent Plan International at senior levels with government, donors, civil society, media and partners, while ensuring the organisation delivers relevant, gender-transformative impact for the most vulnerable children, particularly girls.

This role requires a leader who is comfortable driving transformative change, strengthening organisational culture and accountability, and ensuring that Plan International Cambodia remains a credible, influential and effective development and humanitarian actor.

**In this pivotal role, you will:**

- Provide strategic and operational leadership for Plan International’s development, humanitarian and influencing work in Cambodia, aligned with the global strategy and the organisation’s commitment to gender equality and girls’ rights.
- Lead the development and implementation of an ambitious Country Strategy grounded in gender transformation, child rights and participation.
- Ensure programme and influencing work achieves impact at scale by linking grassroots action with national-level influencing and advocacy.
- Drive effective emergency preparedness, risk reduction and resilience building, and ensure readiness to respond to both predictable and sudden-onset emergencies.
- Strengthen resource mobilisation across institutional, multilateral, corporate and National Office funding sources, ensuring long-term sustainability.
- Lead and develop a high-performing, inclusive and values-driven team, embedding Plan International’s standards on safeguarding, gender equality, accountability and ethical practice.
- Ensure strong financial stewardship, legal and donor compliance, and effective planning, budgeting, reporting and performance management systems.
- Act as Plan International’s senior in-country representative, building trusted relationships with government, donors, media, INGOs, national NGOs, communities and other stakeholders.
- Contribute as an active member of the Regional Leadership Team, supporting regional collaboration, organisational learning and shared services.

**Do you have what it takes?**

*To excel in this role, you will need among other things:*

- Proven senior leadership experience with increasing responsibility in an international development environment.
- A strong understanding of child rights, gender in development and girls’ rights, and the ability to translate these commitments into impactful programmes and influencing strategies.
- Experience in sustainable community development and participatory approaches in development interventions.
- Knowledge of donor compliance requirements and sound financial management.
- Experience of programming in challenging environments, with a strong understanding of the political, social, economic, humanitarian and security context in Cambodia or a comparable environment.
- Demonstrated ability to lead and motivate diverse teams, manage organisational change, and build an efficient and motivated workforce.
- Strong political acumen, networking and negotiation skills, with experience engaging governmental and non-governmental actors.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Khmer, with strong diplomatic and media-facing communication skills.
- A relevant university degree in development, social science, business administration or a related field.

*For a detailed job description which includes the full list of accountabilities and requirements,* [*please go to this link*](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/lk4xz4pp1lld9eelcm2zm/Cambodia-CD-JD-March-2026-final.pdf?rlkey=ap8qwup484gvhvn7h05y4d5nz&st=xfavun0d&dl=0)

jobs.title: Director of Pacific Programmes, Pacific Region
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Director of Pacific Programmes

**Location:** Melbourne or Port Moresby, with frequent travel

**Contract:** Permanent

**Reporting to:** South East Asia and the Pacific Department Director

**Responsible for:** Directing Conciliation Resources’ programmes in the Republic of Fiji, the Solomons Islands and Papua New Guinea

**Salary:** $127,488 AUD (Exclusive of Superannuation)

**Deadline:** 17:00 Friday, 6th Nov 2026.

## Conciliation Resources

Conciliation Resources is an independent international organisation working with people in conflict to prevent violence, resolve conflicts and promote peaceful societies. We believe that building sustainable peace takes time. We provide practical support to help people affected by violent conflict achieve lasting peace. We draw on our shared experiences to improve peacebuilding policies and practice worldwide. We have worked in the South East Asia and the Pacific (SEAP) regions since 1994 and currently work in: the Republic of Fiji, the Solomon Islands, Papua New Guinea and the Philippines.

Our work seeks to contribute to building more peaceful societies through enhanced analysis and comparative knowledge and through supporting and implementing targeted and adaptive peacebuilding and mediation support programmes. We seek to contribute to change through long-term partnerships; and enhance context-specific peacebuilding and mediation practice through comparative learning.

Within the Pacific region Conciliation Resources supports community led peacebuilding initiatives, working with numerous civil society partners, including in Fiji, Solomon Islands and PNG Highlands and Bougainville, PNG. The programme also supports processes of political dialogue and mediation. Conflict challenges the programme is currently working on include: dealing with past legacies of conflict; the intersection between governance and peace; masculinity, youth and violence; and climate change and conflict.

## Job Purpose

The Director of Pacific Programmes leads Conciliation Resources’ peacebuilding and mediation support work in the Pacific region. They are responsible for developing and managing multiple peacebuilding and mediation support teams - the PNG team, with programmes in Bougainville and the PNG Highlands; The Fiji and Solomon Islands team, including developing programmes related to climate change and conflict. This position will provide strategic leadership and operational management to the whole Pacific team, with direct line management of Project Managers.

The postholder is responsible for setting and overseeing programme budgets, and for ensuring the integrity and credibility of Conciliation Resources’ reputation in the Pacific region. They lead the team’s efforts in developing new programmes, and working to secure new funding for our work. The Director of Pacific Programmes is also a member of Conciliation Resources’ Senior Leadership Team, working with Conciliation Resources’ senior leaders around the world.

## Person specification

### Essential knowledge, skills and experience

● Significant (min 6-8 years) project management experience, designing and implementing conflict resolution and peacebuilding interventions, including programme design, budget development, programme implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

● Practical and conceptual knowledge of peacebuilding and conflict transformation processes, of processes of social and political change and of supporting the development of local capacities for peacebuilding.

● Significant (min 4 years) senior team management experience, including line managing project / programme managers and their teams, and overseeing team performance management and professional development.

● Experience of working with local and national partners in an accompaniment role, including capacity enhancement and due diligence.

● Significant financial management, including experience preparing and managing annual budgets of at least AUD1.5mil, monitoring and forecasting spend, and overseeing internal and external financial reporting.

● Experience of managing research projects.

● Experience of leading government or other donor-funded programmes, including donor relationship management, programme development and reporting.

● Significant experience of securing funding for new work, including concept development, building donor relationships and writing proposals and budgets.

● Understanding of anti-racist and decolonisation approaches to peacebuilding practice, team management and programme management.

● Excellent communication skills, to communicate complex issues effectively and adjust communication style to varying circumstances, including ability to listen actively to people from varying backgrounds and with a range of political, cultural, gender and sexual identities and value orientations, combined with an ability to engage with them clearly and sensitively.

● Excellent written and spoken English.

● Experience implementing projects in difficult social and political situations or conflict contexts, and experience of hostile environment training or willingness to undertake hostile environment training.

● Graduate-level study or equivalent by experience in conflict resolution, international relations, development studies, international humanitarian law, gender, peace and security or other related fields.

● Excellent organisational and coordination skills, including the ability to think and plan strategically while also retaining close attention to detail, to manage and prioritise a diverse and demanding workload, to convene and run efficient meetings and meet deadlines.

● Ability to navigate political sensitivities and awareness of the complexity of working in conflict-affected situations, including appreciation of confidentiality and handling sensitive information with due care.

● Willingness and ability to work irregular hours on occasions and to undertake frequent international travel in sometimes uncomfortable or insecure conditions.

● Excellent word processing, spreadsheet, database and email software skills.

### Desirable knowledge, skills and experience

● Experience facilitating workshops and dialogue processes.

● Experience developing and managing advocacy strategies and engagement with policymakers.

● Experience of and managing advocacy projects.

● Experience of producing high-quality written work.

● Experience of designing, organising and managing research and advocacy events.

● Extensive knowledge of the social and political landscape in the Pacific and wider region, and its conflicts.

● Experience living and working in the Pacific region.

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Assistant - Part Time 50%
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
**About ACTED**

“ We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.

**Greening strategy:**

Acted’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each Acted employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities:

- Contribute towards the adherence and development of the greening strategy plan.
- Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles
- Encouraging and promoting environmental safeguarding processes and environmental programming standards in accordance with SOPs and technical guideline notes

**Acted PSEAH Policy:**
The MEAL Assistant has the responsibility to adhere to the PSEAH Policy (Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment). And has the obligation to complete all mandatory trainings related to the Code of Conduct and the PSEA policy and report any safeguarding concern such as breaches of organisational policies or codes of conduct according to Acted’s procedures. The MEAL Assistant carries out work duties in a way that does not harm children, vulnerable adults or other staff or volunteers.
**Location:** **Damascus & Rural Damascus – Syria**
**Start Date:** **ASAP**

**Duration of the Contract: 6 Months.**

**Job Purpose**

The MEAL Assistant is responsible for assisting the MEAL Officers to implement all MEAL field activities and tasks including assessments, beneficiary verification, data entry, reporting, collection of and ensuring adherence to lessons learned and best practices, and any other tasks as required. He/she will be responsible for supporting the team of MEAL enumerators in the field.
**Objectives**

1. Implement MEAL assessments in the field in a reliable, accurate and transparent manner, including collecting primary and secondary data, reporting on findings, and supporting the development of tools and methodologies.
2. Support organizational learning by ensuring adherence to MEAL technical guidelines, lessons learned, and best practices.
3. Ensure lessons learnt and best practices are discoursed and documented by reporting them in a timely manner.
4. Contribute to the effective functioning of beneficiary complaints and response mechanism and enhance the trust and confidence of beneficiaries, identify areas of our work which need to be improved and ensure that Acted learns from the feedback provided through this process.

## **Duties and Responsibilities:**

1. **Appraisals, Monitoring Missions, and Evaluations**

***1.1 Field Data Collection***

- Supervise and support MEAL enumerators team during data collection in the field;
- Coordinate with the Area MEAL Officer to carry out the assessments (including, but not limited to: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) surveys, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, baseline and endline surveys, as well as other types of assessments and data collection that is required);
- Check that material necessary to carry out the assessment is sufficient and appropriate;
- Write down the observations and answers in an ordinate and clear way, recording responses accurately;
- Record and forward all complaints and suggestions received while in the field to the appropriate Accountability Officer/Accountability assistant.
- Collect evidence where applicable
- Probe to clarify unclear answers;
- Write down the observations and answers in an ordinate and clear way, recording responses accurately;

1. ***2 Reporting***

- Report monitoring findings and any other findings and observation emerged during data collection activities frequently to the MEAL Officers so to communicate the progress of assessment activities;
- Recognize and give account of problems in obtaining data and provide useful feedback from field research activities;
- In the absence of a dedicated Data Entry Officer, enter all field data into appropriate databases on an accurate and timely basis;
- Cross-check the accuracy of data entry;
- Support the maintenance of an efficient and accurate filing system for all electronic and hard copy documents;
- Report monitoring findings at Daily/Weekly Area Meetings, as required by MEAL Officer;
- Collect high-resolution and good quality photos of Acted project activities in the field, featuring donor, partner and Acted logos, and delivery photos to the AME Officer (in line with Acted Child Protection Policy and Photo Guidelines).

1. ***3 Support the Development of MEAL Tools and Methodologies***

- Support the MEAL Officer in designing appropriate information collection tools and methodologies, including assessment Terms of Reference, and questionnaires;
- Support the translation of tools and methodologies into local language(s) as required.

1. **Support to Organizational Learning**

***2.1 Collection of Lessons Learned and Best Practices***

- Collect lessons learned and best practices from beneficiaries, community leaders, partners, and other stakeholders during assessment/monitoring missions;

***2.1 Monitoring Adherence to Program Strategies and Guidelines***

- Cross-check that project implementation adheres to the technical guidelines for the program, as required by the MEAL Officer;
- Monitor the implementation of lessons learned and best practices;
- Cross-check the accuracy and relevance of beneficiary selection according to contractual criteria.

**Other**
- Participate in any meetings or conferences as required by the MEAL Officer;
- Perform any other related activities as assigned by immediate supervisor.

**Key Performance Indicators**

- Mechanism in place and functional to provide data on project indicators in a timely manner
- Mechanism in place and functional that allows at least the reporting on Acted 16 global standard indicators
- Lessons learnt and best practices recorded in the Area Lessons Learnt and Best Practices document according to Acted standard learning procedures and updated in regular and timely manner.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS**

- At least one year experience with NGOs and/or International Institutions in Monitoring and Evaluation
- University Degree /institute.
- Number of years of relevant experience in monitoring & Evaluation.
- Basic English skills is an asset
- Resident in Damascus/Rural Damascus governorate
- Ability to travel locally
- Good command of using KOBO application via smartphones.
- Good command of using MS Excel and MS Word
- Good command of using GPS devices/programs for data collection
- Ability to build and sustain relationship with team members and interviewees in the field as well as the local authorities i.e., camp managers…. etc.
- Flexibility and adaptability are essential, as well as the ability to plan, take initiative and work under minimal supervision.
- Capability to work under pressure and travel to the targeted areas within Acted projects
