**Financial Analyst, Manchester UK**

**The starting salary package for this position is £35,604 GBP (plus contributory pension)**

**This is a fixed-term role for 6 months.**

**About MAG:**

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in over 40 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

**About the role:**

The Finance Analyst (FA) will provide remote finance and analytical support to the MAG Ukraine Programme from the UK. The role will focus on financial analysis, budget monitoring, forecasting, donor and management reporting, data quality and month-end support. Working closely with the Ukraine Finance team and relevant UK colleagues, the FA will help turn financial data into clear information for programme decision-making, identify variances and trends, and support timely follow-up on financial actions.

**About the Ukraine programme:**

Since the Russian invasion of 24 February 2022, Ukraine has been subjected to heavy artillery bombardment, missile, and air strikes, as well as the use of landmines and cluster munitions. The scale of the conflict and the use of high impact and indiscriminate weapons requires an urgent and extensive response. MAG responded to the crisis in 2022 and now employs nearly 440 staff in our Ukraine programme, in a range of operational and support/administrative activities, with further scale-up planned during 2026. The programme has a representation office in Kyiv, and operational offices in Mykolaiv (also covering accessible areas of Kherson) and Kharkiv.

**Responsibilities:**

• Prepare and maintain regular budget versus actual analysis for Ukraine projects, departments and cost centres, highlighting significant variances, trends and areas requiring follow-up.

• Support the preparation and updating of programme forecasts, working with budget holders and the Ukraine Finance team to ensure assumptions are clear, reasonable and supported.

• Assist with monthly management accounts and internal financial reporting, including concise commentary for managers and budget holders.

• Support with budgets for proposals or realignments throughout project periods

• Support donor financial reporting and grant-management processes, including review of expenditure, coding, supporting schedules and reconciliation to approved budgets.

• Review financial data for completeness, accuracy and consistency, and raise identified issues with the relevant Finance team member or budget holder.

• Develop and maintain clear financial analysis tools, trackers, and Excel-based reports to support programme management and decision-making.

• Assist with project set-up, budget coding and the maintenance of accurate project and donor financial records.

• Provide finance support to budget holders, helping them understand expenditure, forecasts, variances, and financial responsibilities.

• Work closely with the Ukraine Finance team, Programme colleagues and MAG UK Finance to resolve financial queries and improve the quality and timeliness of financial information.

• Provide ad-hoc financial analysis in response to programme priorities, including scenario modelling, cost comparisons, and other management information as required.

• Maintain confidentiality and ensure all work is carried out in accordance with MAG financial policies, procedures, safeguarding requirements and standards of conduct.

• Undertake other similar finance and analytical duties as reasonably required to support the Ukraine

Programme.

**We’re looking for someone with:**

**Knowledge and Experience**

- Relevant finance, accounting, economics or business qualification, or equivalent practical experience.
- Good understanding of accounting principles, budgeting, forecasting and financial reporting.

**Skills**

- Strong analytical skills and the ability to identify, explain and communicate financial trends and variances.
- Advanced working knowledge of Microsoft Excel; experience of finance systems and data analysis tools is desirable.
- Good written and spoken English. Ukrainian language skills are strongly desirable for effective support to the Ukraine Programme.
- Excellent attention to detail, organisation and ability to work accurately with large volumes of financial information.

**Programme Officer, Senegal**

**The starting salary package for this position is £34,580 GBP, including all allowances.**

**This is a fixed-term role for 6 months with a possibility of extension.**

**This is an unaccompanied post.**

**About MAG:**

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

**About the role:**

Reporting to the Country Director, you will provide direct support to the Country Director in the effective management and implementation of MAG’s programme in Senegal. The role will support grant and project management, donor

reporting and proposal development, project monitoring including the follow-up of results and indicators, and

internal and external programme communications and visibility. The Programme Officer will work across the

programme to ensure that project information is accurate, up to date and clearly communicated, and will contribute

to the effective delivery and continued development of MAG’s activities in Senegal.

**About the Senegal programme:**

MAG has been working in Senegal since 2014, initially supporting the Senegalese Armed Forces with safe destruction of obsolete ammunition, secure storage, and capacity-building. Since 2021, MAG has expanded into Humanitarian Mine Action in Casamance, at the request of the National Mine Action Centre (CNAMS). In Casamance, MAG supports CNAMS through training, strengthening information management systems, and conducting non-technical surveys and risk education to better understand contamination and raise awareness among affected communities. Casamance remains contaminated with mines and explosive remnants of war, limiting access to land and livelihoods. Through the new CLEAR-Casamance project, MAG will reduce these risks, release safe land, and restore access to productive areas. This will support recovery, enable displaced families to return safely, and contribute to lasting peace and stability in the region.

**Responsibilities:**

**Grant management & monitoring**

• Provide day-to-day monitoring of grants and contracts according to work plans agreed by the CD.

• Support the CD to ensure effective grant management and the timely preparation and submission of donor reports.

• Provide timely and accurate information and analysis on current grant and proposal status, as required by the CD and MAG HQ.

• Maintain up-to-date grant management tools, including reporting deadlines, key deliverables and donor requirements.

• Support the CD in ensuring that donor contractual requirements and commitments are understood and followed by relevant programme teams.

• Coordinate with relevant programme, finance and operations colleagues to ensure that information required for grant management and reporting is available and submitted on time.

• Assist the CD in monitoring contracts and MoUs, including those with local partners, and support partners as required to ensure contractual obligations are fulfilled.

• Flag potential delays, compliance issues or other grant-related risks to the CD in a timely manner.

**Proposal Development**

• Support the development of concept notes, proposals and other funding submissions, in coordination with relevant programme teams and MAG HQ.

• Coordinate the collection of information required for proposal development, including programme, operational and financial inputs.

• Contribute when required by CD to donor meetings, visits and briefings, including the preparation of relevant programme information and materials.

**Programme Monitoring & Information Management**

• Develop and maintain systems and tools for recording and monitoring programme activities, outputs, results and indicators.

• Coordinate the regular collection and consolidation of programme data, ensuring information is complete, accurate and up to date.

• Monitor progress against project indicators and targets and highlight gaps or areas requiring follow-up.

• Support the analysis of programme data and results to inform project management, donor reporting and programme decision-making.

• Establish appropriate internal reporting formats and ensure effective information flows between field teams, the country office and MAG HQ.

**Programme Communications & Visibility**

• Support the development and implementation of communications and visibility activities for the Senegal programme.

• Develop high-quality communication materials, including case studies, success stories, programme brief, brochures, presentations and other donor-facing materials.

• Collect and develop programme content, including stories, photographs, key results and operational updates, in coordination with programme and field teams.

• Use tools such as Canva to produce professional and visually engaging communication and visibility materials.

• Ensure that communication materials are consistent with MAG’s corporate identity, messaging and communication guidelines, in coordination with MAG HQ Communications.

• Support donor visibility requirements across projects and ensure that relevant visibility commitments are appropriately implemented.

• Maintain an organised library of programme communication materials, including photographs, case studies and key programme information.

• Support and train programme staff on MAG’s communications and visibility guidelines, including the appropriate collection and use of photographs, beneficiary stories and informed consent.

• Assist in the planning and hosting of programme visits by MAG staff, donors and partner agencies.

**We’re looking for someone with:**

**Essential Experience**

• Significant experience working in development and humanitarian program related field operations or field activities in developing countries

• Experience of developing and supporting projects.

**Essential Skills and Knowledge**

• Experience working in humanitarian or development programmes.

• Experience in grant/project management, including donor reporting and monitoring of project results and

indicators.

• Experience supporting the development of proposals.

• Experience developing communication and visibility materials for programmes, including case studies, programme briefs, brochures and donor-facing materials.

• Experience using tools such as Canva to produce professional communication products.

• Strong written communication skills, with the ability to turn programme information and results into clear and engaging content.

• Good eye for visual presentation and attention to detail.

• Fluent in English and French.

**Desirable**

• Knowledge of relevant institutional donors with an understanding of their needs and requirements.

• Understanding of legal issues in relation to contracts and charity and company law.

**About the role:**

In this role, you will play a vital part in supporting communities living with the daily realities of explosive ordnance. As Community Liaison Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring MAG’s approach to community participation lead how communities shape and guide our mine action work, ensuring their knowledge, priorities, and concerns are central to everything we do in your area of operation. In close coordination with the Community Liaison Manager – Team Leader, you will manage and mentor Community Liaison teams, work closely with technical colleagues, and ensure high‑quality delivery of non‑technical survey and explosive ordnance risk education that directly informs safe land release and clearance.

jobs.title: "Senior Manager, HR” BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF)
jobs.description:
**BRAC International is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential.**

**Position: “Senior Manager, HR” BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF)**

**Job Location: Nairobi, Kenya / Dhaka, Bangladesh** ***(Candidates must be nationals of, or have the legal right to work in, either Kenya or Bangladesh)***

**Application Deadline: 12 October 2026**

**About BRAC International:**

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organisation, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realize their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF) oversees its microfinance subsidiaries outside Bangladesh, which are wholly or majority owned by the legal entity BRAC International Holdings B.V. (BIHBV), operating across eight countries in Africa and Asia. Within this mandate, BI MF expands financial inclusion by responsibly delivering financial services to people at the bottom of the pyramid, particularly women living in poverty in rural and hard-to-reach areas, to create self-employment opportunities, build financial resilience, and harness their entrepreneurial spirit by empowering them economically. The achievement of both ‘Impact and Scale’ are critically important, ensuring that each subsidiary has systems in place to realise both components of the mission.

BI MF provides strategic direction, governance oversight, and institutional strengthening across the portfolio. Today, its operations serve clients (97% women) across the eight operating countries, managing a loan portfolio of approximately USD 277 million, and employing over 7,000 staff, of whom 87% are women.

**About the Position:**

The Senior Manager, HR, BI MF (SM, HR) is an end-to-end generalist HR business partner, reporting to the Associate Director, HR, BI MF (AD, HR), and responsible for an assigned portfolio of BI MF subsidiaries (entities) and designated BI MF Central Team functions/units. The role serves as the HR focal point for assigned Central Team functions/units and strategic people partner to assigned Entity leaders.

The role partners with Entity Heads of HR, Microfinance Management Teams (MMT) and Central Team Technical Leads across its portfolio to understand business priorities, anticipate people implications and shape practical HR responses. In close partnership with the other SM, HR in the team, the role ensures coordinated support across BI MF entities and Central Team functions, aligning on shared and cross-cutting priorities, providing cover during periods of absence or peak demand, and promoting consistency in HR delivery. Working closely with the AD, HR, the role brings insights from its portfolio to inform BI MF-wide HR priorities, decisions and interventions.

Working within BI’s matrixed three-part HR model, the role connects business and Entity needs with HR Centers of Excellence (CoEs) and HR Central Services, ensuring enterprise frameworks and expertise are effectively translated into business context and applied appropriately. The role strengthens Entity HR capability and follow-through, provides trusted advice on complex people matters, and drives cross-entity learning and strategic HR priorities that support growth, impact and sustainable performance.

**Key Responsibilities:**

***1. Strategic HR Partnership***

- Own the HRBP agenda for an assigned portfolio of BI MF entities, partnering with Entity Heads of HR, MMTs and relevant leaders to understand business priorities, challenges and people implications.
- Serve as the HR focal point for designated BI MF Central Team functions/units, partnering with their leaders and BI MF Senior Management Team on people priorities, workforce needs and HR matters.
- Translate business priorities into people priorities, provide constructive challenge and shape practical HR responses that support business performance.
- Strengthen Entity HR capability, judgement and follow-through, enabling Entity HR teams to lead local implementation while providing advice, challenge and escalation where required.
- Strengthen HR delivery across assigned Central Team functions/units, ensuring their people priorities are connected to the wider BI MF HR agenda.
- Work closely with the other SM, HR, to align on shared and cross-cutting priorities, and facilitate knowledge sharing, peer learning and transfer of good practices to promote consistent and effective HR delivery across their respective portfolios.
- Work closely with the AD, HR, bringing insights from the portfolio to inform BI MF-wide HR priorities, decisions and interventions.

***2. Business and Workforce Effectiveness***

- Partner with leaders on business-led workforce, organisation and people decisions arising from growth, transformation, restructuring, productivity or changing business needs.
- Assess people’s implications of organisational changes and alignment initiatives, develop options with leaders and advise on effective workforce and organisational solutions.
- Provide HR input into business planning and strategic decisions, ensuring people’s considerations are integrated into business priorities and execution.

***3. Leadership & Talent Management***

- Partner with leaders and Entity HR to strengthen critical talent and leadership pipelines, succession and readiness for current and future business needs.
- Facilitate talent reviews and succession discussions, leveraging enterprise frameworks and CoE expertise while ensuring business ownership of talent decisions and development actions.
- Partner with leaders on leadership development, talent mobility and internal movement to strengthen organisational capability and retention.
- Promote inclusive and sustainable leadership pipelines, including women in leadership and other priority talent groups.

***4. People Risk & Organisational Effectiveness***

- Identify people-related risks, recurring organisational issues and improvement opportunities across the assigned portfolio, including regulatory, policy, audit, employee-relations, safeguarding, conduct and culture-related risks.
- Strengthen Entity HR capability and follow-through on risk mitigation, audit actions and organisational improvements, ensuring agreed actions are implemented and escalating material or recurring risks where required.
- Partner with Entity HR and leaders to ensure follow-through on recommendations arising from safeguarding and conduct investigations, disciplinary processes, culture assessments and other people-related reviews.
- Identify cross-entity themes and lessons, working with the Associate Director, HR and relevant CoEs to inform improvements to enterprise policies, frameworks and practices.

***5. Complex HR Advisory***

- Provide trusted HR advice to Entity leaders, MMTs, BI MF Senior Management Team and Entity HR Heads on complex people matters, including employee relations, performance, productivity, leadership and organisational change.
- Help leaders assess options, risks and implications and make sound, balanced people decisions.
- Provide targeted tactical or interim support during critical transitions, capacity gaps or high-priority interventions, while building sustainable Entity HR ownership and capability.

***6. Enterprise HR Integration***

- Connect business and Entity needs with the relevant CoEs and Central Services, ensuring the right expertise is engaged at the right time.
- Translate and contextualise enterprise HR frameworks, policies and solutions for BI MF business needs, without duplicating CoE ownership.
- Coordinate cross-functional and cross-entity HR priorities, ensuring alignment, business ownership, effective implementation and follow-through.
- Bring Entity and Central Team insights into BI MF-wide HR priorities and support the AD, HR in shaping strategic HR interventions.

***7. People Insights & Decision***

- Analyse people data and business trends to identify risks, patterns and opportunities, translating insights into practical recommendations for HR and business decisions.
- Develop and maintain HR dashboards and portfolio reporting, providing clear visibility of workforce, talent, mobility, performance and other key people indicators.
- Use people insights to inform workforce planning, talent and leadership decisions, organisational effectiveness and strategic HR initiatives.
- Analyse workforce and employee data across areas such as recruitment, onboarding, performance, employee experience, benefits, mobility, work permits and career development to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
- Prepare regular and ad-hoc analysis, reports and presentations for BI MF leadership, Entity leaders and relevant governance forums, highlighting key trends, implications and actions.
- Strengthen the quality and consistency of Entity HR reporting and data, supporting Entity HR teams to use insights more effectively in business discussions and decision-making.
- Leverage insights across the portfolio to identify cross-entity patterns, share learning and inform BI MF-wide HR priorities and interventions.
- Stay abreast of relevant HR analytics practices and emerging approaches to strengthen evidence-based people decision-making.

***8. Safeguarding***

- Establish a safeguarding culture across all levels of the programme by implementing the safeguarding policy. Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
- Responsible to ensure team members are appropriately trained, supported and have access to resources regarding issues that are identified and actioned in accordance with the safeguarding policy and procedure.
- Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place, encourage others to do so.
- Support the HR department to provide clarification on safeguarding policies and disseminate Safeguarding policies and all supporting promotional materials within the program, department and field offices in the country.
- Attend regular Safeguarding Focal meetings with BI MF SG focals and provide safeguarding-related updates.

**Academic Qualifications:**

- Minimum Bachelor’s Degree in degree in business administration, Human Resource Management or a related field.
- A postgraduate qualification in Human Resources, Business, Organisation Development or a related field is desirable.
- Professional HR qualification/certification (e.g., IHRM, SHRM, CIPD or equivalent international HR certification is preferred.

**Experience:**

- 7+ years of progressive HR experience, including at least 3 years in an HRBP or strategic generalist HR role supporting senior leaders.
- Demonstrated experience partnering with business leaders on workforce, organisational, talent and complex people decisions, with the ability to translate business priorities into practical HR responses.
- Experience in financial services, microfinance, banking, fintech or another regulated and operationally complex environment. Experience in financial inclusion, frontline-led operations or organisations delivering impact at scale to underserved communities is an advantage.
- Experience working across multiple entities, countries or diverse organisational environments, preferably within an international, matrixed or geographically dispersed organisation.
- Demonstrated ability to strengthen HR capability and enable local HR teams to improve judgement, ownership and execution.
- Strong experience in employee relations, organisational change, people risk and other sensitive HR matters, with sound judgement and understanding of regulatory implications.
- Experience using people data and insights to inform business recommendations, workforce decisions and leadership priorities.
- Experience working effectively with HR CoEs and specialist teams, translating their expertise into practical business solutions without duplicating their role.

**Knowledge, Skills and Competencies:**

- **Generalist HR expertise:** Broad HR knowledge and sound technical depth across talent, organisation effectiveness, workforce planning, performance, employee relations, reward, mobility, policy and compliance; able to assess people and regulatory risks and engage specialist expertise appropriately.
- **Business acumen & HRBP capability:** Ability to connect people priorities and HR risks to business performance, operational continuity and regulatory requirements.
- **Strategic thinking & judgement:** Sound judgement, critical thinking and problem-solving in complex, sensitive and ambiguous situations.
- **Stakeholder management & influence:** Ability to build trusted relationships and influence without authority across a matrixed, multicultural environment.
- **HR integration:** Ability to translate enterprise HR frameworks and specialist expertise into practical, context-appropriate business solutions without duplicating CoE responsibilities.
- **Advisory & capability building:** Strong coaching, advisory and capability-building skills, particularly in strengthening Entity HR judgement, ownership and effectiveness.
- **People insights:** Ability to analyse people data and trends and translate insights into practical business recommendations and decisions.
- **Execution & prioritisation:** Strong follow-through and ability to manage competing strategic and operational priorities across a multi-entity portfolio.
- **Communication & professionalism:** Excellent communication, presentation and relationship-building skills, with sound discretion, integrity and confidentiality.

**Additional Requirements:**

- **Willingness to travel:** approximately 30% to entity locations, including planned entity visits, long stays to provide interim cover and support during critical interventions.

jobs.description:
## Role Information:

Job Title: Finance, HR and Logistics Manager in the Central African Republic

Location: Bangui, CAR with regular visits to the base(s) in the country

Report: Country Peacebuilding Manager, CAR and the Director of Finance in the UK

Type of contract: This position is open to both national and international candidates

Supervision : Hierarchical management of 3 Hub Finance, Administrative and HR Officers, and a small support team in Bangui

Salary: 50,000-54,000 € gross, 33 days of annual leave plus R&R, in-country accommodation (shared housing) and per diem

## Duties and Responsibilities:

He/she ensures legal monitoring, ensures that financial standards are applied in terms of accounting, internal control system and reporting.

The Finance, HR and Logistics Manager provides technical support and strengthens the capacity of the support team under his/her responsibility.

### **Key Responsibilities:**

1. ### – Administrative and HR management:

- Ensure fiscal and legal monitoring of the mission vis-à-vis the country's institutions and ensure compliance with the legislation in force in all the actions of the program
- Ensure the follow-up of the procedures for registering the mission with the authorities concerned
- Manage national staff contracts in conjunction with the Ministry or Delegation of Work and Social Security
- Participate in inter-admin meetings with other NGOs
- Ensure the recruitment and support of national staff, including members of his team
- Identify training needs, train and provide technical support to team members
- Conduct annual appraisal interviews for your team
- Ensure all new staff receive a comprehensive induction, including mandatory Safeguarding training, and maintain accurate records to confirm completion and compliance
- Work closely with the Safeguarding Team to promote a strong safeguarding culture and ensure that all safeguarding policies, procedures, reporting requirements, and follow-up actions are implemented and adhered to across the country programme

1. ### - Accounting and treasury:

- Supervise the accounting cycle of the mission
- Ensure the supervision, control and accounting consolidation of the mission, the monthly accounting closing for sending to the headquarters and supervise the archiving of accounting documents on SharePoint
- Ensure smooth cash flow control and management
- Validate cash inventories, bank reconciliations
- Monitor and manage cash flow in the safe and bank accounts, and ensure that cash requests are anticipated and communicated in advance
- Compile the cash flow forecasts of the bases and prepare the request for funds at the headquarters
- Checking analytical assignments and making corrections
- Ensure the proper preparation of internal and external audits and ensure financial controls

1. ### - Finance and Reporting

- With colleagues associated with the program, use budget tracking reports to forecast future expenditures and recommend reallocation or modification of the agreed budget
- Analyse financial information, ensure compliance with the mission's financing plans, donor contracts and anticipate possible financial risks
- Is responsible for ensuring that financial procedures and mission control are respected and updated
- Ensure the preparation of new budgets and follow up on them
- Provide technical support to operational and budget holders on financial management
- Develop and implement procedures and financial monitoring tools
- Ensure compliance with the country's tax rules, prepare tax returns and make their payments
- Ensures the training and follow-up of partnerships for financial, HR and logistical aspects
- Prepare financial reports and submit to the Director of Finance in the UK

1. ### -Logistics

- Ensure the management of the supply chain and logistics
- Participate in security management with the Country Manager
- Ensure compliance with the logistics and procurement procedures of the European Union (PRAG) and Concordis International on the mission
- Manage IT and communication equipment and Concordis leases on the mission

1. ### - Qualifications and Skills

- Master's degree or professional qualification in accounting, finance, economics, business administration or related field
- Minimum 5 years of experience in administrative and financial management within an NGO/international organization
- Proven knowledge of financial systems, experience in supervising financial operations in the context of NGO project management, and experience in financial reporting to international donors such as the European Union
- Excellent financial and analytical skills
- Excellent communication and writing skills to effectively report on the financial performance of programs
- Ability to manage teams and demonstrate leadership
- Ability to assess the finance, HR and logistics skills of the teams, and to train them
- Experience in supervising logistics and HR operations, including remote team management
- Full professional skills in French (written and spoken) and English are desirable
- Excellent command of computer tools, in particular Microsoft Excel
- Strong communication and presentation skills
- Ability to interact, communicate and negotiate with local authorities and communities in an open, transparent, constructive, patient and effective manner
- Ability to grasp sensitive issues related to cultural differences and political issues, and to be able to approach them with tact, diplomacy and sensitivity.

jobs.title: CHARGE-E DE PROJET APPUI AUX PARTENAIRES
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Le.la chargé.e de projet Appui aux partenaires contribue à la définition et la mise en oeuvre de la stratégie de la Mission France en Ile-de-France

Contribuer à la définition des activités d'accompagnement des partenaires dans sa zone d'intervention
Contribuer à la définition et au cadrage des activités d'accompagnement des partenaires de la base en lien avec la coordinatrice terrain et en concertation avec les autres chargé.es de projet et le coordinateur programme ;
Assurer le déploiement des activités d'accompagnement des partenaires dans sa zone d'intervention
Proposer les protocoles d'intervention, les outils de diagnostics, les outils et méthodologie de suivi et évaluation, et formation sur base du cadre défini avec la coordinatrice terrain

Assurer la qualité des activités menées sur le terrain
Appuyer la participation active à la coordination externe, aux dynamiques de mutualisation inter-partenariales et aux formations externes des partenaires (réunions externes, sessions de travail inter-acteurs, sessions de restitution inter-acteurs, etc.).
Assurer le suivi et la mise en oeuvre des projets co-portés dans sa zone d'intervention en lien avec la stratégie d'influence de la mission France
Participer à la rédaction de nouveaux projets en coordination avec l'équipe et les partenaires
Proposer les protocoles d'intervention, les outils de diagnostics, les outils et méthodologie de suivi et évaluation adaptés et nécessaires pour le déploiement des activités, en co-construction avec les différents acteurs et personnes impliqués et en lien avec la coordinatrice terrain
Animer ou co-animer des cadres de travail collectif et/ou des dynamiques de gouvernance en lien avec le déploiement des projets, en lien avec la coordinatrice terrain ;
Développer et assurer un suivi du Plan de Suivi Evaluation Redevabilité et Apprentissage des activités des projets ainsi que le suivi des changements, en lien avec la coordination ACF ;
Appuyer la remontée des informations de terrain à des fins de communication et de plaidoyer
Contribuer à la rédaction des documents de communication interne et externe
Assurer le reporting des activités et l'analyse des données qualitatives et quantitatives et contribuer à la rédaction des reporting
Manager et superviser l'équipe
Recruter, encadrer, piloter et accompagner l'équipe

Profile :

Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme niveau Master (Bac+5) dans l'un des domaines suivants : sciences politiques, développement local et territorial, gestion ou coordination de projet, politiques publiques, affaires publiques, design social ou domaine équivalent.
Vous avez un minimum de 4 ans d'expérience professionnelle en gestion de projet principalement en France, dans les domaines de l'action sociale, de la sécurité alimentaire, de la lutte contre la précarité alimentaire, de l'accès aux droits ou du suivi-évaluation.
Vous avez une expérience avérée de coordination de projets multi-acteurs associant collectivités territoriales, services de l'Etat, associations et autres partenaires locaux.
Vous maîtrisez des méthodes de diagnostic des besoins, de collecte, d'analyse et de valorisation de données.
Vous avez la capacité à concevoir et à animer des ateliers participatifs, en vous appuyant sur les méthodes d'intelligence collective et d'éducation populaire.
Votre connaissance fine du tissu associatif et institutionnel de Seine-Saint-Denis constitue un réel atout.
Vous avez la capacité à fédérer et à travailler en équipe.
Vous êtes reconnue pour votre créativité, force de proposition et de votre aisance à travailler dans des environnements complexes.

Conditions d'emploi

Statut : Cadre intégré - CDD - Temps plein
Lieu : Montreuil
Rémunération : De 37K à 41Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience,
Prime d'ancienneté à partir de 3 années de présence au siège
Avantages: 25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT
Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF. Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)
Indemnités Transport : Prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail
Indemnités Tickets-restaurant (Carte déjeuner Up):Prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros
Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)
