jobs.title: Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Advisor
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we’d like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action. Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home.

The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, asking “Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

**Job Overview:**

IRC’s Global Crisis Analysis, Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security, and Preparedness teams have come together to form ‘ASAP’ (Analysis, Security, Access and Preparedness) to strengthen global and regional support to IRC teams to deliver in the most complex, volatile and high-risk operating environments to reach the worst-affected and least-served people in need. Housed within the IRC’s Emergency Unit, but supporting countries and emergencies responses across IRC’s footprint, the Advisor allies with country and emergency response leadership, ASAP colleagues, and Regional Safety and Security Directors, to provide strategic, technical and operational support to enable IRC to open, expand, and sustain programs in emergencies, major crises, and complex environments – to reach the worst-affected and least-served populations.

The Advisor will work alongside the Director, and the Emergency Response Team Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Coordinator, to split responsibilities by country portfolio and/or thematic demands and/or level of complexity based on their respective scope of work and experience. The role brings additional capacity, and challenges and supports teams to meet IRC’s mandate through effective analysis and scenario planning to inform program and operational ambitions, and support to deliver on these with enhanced humanitarian access and security management.

The International Rescue Committee’s Emergency Unit (EmU) leads IRC’s global emergency preparedness and response to sudden-onset crises, complex emergencies, and high-risk contexts. EmU strengthens IRC’s ability to operate safely and effectively in volatile environments through surge capacity, systems development, and expert technical leadership.

***Location:** This position is open to national candidates or candidates who have residency in either Kenya, UK or Geneva. Candidates from any other country that has an IRC Office, are welcome to apply as well and will be hosted in that country.*

***Fluency in both written & Spoken French & English required***

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Humanitarian access management**

- Plan and deliver inclusive in-person and remote scenario development workshops as part of wider ASAP support to frontline program teams responding to major crises, linking those scenarios relevant strategies to support the IRC to serve the worst-affected and least-served populations despite conflict, volatility and risk.
- Support frontline program teams to develop and track indicators for tracking crisis developments in support countries, where requested as part of wider support, and actively contribute to information sharing with IRC colleagues about key crisis developments in support countries.
- Support country leadership to develop and implement specific access and acceptance strategies, in support of the Country Director/Emergency Team Leader, ASAP and/or RSSDs to enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access to reach target populations, in line with IRC policy and international humanitarian law – these may include a wide range of access approaches including broader risk management and remote management.
- Ensure strategies include how IRC builds relationships, engages and negotiates with authorities, key power brokers, security actors, and community stakeholders, including with state and non‑state actors, to ensure IRC’s mission and activities are understood and accepted, and that staff and programs can operate safely and without disruption.
- Build and maintain an active network of humanitarian access and security staff internally and across organisations.
- Maintain currency with methods, approaches and professional developments in relevant topics, and represent IRC in relevant global fora where needed.

**Safety and security management**

- Support country leadership and access, safety and security teams to identify, analyze and mitigate safety and security (S&S) risks across emergency responses, ensuring alignment with IRC Security Minimum Standards (SMS), Duty of Care, GEDI and PEERS principles, and integrate into access, security, preparedness strategies where relevant.
- Support the implementation of S&S standards and approaches to strengthen humanitarian access, and ensure S&S preparedness and contingency align with program ambitions.
- Support country/response teams in incident management, where relevant.

**Emergency preparedness**

- In close collaboration with ASAP and the Director, Emergency Performance and Quality, support country programs to develop and implement humanitarian access, safety and security approaches in their emergency preparedness and contingency plans, streamlining existing strategies and plans where relevant/possible, through in-country or remote mentoring, training and technical support.
- Support EmU in the development and adaptation of humanitarian access, safety and security systems, practices and resources, and centralized knowledge management.

**Learning & Development**

- Co-develop, with consortium partners, a humanitarian access framework that is accessible and used by partners to define access ambitions and strategies.
- Support the development, revision and uptake of IRC’s technical resources for analysis, security, access and preparedness, learning from operational experience, as well as global trends and good practices.
- Guide, train, coach and mentor IRC country leaders and frontline staff on humanitarian access approaches, safety and security, including Security Risk Management (SRM), and partner capacity strengthening, ensuring the inclusion of gender-sensitive approaches that address gender-specific risks.
- Design, deliver and track humanitarian access, safety and security capacity strengthening activities (including training, coaching, peer-to-peer learning) for EmU and priority country teams in access, safety and security training (including READI and humanitarian negotiation) and context analysis and scenario planning – leveraging internal and external resources.
- Ensure an ongoing exchange of learning and good practice in ASAP methods and approaches with partners; and deliver capacity sharing activities on analysis, access and security where relevant and prioritized.
- Contribute humanitarian access, safety and security content to EmU trainings and conferences and support cross-learning, and to global Safety and Security resources, as relevant.

**Partnerships**

- Champion a culture of effective and respective partnerships across the EmU, including supporting country and emergency teams to provide technical or operational support to partners.
- To further IRC’s partnership ambitions, ensure partners play a central role in the development of access, security and engagement strategies, and the identified approaches, including capacity sharing initiatives.
- Working with the EmU Partnerships focal points, ensure IRC technical resources for humanitarian access, safety and security are adapted and/or oriented towards partners for their own adaptations, and support partners in their uptake and cross-contextual learning and application amongst partners and IR.
- Design and deliver capacity sharing activities with partners where this is identified by the country program and ASAP access and security support, including peer-to-peer exchange and humanitarian negotiation.
- Collaborate closely with consortium partners to learn, coordinate and ensure the shared delivery of each organisation’s analysis, security, access and preparedness approaches within the defined Project results, including grant reporting and capturing case studies.

**Team Culture**

- Build and maintain strong working relationships across EmU, the Global S&S Department and regional/country colleagues to promote a culture of partnership, collaboration and One IRC.
- Cultivate and maintain a positive, collaborative, safe and protective work environment, while additionally setting an example of ‘One IRC’-way of working within the team, EmU, and the wider organization.
- Contribute to efforts across EmU and through ASAP support to safe, diverse, and inclusive culture and ways of working across our programming.
- Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding, GEDI commitments, and IRC values.

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Work Experience:**

- At least 8 years of non-profit or NGO work experience within international humanitarian assistance programs with demonstrated successes in planning, organizing and managing safety and security in complex and volatile environments.
- Significant practical experience in humanitarian access, humanitarian negotiation, civil-military coordination, security management or related competencies.
- Substantial and documented prior experience as a facilitator – the ability to develop, implement, facilitate and impart learning to a wide range of audiences.
- Experience with collaborative/inclusive development of tools, guidance and learning materials for/with practitioners.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of legal and normative frameworks for humanitarian action and expertise in applying humanitarian principles in practice.
- Thorough familiarity with principles and current approaches to humanitarian access and acceptance models of security management, including demonstrated understanding and successes in gender security management and gender equality.
- Ability to gain a precise understanding of the various local, regional, country and international policies, operational positions and interactions, and ability to support analysis and its uptake into decision making before and during emergencies and major crises.
- Advanced skills in humanitarian negotiation, humanitarian-military relations and/or engagement with armed groups.
- Strong communication, diplomatic, relationship building and interpersonal skills, including to influence and obtain cooperation of individuals not under supervisory control.
- Proficiency in facilitating challenging conversations, and challenge teams, on strategic, technical and operational subject matter to create shared understanding and inform decisions.
- Proficiency in delivering training and coaching support to individuals, teams and/or partners.
- Humility in analysis, ways of working and willingness to learn with teams in the most complex settings.
- Able to work as member of multinational team and manage a variety of external and internal relationships to achieve results.
- Excellent ability to produce user-centered, effective, and responsive guidance, tools and materials.
- Ability to summarize sophisticated topics and information inclusively, clearly and succinctly.
- Demonstrated commitment to gender equality, diversity, and inclusion in humanitarian settings.
- Ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized and underrepresented groups in emergency response.
- Experience working with diverse teams and communities, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other groups at risk of exclusion.
- Commitment to ongoing learning and reflection on personal and organizational biases, and willingness to adapt practices to promote inclusion.

**Language Skills:** Proficiency in English and French required; Arabic and Spanish of additional added value.

**Key working relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Director of Emergency Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security

**Position directly supervises:** N/A

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:** ASAP colleagues, Regional Safety and Security Directors, Emergency Safety & Security Coordinator

**Working Environment*****:*** Up to 40% international travel may be required, including to environments affected by armed conflict.

**Compensation:** (Switzerland Pay Rate: CHF 100,000 - 115,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: GBP 60,000 - 66,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Gender Equality**: The IRC is committed to advancing gender equality, diversity, and inclusion in all aspects of our emergency response. We recognize that diverse teams and inclusive approaches are essential for effective humanitarian action and for ensuring that the needs and rights of all affected populations are respected and addressed.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Travel Administrator
jobs.description:
**Location: Amsterdam, Barcelona, Brussels, Geneva, Paris** (the candidates must hold a valid work authorisation in one of these locations)

**Contract:** Fixed term 12 months - 50%

**Starting date**: 01st of January 2027

**Deadline to apply:** 20th of October 2026

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract.

**I. MSF INTERNATIONAL**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and other offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information, and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**II. CONTEXT**

The role of Travel Administrator involves managing the travel arrangements for MSF International staff based in various MSF entities. The role replaces that of the Travel Referent for all staff travel, liaising with the finance and procurement departments, MSF partner sections, decentralized hubs, the Global Procurement Unit, as well as external suppliers such as the AMEX travel agency and accommodation providers.

**III. PURPOSE OF THE JOB**

The Travel Administrator is responsible for booking and coordinating travel arrangements for MSF International staff, ensuring that travel services are delivered accurately, efficiently and in compliance with the Travel Policy. The role provides operational and administrative support to travellers and contributes to the smooth delivery of travel services across MSF International.

**IV. ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**Coordinate travel bookings and related travel services for MSF International staff, ensuring compliance with the Travel Policy and operational requirements.**

- Review travel requests for completeness and compliance.
- Book flights, trains, buses, accommodation and related travel services.
- Ensure travel arrangements meet traveller and organisational needs.

**Provide travel administration and traveller support throughout the travel process.**

- Advise travellers on travel procedures and documentation requirements.
- Support visa and travel preparation processes.
- Respond to travel-related queries and provide accurate travel information.

**Contribute to efficient and sustainable travel management.**

- Identify travel options that balance cost, duration, comfort and environmental impact.
- Apply the most appropriate booking channels according to organisational requirements.
- Promote responsible travel practices among travellers.

**Maintain travel records and support travel monitoring and reporting.**

- Update and maintain travel-related data and records.
- Consolidate information required for travel reporting and monitoring.
- Escalate irregularities or non-compliance with the Travel Policy

**V. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY**

**Autonomy**

Works within established procedures and the Travel Policy, organising travel bookings and managing competing priorities while referring exceptional situations to the Travel Referent

**Complexity**

Operates in an international and multicultural environment, coordinating with multiple stakeholders while balancing operational, administrative, budgetary and data protection requirements.

**VI. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE**

The incumbent is committed to contributing to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse, including those detailed in MSF’s Typologies of Abuse, and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

**VII. REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Secondary education and relevant administrative training or equivalent professional experience.

Asset: Training in travel, tourism, business administration or a related field.

**Experience**

- Minimum 2 years' experience in travel administration, travel coordination, travel agency services or a similar role.
- Experience organising international travel arrangements.
- Experience working with multiple stakeholders and service providers.

Asset: Experience in an international and multicultural environment and/or the humanitarian sector.

**Knowledge**

- Knowledge of travel booking processes and travel administration.
- Understanding of international travel requirements, visas and travel documentation.
- Proficiency in travel booking systems, databases and standard IT applications.
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to prioritise workload and manage multiple requests.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.

**Languages**

- Fluency in English; French is an advantage.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

**We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**

jobs.title: National HLP Legal Associate
jobs.description:
Overview of position

HLP and protection programming to support durable solutions for displacement-affected communities. The programme focuses on strengthening access to Housing, Land and Property rights, improving protection-sensitive case management, and supporting safe, informed, and rights-based pathways for return, relocation, reintegration, and recovery.

HLP and protection concerns remain closely linked in South Sudan. Displaced persons, returnees, and host communities often face land disputes, forced evictions, secondary occupation, lack of documentation, family and community-level disputes, and limited access to safe referral pathways or effective dispute resolution mechanisms.

The Case Management HLP legal Associate will support HLP case management activities by providing legal advice, facilitating access to community-based mediation mechanisms and administrative dispute resolution processes, and assisting vulnerable individuals to access appropriate legal and administrative remedies for Housing, Land and Property-related disputes in a manner that is confidential, inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and aligned with do-no-harm principles.

Under the supervision of the designated supervisor and technical guidance of the HLP/Protection Associate, the incumbent will contribute to case management services by supporting affected individuals through legal information, referrals, dispute resolution, access to administrative remedies, and community-based alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms. To strengthen access to justice and support timely, rights-based resolution of HLP disputes, the programme seeks to recruit a qualified Legal Practitioner based in Juba.

Role objectives

Legal Advice and Assistance

• Conduct legal assessments of HLP cases referred by HLP case workers.

• Provide legal information and advice to clients on applicable South Sudan laws, policies, regulations, and administrative procedures.

• Advise clients on available legal remedies and appropriate dispute resolution options.

• Support the preparation and review of legal and administrative documents required for dispute resolution processes.

Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)

• Facilitate access to mediation and negotiation support and processes between disputing parties.

• Coordinate with community leaders, Sheikhs, traditional authorities, and local administration to promote amicable dispute resolution.

• Promote voluntary, rights-based, impartial, and non-discriminatory approaches to dispute resolution.

• Document mediation processes, agreements, and outcomes in accordance with programme requirements.

Administrative Dispute Resolution

• Liaise with the Ministry of Housing, Land and Public Utilities and other relevant government institutions.

• Support Persons of Concern in navigating administrative procedures related to housing, land, and property matters.

• Facilitate access to administrative settlement of disputes where appropriate.

• Follow up with authorities and stakeholders on pending cases.

Case Management Support

• Participate in case conferences and provide legal input into case action plans.

• Work closely with HLP case workers and case managers to ensure effective progression and resolution of cases.

• support referral of cases requiring formal legal representation or court intervention to appropriate agency or legal aid programs.

• Ensure confidentiality and adherence to protection principles throughout case management processes.

Capacity Building and Community Engagement

• Support community awareness activities on HLP rights and dispute resolution mechanisms.

• Deliver legal briefings and mentorship sessions to HLP staff, community leaders, and relevant stakeholders.

• Contribute to the development of legal awareness and information materials.

• Perform any other related duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Project reporting

To: HLP/Protection Associate

Key competencies

REQUIREMENTS

1\. Education: Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) from a recognized institution (being admitted to legal practice in South Sudan and possessing a valid practicing license is an advantage) with relevant experience in protection, HLP, community engagement, case management, or humanitarian programming.

2\. Experience:

• Minimum three (3) years of legal practice experience in South Sudan, preferably in Juba.

• Demonstrated experience handling civil law and Housing, Land and Property (HLP) matters.

• Proven experience in mediation, negotiation, and alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.

• Experience working with government institutions, traditional authorities, community leaders, and administrative structures.

• Experience supporting humanitarian, development, protection, or rule of law programmes is highly desirable.

• Experience working with displacement-affected communities, returnees, host communities, or individuals affected by HLP disputes, protection risks, land-related conflicts, civil documentation challenges, or other vulnerabilities.

• Experience supporting case management, community outreach, legal information, dispute resolution, referral pathways, or field monitoring is desirable.

• Knowledge of HLP issues, customary and statutory land practices, local governance structures, protection principles, and conflict-sensitive approaches in South Sudan is an advantage.

• Experience preparing field reports, activity summaries, case documentation, meeting notes, or basic data tracking tools is desirable.

3\. Additional Requirements:

• Strong knowledge of South Sudan land, property, inheritance, and civil law frameworks.

• Excellent mediation, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills.

• Strong interpersonal, communication, facilitation, and community engagement skills.

• Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and maintain confidentiality.

• Ability to work respectfully with affected populations, local authorities, community leaders, partners, and colleagues.

• Commitment to accountability, inclusion, gender equality, protection mainstreaming, and do-no-harm principles.

• Good drafting, reporting, coordination, and organizational skills, with the ability to meet deadlines.

Team management

No

Further information

**1. Languages:**

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Arabic or other local languages spoken in South Sudan is an advantage.

jobs.title: ETC Construction Coordinator
jobs.description:
Overview of position

CTG is looking for five (05) ETC Construction Coordinators to assist in a DRC client Ebola response requiring the rapid construction and adaptation of treatment and isolation facilities in remote and operationally challenging locations across Eastern DRC. Works include site preparation, temporary and semi-permanent structures (tents, wood or bricks), tent erection, fencing, drainage, WASH facilities, electrical works, and supporting infrastructure within existing health facilities designated by the country Ministry of Health and WHO.

To support implementation, CTG client deploys rapid intervention teams comprising skilled technicians and casual labour operating under emergency timelines, often in environments characterized by insecurity, limited market capacity, inadequate infrastructure, and challenging logistical access. The ETC Construction Coordinators must be highly agile and capable of deploying across multiple sites as construction activities evolve, transitioning rapidly from one location to the next upon completion of works.

Given the highly dynamic nature of outbreak responses, the incumbents will be expected to maintain a high degree of flexibility and readiness to redeploy at short notice in line with operational priorities. The ETC Construction Coordinators will play a critical roles in translating engineering plans into effective field execution, ensuring that construction activities are delivered safely, efficiently, and in compliance with technical standards, operational requirements, and emergency response timelines..

Role objectives

Role objectives:

Lead day-to-day management of construction sites, supervising teams of carpenters, masons, plumbers, electricians, welders, labourers and local contractors.

Organize and allocate labour, materials, tools and equipment to ensure efficient execution of site activities and achievement of construction targets.

Source construction materials, tools and equipment from local markets whenever feasible.

Coordinate with our client and designated medical partners to ensure the timely mobilization and delivery of required resources to support uninterrupted construction activities.

Identify practical solutions to technical and operational challenges arising in remote and resource-constrained environments while maintaining construction quality and programme objectives.

Support implementation of Ebola Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures on construction sites and ensure compliance with site-specific health and safety requirements.

Liaise with local authorities, facility operators, community representatives and partner organizations to facilitate construction activities and support community acceptance.

Support rapid deployment of intervention teams to new sites and contribute to standardization of construction practices across multiple ETC locations.

Daily supervision of installation teams, labourers and service providers, ensuring adherence to safety standards, quality requirements and agreed timelines.

Construction progress reports, completion notes, snag lists, photos and handover records submitted to the Logistics team for tracking and audit purposes.

Construction teams effectively supervised, coordinated and deployed across assigned worksites to achieve agreed implementation schedules.

Skilled labour and casual workers trained, guided and monitored to ensure compliance with technical specifications, quality standards and safety procedures.

Construction materials, tools and equipment properly managed, accounted for and utilized efficiently to minimize delays and wastage.

Site constraints, technical issues and operational bottlenecks identified early, with practical mitigation measures implemented and communicated to management.

Positive engagement maintained with local communities and facility stakeholders to support smooth site operations and project acceptance.

Ebola IPC measures consistently implemented and monitored throughout all construction activities.

Comprehensive handover to medical partner once a construction / ETC is completed.

Perform any other tasks when required

Project reporting

Provide concise daily progress updates covering completed works, pending activities, constraints, required materials, safety issues and support needed.

Maintain installation records, basic measurement sheets, site photos and handover documentation for each completed structure.

Report regularly on labour utilization, contractor performance, material consumption, equipment status and site productivity.

Escalate technical, operational, security or community-related issues affecting implementation and propose practical corrective actions.

Maintain daily site diaries documenting workforce deployment, completed activities, incidents, weather conditions and key operational decisions.

Key competencies

At least eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in construction supervision, site management, civil works, building construction, humanitarian infrastructure projects, or related activities.

Experience supervising multidisciplinary teams of skilled labour and casual workers is required.

Experience with UN agencies, international NGOs, UN logistics operations, emergency response, humanitarian supply chain, or construction works in remote and high-risk field locations.

Formal academic qualifications are desirable but not mandatory.

Technical training, vocational qualifications, professional certifications, or extensive practical experience in construction, infrastructure delivery, site management, public works, logistics, emergency response, or related fields may be accepted.

Candidates with substantial experience leading field construction or infrastructure projects in humanitarian, development, military, public-sector, or private-sector environments are strongly encouraged to apply.

Demonstrated practical knowledge of field infrastructure construction, site preparation, occupational safety and supervision of construction or installation teams.

Training in occupational health and safety, working at height, safe lifting, first aid, infection prevention and control, or UN/UN agencies security procedures, SSAFE or similar security awareness trainings.

Previous experience working in DRC or comparable emergency, hardships or insecure field environments.

Experience in eastern DRC, including Bunia, Beni or other forward hubs, or prior deployment in Ebola or public health emergency response operations.

Working knowledge of English is desirable. Knowledge of Swahili or another local language used in eastern DRC is an asset.

Key competencies

Proven experience supervising multidisciplinary construction teams comprising carpenters, masons, plumbers, electricians, skilled technicians and large numbers of casual labour in remote or emergency environments.

Strong practical construction background with demonstrated ability to organize works, manage labour forces and deliver infrastructure projects under difficult field conditions.

Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to develop practical solutions using limited local resources and constrained supply chains.

Previous involvement in Ebola response operations, Ebola Treatment Centres (ETCs) construction, isolation facilities, outbreak-response infrastructure, or infection prevention and control environments is a strong asset.

Knowledge of our client operational procedures, humanitarian field operations and UN security operating environments is a strong advantage.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively in insecure locations, under pressure, and with minimal supervision.

N/A

jobs.title: FIELD COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Blue Economy Investment Specialist, IPSA11, Fiji - Suva (UNCDF)- [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, UNOs, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

- SME Finance

- Sub-National Finance

- Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

UNCDF is seeking a Blue Economy Investment Specialist to lead the origination, structuring, and deployment of ocean-positive and nature-based blended finance investments in the Pacific. The position will focus on mobilizing concessional and catalytic capital toward enterprises and financial intermediaries that generate sustainable livelihoods while protecting and restoring coastal and marine ecosystems, with a particular emphasis on reef-positive, fisheries, aquaculture, coastal tourism, waste management, and ocean-climate resilience solutions.

Among other tasks, the incumbent is expected to manage the blue economy portfolio in the Pacific, in particular the EU-funded Sustainable Pacific Blue Circle Fund (SPBCF) project, an impact investment vehicle that provides investment capital backed by venture-building support (technical assistance, grants, loans, guarantees) to businesses that have the potential to generate revenue and create a positive development impact ongoing till 2028. The incumbent is also expected to oversee other blue economy focused and reef-positive interventions that are implemented in the Pacific region.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Regional Investment Specialists for the Pacific and in close collaboration with other colleagues in IID and IFOD, the Blue Economy Investment Specialist will lead and support the development, structuring and execution of blue‑economy or other relevant sectoral investment initiatives. The Specialist will work closely with IID and IFOD colleagues, as well as other UNCDF counterparts, country focal points, government partners, private sector actors and development partners.

1) Project Management of Blue‑Economy Investment Initiatives

- Manage all aspects of the blue economy initiatives implemented in the Pacific.

- Lead the preparation and implementation of Annual Work Plans (AWPs), budgets and activity schedules for Pacific blue‑economy investment programmes.

- Manage day‑to‑day implementation of activities, including stakeholder engagement, technical assistance delivery, pipeline development and progress monitoring.

- Manage project documentation, track financial delivery, oversee audits when required, and support organization of steering committee meetings.

- Ensure effective coordination between countries, regional teams, and corporate oversight units to deliver a complex multi-country programme.

- Apply UNCDF Social and Environmental Standards (SES), including safeguards related to human rights, gender equality, SEA/SH prevention, and grievance mechanisms.

- Maintain and update project risk registers, escalate high-risk issues, and contribute to assurance activities, audits, and evaluations.

- Apply adaptive management approaches, identifying implementation risks and bottlenecks and proposing timely corrective actions.

- Ensure efficient use of project resources, value for money, and adherence to approved budgets.

2) Investment Pipeline Development and Blended Finance Execution

- Lead the sourcing, screening, and development of a diversified pipeline of blue and green economy MSMEs

- Oversee incubation and acceleration pathways, ensuring MSMEs receive tailored technical assistance and progress toward investment readiness.

- Guide and quality-assure financial, technical, environmental and social (ESG), and gender-lens due diligence processes for MSMEs and financial-sector partners.

- Coordinate the structuring and deployment of investment grants, concessional loans, and credit guarantees benefiting the blue economy in line with UNCDF investment policies and approval committees.

- Support engagement with local financial institutions, development banks, and impact investors to crowd in private capital in support of the blue economy.

- Ensure supported enterprises are prepared for graduation to concessional or commercial finance.

- Contribute to the design, feasibility assessment, and investor engagement for the expansion of blended finance in the blue economy, ensuring alignment with UNCDF’s catalytic mandate.

3) Partnership Development, Stakeholder Engagement, and Policy Dialogue

- Serve as UNCDF’s primary focal point for blue economy related engagement with governments, central banks, regulators, donors, financial institutions, NGOs, business development service providers, and private investors.

- Build and sustain strategic partnerships that enhance MSME incubation, financial sector capacity, and capital mobilization for blue and green economy investments.

- Support structured dialogue with policymakers and regulators to strengthen enabling environments for sustainable finance and MSME access to capital.

- Coordinate engagement with regional and international partners working in the blue economy to leverage synergies and avoid duplication.

- Represent UNCDF in national, regional, and international forums related to blended finance, blue economy, and climate finance.

- Promote South–South and Triangular Cooperation initiatives and knowledge exchange around blue economy matters.

4) Monitoring, Reporting, Knowledge Management, and Learning

- Oversee and maintain robust M&E systems capturing both programme and investment‑level results, including blue‑economy‑specific indicators (e.g., sustainable fisheries outcomes, marine ecosystem co‑benefits, climate resilience).

- Ensure high-quality data collection, analysis, and reporting, including disaggregation by sex, youth, sector, and country.

- Contribute to timely and accurate donor reports, annual progress reviews, and mid-term and final evaluations.

- Lead knowledge capture and dissemination, including case studies, lessons learned, and good practices for blue and green economy finance.

- Support learning and replication by sharing evidence and insights within UNCDF and with regional and global partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022 - 2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, UNOs, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

- SME Finance

- Sub-National Finance

- Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

Within UNCDF’s thematic area of peace and resilience financing, the Pro-Congo project, a joint initiative by UNEP and UNCDF under the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI) Private Sector Window, aims to support entrepreneurs and Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Congo Basin countries by providing technical assistance and access to financial instruments including grants and loans, to promote tropical forest conservation, emission reductions, job creation, and biodiversity protection. Targeting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Republic of Congo (RoC), Cameroon and Gabon, the project seeks to drive sustainable economic growth by facilitating access to capacity building, finance and market access for both mature and early-stage businesses.

To facilitate the achievement of these objectives, UNCDF seeks to hire a Project Manager to lead project implementation, coordinate the project team, and ensure successful achievement of project objectives

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager will report to UNCDF’s Senior Portfolio Manager and will maintain a close collaboration with the Resident Coordinator’s Office in the countries of implementation through the UNCDF Regional Lead for West and Central Africa and the Caribbean.

Under the guidance of UNCDF’s Senior Portfolio Manager, the overall responsibility of the Project Manager will be to act as liaison for all project stakeholders, providing technical assistance and ensuring proper implementation of the Pro-Congo project. He/She will conduct the following tasks:

a) Ensure the implementation of all project activities and achievement of deliverables:

• Develop detailed annual workplans and timelines for all project activities, ensuring alignment with the overall project objectives and oversee effective execution.

• Lead the overall management and timely implementation of the project outputs and activities.

• Provide strategic guidance and management oversight to ensure project implementation is on track to ensure achievement of the planned results.

• Lead and coordinate high-level task forces and steering committees related to the implementation of the project, including ensuring regular communication and collaboration with CAFI and UNEP for successful programme implementation.

• Facilitate and support the work of the programme’s implementing partners and deliver specialized technical assistance for effective program implementation.

• Ensure implementation of gender mainstreaming in line with UNDP and UNCDF guidelines and global standards.

b) Ensure proper monitoring and reporting of the programme:

• Organize regular coordination meetings and draft regular progress reports as agreed in the project document, including regular briefing to donors and other relevant partners.

• Ensure the guidelines, frameworks and requirements of CAFI are followed throughout project implementation.

• Update the Quantum and Quantum+ Project Management tools as required and monitor changes in the external environment and promptly propose to the UNCDF management of necessary solutions/actions.

• Monitor project progress, Environmental & Social Safeguards, and risks, ensuring that changes are controlled and problems addressed.

• Monitor the utilization of programme resources and budget to ensure cost-effectiveness and efficiency.

• Take lead on the preparation of reviews and evaluations as defined in the project document.

• Participate in the mobilization of additional resources including from CAFI.

• Travel to the project's target countries as needed for stakeholder engagement and on-site verification of results.

c) Build partnerships with relevant stakeholders and undertake advocacy activities:

• Coordinate dialogue, engagement and partnerships with the respective Government authorities and lead advocacy activities with other relevant stakeholders at both project and country level, including with bilateral, multilateral and private sector actors.

• Ensure alignment of the project with relevant UN initiatives in the countries/region.

• Advise on the contribution of the project to the countries national priorities, progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and UNCDF’s Strategic Framework.

d) Implement knowledge management activities:

• Ensure implementation of knowledge management activities.

• Participate in training events, communities of practice, codifying and sharing knowledge on sustainable practices.

• Facilitate development of success stories and other communication materials.

e) Support broader UNCDF operations:

• Contribute to knowledge-sharing initiatives and best practices in peace and resilience finance.

• Share knowledge and lessons learned from private sector operations and best practices in relevant fields.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management:

LEVEL 3: Appropriately involves team in different stages of work and decision-making

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area Name Definition

Partnership management

Relationship management

Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Partnership management

CSO engagement

Knowledge and understanding of CSOs and the ability to engage with CSOs

Partnership management

Strategic engagement

Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives

Business Direction & Strategy

Strategic Thinking

Ability to develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNCDF’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks and opportunities; linking the vision to reality on the ground, and creating tangible solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight

Business Direction & Strategy

Entrepreneurial Thinking

Identify and seize opportunities to service and add value to clients, create clarity around UNCDF value proposition to beneficiaries and partners, develop clear service offers responding to client needs in line with UNCDF’s organizational priorities and mandate.

Business Direction & Strategy

System Thinking

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management

Portfolio Management

Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimising return on investment. . Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Environmental Sciences, Development Studies, International Relations, Programme or Project Management, Economics, or related fields is required, or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in above or related fields in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of master´s degree.

Experience:

Minimum 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant work experience in managing complex, multi-country projects or programmes in climate, environment, sustainable finance or international development, including work planning, resource and budget monitoring, results-based management and risk management.

Required Skills:

International experience working in developing countries in Africa.

Track record of experience managing donor-funded projects (CAFI, UNCDF, UN agencies, or similar).

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

Experience with reporting to and managing donor and partner relationships including grants and reporting mechanisms.

Experience applying UNDP and UNCDF rules, procedures, and corporate project-management tools

Experience leading a multidisciplinary project or programme team, including non-staff personnel, consultants or implementing partners.

Experience working with the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI), Global Funds, IFIs, UNCDF and/or another UN entity.

Experience of engaging with private sector, development partners and government stakeholders in Central Africa.

Experience managing or overseeing private-sector investment programmes and/or transactions, including investment due diligence, transaction structuring and/or monitoring of financing instruments for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).

Required Languages:

Fluency in French and English, is required.

Working knowledge of another United Nations official language is an asset.

Travel and Reimbursement:

The Project Manager is expected to render services from the UNCDF regional office in Dakar, Senegal. UNCDF will cover the cost of travel of the individual to the duty station, as well as their return to their home upon completion of their services. Frequent travel within Central Africa (DRC, RoC, Gabon and Cameroon) for stakeholder engagement and on-site verification of project activities will be required and will be paid for by UNCDF, in accordance with UNCDF travel policies. A separate TOR with clear deliverables, budget and timelines will be prepared and agreed prior to each field mission.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Org. Setting and Reporting

The Department of Operational Support (DOS) was established to provide end-to-end operational support, advisory services and other solutions to operating entities across the Secretariat, including departments, offices away from headquarters, peace operations, and regional commissions. The Division of Administration (DOA) in New York provides administrative support functions (human resources, budget, finance and general administration) and facility management and commercial services to entities at United Nations Headquarters. It also provides financial operational services to entities across the globe. As Common Administrative Platform, the Division comprises the OneEO, the Financial Operations Service (including OnePayroll), and the Facilities and Commercial Activities Service. This position is located within the Common Administrative Platform at United Nations Headquarters, referred to as the One Executive Office ("One EO"), under the Division of Administration in the Department of Operational Support (DOS). One EO started its transition phase on 1 January 2026 as part of the UN80 reform initiative, which aims to consolidate common administrative functions across Secretariat entities into unified service platforms. One EO provides the full range of administrative and operational services required by New York–based Secretariat client entities to fulfil their mandates, including human resources management, financial administration, travel, and general administrative support. The Associate Human Resources Officer will report directly to the Chief of Unit/desk.

Responsibilities

General:

- Provides advice and support to managers and staff on human resources related matters.- Keeps abreast of developments in various areas of human resources. Recruitment and placement:- Reviews requests, signs job offers and coordinates onboarding of new staff.- Prepares and presents cases to appointment and promotion bodies.- Serves as ex-officio in examinations boards.- Monitors the work of the Human Resources Assistants in carrying out all human resources administrative transactions including preparation of personnel actions, transactions related to onboarding and separations, processing of contracts, and others.- Supervises and monitors the work of the human resources assistants in carrying out all human resources transactions related to onboarding, including preparation of personnel actions, onboarding clearances and other. Administration of entitlements:- Administers and provides advice on salary and related benefits, travel and entitlements.- Provides advice on interpretation and application of policies, regulations and rules. Staff development and career support training:- Designs plans and conducts period entitlements monitoring exercises and provides reports on the findings and recommendations to other stakeholders.- Provides induction orientation and briefing to new staff members. Other duties:- Contributes to the collection and analysis of data as well as identification of trends or patterns and provides draft insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods for data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting.- Performs other duties as required.

PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of main principles and building blocks of human resources management in general, and, in particular, knowledge of UN Staff Regulations and Rules and their application in the organizational settings covering recruitment, onboarding, contract management and administration of entitlements and benefits; Demonstrated technical knowledge on the development of e-staffing guidance materials; knowledge of the United Nations staff rules and regulations, human resources policies, procedures and practices. Able to perform analysis, modeling, and interpretation of HR data in support of decision-making. PLANNING & ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies. Identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required. Allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work. Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning. Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary. Uses time efficiently. CLIENT ORIENTATION: Ability to identify clients' needs and propose appropriate solutions; ability to establish and maintain productive partnerships with clients; Considers all those to whom services are provided to be "clients" and seeks to see things from clients' point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients' needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients' environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.

A first level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of an advanced degree. A first-level university degree and no experience will be accepted for candidates who have passed the Young Professionals Programme Examination (YPP), the United Nations National Competitive Recruitment Examination (NCRE) or the General Service to Professional Examination (G to P).

No experience is required for candidates who have passed the United Nations Young Professional Programme Examination (YPP), the United Nations National Competitive Recruitment Examination (NCRE) or the General Service to Professional Examination (G to P). Org. Setting and Reporting

This position is located in the Business Relationship Management (BRM) within the Enterprise Programme Management Section, Office of Information and Communications Technology. The Programme Assistant reports to the P4 Information Systems Officer. The Business Relationship Management (BRM) team serves as the strategic link between OICT and UN Secretariat entities, providing a single point of contact to align ICT solutions and digital transformation initiatives with business needs and priorities. The Office of Information and Communications Technology (OICT) is leading the digital transformation of the Organization to enable a better, safer, more sustainable future through secure, reliable, and innovative technology solutions. OICT is committed to achieving 50/50 gender balance and geographical diversity in its staff, and female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position. OICT supports the principles of work-life balance and flexible work arrangements.

Responsibilities

Within limits of delegated authority, the Programme Assistant is responsible for the following duties:

Official notice

Org. Setting and Reporting

The United Nations Secretary-General is responsible for the investment of the assets of the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF). The Secretary-General has delegated this responsibility to the Representative of the Secretary-General for the investment of the assets of the UNJSPF (RSG). The RSG heads the Office of Investment Management (OIM), which manages a $100+ billion multi-asset class, global investment portfolio, about 85% of which is actively managed in-house. Asset classes under management comprise global equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, private equity, real estate, infrastructure, timber and commodities. OIM’s staff are all based in New York but come from over 40 countries. For more information, please visit OIM's website at https://oim.unjspf.org/. This position is located in the Office of Investment Management (OIM) of the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF). OIM is responsible for the investment of the assets of the Fund. The temporary position supports organizational development at OIM to facilitate the implementation of Total Portfolio Approach (TPA) best practices at the Fund. Following the TPA Feasibility Study, OIM identified a sequenced programme to move the Fund towards a best-practice total portfolio model under Project Blue Print 2030. The One-Organization Enablement workstream seeks to strengthen enterprise-wide decision-making by improving coordination across investment teams, operations and governance functions; creating common investment language and aligned performance objectives; and establishing integrated governance, reporting and delegated-authority arrangements. The Programme Management Officer reports to the Representative of the Secretary-General for the investment of the assets of UNJSPF (RSG).

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the Programme Management Officer will be responsible for the following duties:

- Plan and coordinate the delivery of the One-Organisation Enablement project, including workplans, milestones, deliverables, risks, resources and consultant budgets.- Support governance, engagement and decision-making frameworks across investment, operations and governance functions, including delegated-authority structures and accountability mechanisms, to support total-fund outcomes.- Analyze the application of total portfolio principles within the Fund's governance, regulatory and operating environment and recommend practical solutions.- Coordinate development of the TPA Mindset framework, change-management materials, KPI/KRI structures and related documentation.- Support the review and standardization of performance measurement practices, including team and individual KPIs and peer benchmarking.- Monitor project delivery and change effectiveness, conduct governance and quarterly review processes, capture lessons learned and implement corrective actions.- Coordinate training and coaching for OIM leadership and teams on the TPA mindset and governance processes.- Develop system maps of key stakeholders, decision forums and information flows across asset-liability management, the reference portfolio and implementation functions.- Prepare presentations, briefings and reporting materials for governance bodies, including the Investments Committee and Pension Board.- Maintain governance records, audit-ready documentation and decision trails for project deliverables.- Provide strategic analysis and executive reporting on organizational readiness, accountability, delegated authorities and change management.- Performs other related duties as required.

Competencies

Professionalism: Knowledge of project and programme management, organizational change, governance design and performance measurement in complex institutional environments. Ability to analyze complex issues, identify practical solutions and produce clear, audit-ready documentation. Understanding of institutional investment governance and total portfolio concepts is desirable. Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems and remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work.

Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; values others' ideas and expertise; supports and acts in accordance with final group decisions; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for shortcomings.

Planning and Organizing: Develops clear goals consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate time and resources; foresees risks and allows for contingencies; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently.

Education

An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in business administration, finance, investment management, organizational management or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Job - Specific Qualification

Not available.

Work Experience

A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in project or programme management, investment, organizational change, governance or a related area is required. Experience managing business-driven programmes in the financial services, preferably at an asset owner with similar profile as UNJSPF), is required. Experience delivering organizational or governance transformation in institutional or client engagements is required. Experience with stakeholder engagement, organizational culture change and the design of key performance and key risk indicators in complex, multi-stakeholder institutional environments is desirable. Experience developing or overseeing governance frameworks, RACI matrices and delegated-authority arrangements is desirable.

Languages

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. Amman serves as a major operational base for humanitarian and development agencies responding to crises in the Middle East. UNHCR, UNICEF, WFP, UNDP, and UNRWA maintain significant offices here, with roles in refugee protection, programme delivery, and regional coordination.

More on this market+Amman functions as the primary coordination hub for the Syria crisis response and broader Middle East humanitarian operations. About Food and Agriculture Organization

FAO leads international efforts to defeat hunger. It helps countries modernize agriculture, improve food systems, and manage natural resources sustainably. FAO acts as a neutral forum and a source of technical expertise on food and agriculture for 195 member nations.

More about FAO+FAO recruits through its own portal (fao.org/employment) for professional, general service, consultant, and national project positions. Technical expertise in agriculture, food systems, or natural resource management is a common requirement. English and French are the most-needed languages.

The Food and Agriculture Organization is headquartered in Rome and employs approximately 3,200 staff. FAO uses its own recruitment portal and career framework (separate from the UN Secretariat's Inspira). Technical specialists in agriculture, fisheries, forestry, animal health, food safety, and natural resource management are in consistent demand. FAO also hires extensively for data and statistics roles, particularly related to food security monitoring (IPC, FAOSTAT). Field offices operate in over 130 countries.
